target.title: refactor: consolidate duplicate helper exports
target.body:
Closes #105996

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a maintenance problem where identical helper names in core and workspace packages hid copied or incompatible implementations. The copies could drift while callers had no signal that, for example, one duration parser throws and accepts composites while the cron parser returns `null`, requires a unit, floors values, and rejects non-positive results.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Moves shared string coercion, duration parsing, and agent-id normalization into `@openclaw/normalization-core`.
- Derives normalization-core source/native aliases from its package exports, retaining packaged-dist fallback instead of another copied subpath inventory.
- Deletes memory-host-sdk's copied string helper module and adds the already-valid package dependency to media-generation-core.
- Keeps Gateway transcript whitespace preservation under the explicit `readNonBlankStringPreservingWhitespace` contract.
- Renames the cron parser to `parsePositiveCronDurationMs` and the standalone memory path helper to `resolveMemoryHostUserPath`.
- Consolidates core's two `resolveUserPath` definitions in `src/infra/home-dir.ts`; `src/utils.ts` remains a compatibility re-export.

The memory-host package can depend on normalization-core, so coercion primitives now import it directly. It cannot import core `src/**` without reversing the package boundary; standalone home/config/SQLite/secret helpers therefore remain package-owned where they have narrower contracts. Existing plugin/runtime facades and public compatibility exports were not renamed opportunistically. Sibling-owned `retryAsync` and `formatErrorMessage` work was intentionally untouched.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible behavior change. Maintainers get one implementation for compatible helpers, explicit names for incompatible contracts, and 166 fewer non-test lines (`+228/-394`).

## Evidence

- Exact-head Blacksmith Testbox-through-Crabbox `tbx_01kxcy8tnkmp19kvj2et35xfw6`: full `pnpm build`, formatting and LOC-ratchet proof, and 1,118 focused normalization, memory-host, Gateway, CLI, routing, path, plugin-resolver, and packaged-alias tests; green after rebasing onto current main.
- Initial hosted CI feedback was fixed before landing: formatting, the tsdown LOC ratchet, and native/package alias coverage. `tsdown.config.ts` is now five lines smaller than the PR base.
- Per-cluster Codex autoreview runs: clean after accepted whitespace-preservation fix; final branch review recorded separately in the landing proof.
- `git diff --check`: clean.

## Actionable duplicate clusters

| Cluster | Baseline definitions | Resolution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| string coercion | `normalizeOptionalString`, lowercasing/list/unique variants across normalization-core, memory-host-sdk, media-generation-core, Gateway | normalization-core canonical; Gateway's distinct preserve-whitespace behavior renamed |
| duration parsing | CLI throwing/options parser, memory-host copy, cron positive/null parser | normalization-core canonical; cron contract renamed |
| agent id | routing and memory-host copies | normalization-core canonical and re-exported |
| user path | two core definitions plus memory-host standalone copy | `home-dir.ts` canonical; core re-export; package-only contract renamed |

## Full baseline enumeration table

Generated at `2ecd485cd5f41f8884117eac91e9c57fbe7c4c98` with exported `function`/`const` definitions under `src/` and `packages/`, grouped by name and deduplicated by module. Re-exports do not match the defining-expression scan; `*.runtime.ts(x)` facades are excluded as requested. The full 417-cluster table is below, including deliberately unrelated domain-local names and test helpers left unchanged.

target.title: fix(googlechat): keep accounts.default streaming when doctor migrates named accounts
target.body:
Closes #105940

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw doctor --fix` could drop an inherited Google Chat `accounts.default.blockStreaming` setting when migrating a named account that only had a flat streaming key such as `chunkMode`. Runtime then treated the named account's partial `streaming` object as a wholesale replacement, so block streaming silently turned off for that account.

## Why This Change Was Made

Google Chat named-account resolution layers `accounts.default` before the named account and replaces `streaming` wholesale (same inheritance shape as WhatsApp). The generic root-only seeding path (`accountStreamingReplacesRoot`) only copied channel-root streaming into newly materialized account objects and never consulted `accounts.default`.

This mirrors the WhatsApp plugin-local `seedMigratedAccountStreaming` repair from #105709: migrate flat aliases, then deep-fill missing fields from `accounts.default` (falling back to root) for accounts that did not already have a nested `streaming` object.

## User Impact

Multi-account Google Chat configs that shared block-streaming (or other delivery settings) via `accounts.default` keep those settings after `openclaw doctor --fix`, instead of losing them when a named account also had a flat streaming key to migrate.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test extensions/googlechat/src/doctor-contract.test.ts` → 6 passed
  - includes regression: `accounts.default.blockStreaming` + named `chunkMode` retains both after migration
  - includes case-insensitive `accounts.Default` seeding
  - existing root-seeding and legacy streamMode/group allow cases still pass
- No competing open PRs for #105940 at open time

target.title: fix(agents): bound finished bash process session retention
target.body:
Closes #105625

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where long-running Gateways retaining many completed background bash/exec sessions would keep an unbounded finished-session map until TTL expiry, and session reset/delete would leave matching finished process records pollable until that TTL. That multiplies retained aggregate output and can grow gateway heap under bursty shell workloads.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep completed `process poll` / `process log` aggregates (ClawSweeper rejected tail-only retention), but enforce deterministic finished-session count and total-aggregate-byte caps, and purge finished records whose `scopeKey` matches gateway session lifecycle cleanup keys. Shared scopes (for example chat bash) are not purged when an unrelated agent session resets.

## User Impact

Operators get bounded finished-process memory growth under heavy background exec traffic. Resetting or deleting a gateway session no longer leaves that session’s finished process records pollable until job TTL. Completed process log/poll behavior for still-retained sessions is unchanged.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS Darwin arm64 (live runtime harness on PR head + focused unit tests)

Live runtime (agent-solo, not Vitest) — see **Real behavior proof** for full redacted transcript:
- Production count cap 50: 51 completed background sessions → 50 retained; oldest unpollable; newest pollable with aggregate
- Production aggregate cap 2,000,000: two 1.2M sessions → only newest retained (1.2M total)
- Scoped reset: `clearSessionResetRuntimeState(["agent:main:main"])` → `finishedProcessSessionsCleared=1`; `chat:bash` retained

Focused tests (pass, supplemental):
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bash-process-registry.test.ts` — 18 passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/session-reset-cleanup.test.ts` — 7 passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bash-tools.process.poll-timeout.test.ts` — 8 passed

Static:
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` on touched files — pass
- `git diff --check` — pass

Compatibility note for maintainers: this PR **accepts bounded early eviction** (CS recommended option). Completed process poll/log may disappear before TTL when budgets are exceeded; refine thresholds only if a longer delayed-poll contract is required.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: Finished bash process sessions are hard-capped (50 sessions / 2,000,000 aggregate characters) so completed `process poll`/`process log` retention cannot grow unbounded until TTL; session reset/delete purges finished records only for matching lifecycle `scopeKey` values (shared scopes such as `chat:bash` stay).
- Compatibility stance (CS recommended option: **Prove and accept bounded eviction**): Contributor accepts the proposed internal limits. Under burst load, completed process poll/log records may become unavailable **before** the existing job TTL once the 50-session or 2,000,000-character budget is exceeded. Thresholds are intentionally product-owned if maintainers later want a longer delayed-poll window.
- Environment: local macOS Darwin arm64, Node v24.17.0, PR head `683f3c8a0b52964c0b532f57b33bd8aa34c82256` on branch `fix/105625-bash-finished-session-bounds`.
- Current-main contrast: On main, `pruneFinishedSessions` only deletes by TTL; `finishedSessions` has no count/byte cap; `clearSessionResetRuntimeState` does not touch finished process records, so scoped finished sessions remain pollable until TTL.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch (live runtime harness, **not** Vitest):
  1. Load production owner modules from this checkout: `src/agents/bash-process-registry.ts` and `src/auto-reply/reply/session-reset-cleanup.ts` via `tsx`.

target.title: fix(agents): follow through on promised asynchronous work
target.body:
Related: #58450

AI-assisted: yes (Codex)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an agent could promise to continue background or delegated work, end the turn without establishing a completion path, and leave the requester to ask again for the result.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds one shared prompt policy for the canonical full/minimal agent prompts and the standalone agent-bundle prompt. A promised follow-up now carries explicit ownership: arrange a push/watch completion path, keep the originating request open, proactively return with a result/link/proof or concrete blocker, and do not treat progress such as `running` as completion.

This is intentionally a prompt-policy fix, not a natural-language reply rewriter or runtime delivery gate. The broader runtime enforcement proposed in #58450 remains a separate product decision.

## User Impact

Agents using the default full, minimal, subagent, or agent-bundle prompts are explicitly instructed to close promised asynchronous work loops without waiting for another user nudge. Raw/custom replacement prompts retain their existing ownership semantics.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: promised background, continued, or delegated work must retain ownership through a result, link, proof, or concrete blocker.
- Real environment tested: Actions-hydrated AWS Crabbox Linux lease (`c7a.8xlarge`) plus source-blind prompt-contract validation.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: `corepack pnpm test src/agents/system-prompt.test.ts src/agents/sessions/system-prompt.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/system-prompt.test.ts`

target.title: fix(slack): suppress progress chrome sends
target.body:
## Summary
- detect progress-only Slack tool chrome payloads with leading tool emoji plus command/status body
- convert thread-scoped chrome to reactions instead of `chat.postMessage`
- fail closed by suppressing chrome without a reaction target while preserving semantic replies
- type automatic tool-progress payloads at the producer boundary with a closed generic plugin-SDK progress intent so Slack does not infer from arbitrary text

## What Problem This Solves
Progress-only operational chrome like `:hammer_and_wrench: \`pnpm test\`` or `:writing_hand: Write: MEMORY.md` can leak into Slack as user-visible messages when a tool/status payload accidentally reaches the Slack send path. This creates noise in working channels and violates the progress-chrome pre-send gate. The Slack extension now classifies only narrow progress-only payloads and prevents them from becoming chat posts.

## Evidence
Current head: `1e3f34f78d97ec5790a39b722f55b53e640488c5`.

- `pnpm --config.verify-deps-before-run=false vitest run --project extension-codex extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts` passed (149 tests)

## Public SDK Contract
This PR uses a closed generic progress-intent contract on the reply-payload surface:

- shared field: `channelData.openclawProgressKind`

target.title: fix(media): bound hung remote downloads in media store
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users and gateway paths that persist remote media through `saveMediaSource()` would hang indefinitely when a media URL accepted the TCP connection but never sent response headers, or sent a partial body and then stalled. Only a max-bytes cap existed; there was no header or idle-read timeout, so requests, temp files, and caller chains could stay pinned forever.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add 30s response-header and idle-body timeouts to `downloadToFile()` in the media store path, matching the hang-bounding intent already used by `src/media/fetch.ts` / web-media reads. On failure, abort the request/response/write stream, await pipeline shutdown, then remove the temp file before rejecting—so platforms that reject unlinking an open file cannot retain partial media.

This path stays local to `saveMediaSource()` because that caller streams into a sibling temp file while sniffing MIME; `saveRemoteMedia()` / fetch.ts does not own that contract. Shared outcome is the same hang bound, not a duplicated fetch stack.

Timeouts are overridable in tests via `setMediaStoreNetworkDepsForTest`. MIME sniffing, redirect header stripping, and the 5MB size cap stay unchanged.

## User Impact

**Before:** A hung or adversarial media URL could block `saveMediaSource()` (including gateway managed-image ingestion) with no recovery besides process restart, and failure cleanup could race stream close.

**After:** Stalled header waits and idle body reads fail within 30s; streams close before temp removal; callers get a clear timeout/stall error with no leftover media files.

## Evidence

- Changed: `src/media/store.ts` (`downloadToFile`)
- Caller under test: production `saveMediaSource(httpUrl)` against a real local `node:http` server
- Regression: `src/media/store.download-timeout.test.ts`
- Sibling redirect suite still green: `src/media/store.redirect.test.ts`

### Unit regression

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/media/store.download-timeout.test.ts src/media/store.redirect.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

```text
 ✓ |media| src/media/store.download-timeout.test.ts > media store download timeouts > times out when the server accepts a connection but never sends headers 52ms
 ✓ |media| src/media/store.download-timeout.test.ts > media store download timeouts > times out when the response body stalls after partial data 45ms
 ✓ |media| src/media/store.download-timeout.test.ts > media store download timeouts > still saves when the remote body completes before idle timeout 12ms
 ✓ |media| src/media/store.redirect.test.ts > media store redirects > follows redirects and keeps detected mime/extension 31ms
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 3.98s
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** `saveMediaSource()` remote downloads no longer hang forever on servers that accept connections without sending headers, or that stall after partial body data; temp files are cleaned up only after stream teardown.
- **Canonical reachability path:** gateway/managed-image and other callers → `saveMediaSource(url)` → `downloadToFile()` → header timer / idle body timer → abort streams → await pipeline → temp cleanup → reject.

target.title: fix(ai): serialize ChatGPT websocket message decode order

Closes #105435

## What Problem This Solves
`parseWebSocket` started an independent async decode task per `message` event. Blob-like frames await `arrayBuffer()` while strings decode immediately, so later frames could enter the parser queue first and reorder Responses stream events.

Serialize decode-and-parse on a per-socket promise chain so arrival order is preserved without dropping the accepted binary/Blob path. Codex sibling `responses_websocket.rs` already consumes one WebSocket message at a time before reading the next; OpenClaw now matches that ordering invariant while keeping Blob compatibility.

ChatGPT Responses websocket streams no longer reorder events when a delayed Blob decode races a later text frame. Normal string-only traffic behavior is unchanged aside from the ordered chain.

Closes #105434

## What Problem This Solves
Releasing a reused ChatGPT Responses WebSocket deleted `websocketSessionCache` by session id without checking whether a newer same-session connection already owned that slot. A stale release could close/evict a valid replacement connection.

The new-connection release path already guarded deletion with an identity check (`cache.get(sessionId) === entry`). Cached WebSocket sessions are less likely to drop a healthy replacement connection when an older reused lease later releases or expires. No config or API changes.

target.title: improve(gateway): reduce startup work before readiness
target.body:
Closes #105912

AI-assisted: Codex implementation and review.

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway startup performed restart-scoped managed-plugin cleanup and loaded the full worker-environment runtime before the server was ready, including on the common path with no configured or durable workers. This added avoidable cold-start module initialization, filesystem work, and duplicate durable-record scans before the first interactive turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retained managed-plugin cleanup now runs as a cancellable post-ready idle task. It resolves the current installed-plugin index at execution time, preserving plugins installed or reloaded during the delay. The Gateway carries the initial worker record snapshot forward, loads the worker service/runtime bundle only when configured or durable records require it, and imports the protocol schema only when preparing an installation.

Worker-provider lookup and reload planning retain their live lifecycle semantics: provider resolution reads the current plugin registry, and reloads recompute durable providers from the current worker store. The startup benchmark also excludes counters and memory fields from its duration ranking.

Final exact-head CI also exposed dead-export drift in newer `main` merge state. The stack keeps the new SMS reset as an intentional test seam, makes an internal transcript target type file-local, and removes a stale baseline entry; runtime behavior is unchanged.

## User Impact

Gateway restarts perform less work before readiness, with the largest benefit on cold starts and installations carrying managed plugin history. Dormant worker-environment support no longer imposes its full module-loading cost on every boot. No configuration, protocol, data, or plugin SDK contract changes.

## Evidence

- Linux AWS Crabbox focused proof:
  - `run_3e07b71057d3`: 324 tests plus `tsgo:prod` passed after the live-registry fix.
  - `run_717dd41f456d`: 354 behavior tests passed; the only failures were two copies of an obsolete source assertion, updated to require current install-index resolution.

- Exact runtime build: Node 24 `cliStartup` production profile passed in 4.80 s. The full AWS build lane was blocked by a temporary `main` lockfile defect and missing hydrated build-only assets; the later `main` ratchet repair is included in the final rebase, and [hosted exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29225663179) passed at `147ba8f2e847`.
- Final five-run startup benchmark after one warmup:
  - default `/readyz` p50 4761 ms
  - skip-channels `/readyz` p50 4641 ms

- Same-box cold one-shot from the causal cleanup loop: 9756 ms before, 8721 ms after deferring retained-install cleanup (10.6% faster).
- Live OpenAI-on-Crabbox proof, `run_65f7344f794b`, model `openai/gpt-5.6`:

The final remaining suggestion referenced fields absent from the worker record contract and was rejected against current `main`, whose canonical implementation uses the same `listForReconcile().map(providerId)` rule.

target.title: fix(doctor): SQLite migration recovery report corrupts emoji when truncating
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running `openclaw doctor --session-sqlite recover` after a failed migration would get a prefilled GitHub recovery report whose body contained malformed characters when a migration failure message included an emoji or other astral-plane character.

## Why This Change Was Made

The doctor SQLite migration recovery report builder truncated the rendered report body at three length boundaries (20 000 chars for the local body, 6 000 chars for the GitHub new-issue URL body, and 500 chars per sanitized issue field) using raw `.slice(0, N)`. When the cut point landed inside a UTF-16 surrogate pair (e.g. an emoji in a runtime error message), the result was a lone surrogate half — a malformed string that produces replacement characters or garbled text in the GitHub issue body and URL.

The repo already ships a canonical surrogate-safe helper, `truncateUtf16Safe` (`@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`), adopted across 200+ files for exactly this invariant. This module was a missed adoption site. This PR swaps the three raw `.slice(0, N)` calls for `truncateUtf16Safe`, leaving the length limits, inputs, outputs, and call signatures unchanged.

## User Impact

A user who runs `openclaw doctor --session-sqlite recover` and whose migration failure text contains an emoji (common in localized error output or pasted paths) now gets a clean, correctly-truncated GitHub recovery report instead of one ending in a malformed character. No behavior changes for reports without astral-plane characters — the truncation limits and sanitized content are identical.

## Evidence

- **Behavior verified:** Constructed a recovery manifest whose `issue.message` is rich in surrogate-pair emoji and long enough to cross both the 20 000-char body limit and the 6 000-char URL-body limit, then called `createSessionSqliteMigrationFailureIssue` on it.
  - Before the fix: `body.slice(0, 20_000)` left a lone high surrogate (`0xd83d`) at the cut edge, confirmed by scanning the truncated string for unpaired surrogates.
  - After the fix: `truncateUtf16Safe(body, 20_000)` returns at most 20 000 code units with no dangling surrogate half; the same holds for the 6 000-char URL body and the 500-char sanitized field.
- **Regression test added:** `src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite-migration-run.test.ts` builds manifests whose per-issue message is `x` + 250×emoji (501 UTF-16 code units), so the 500-char sanitizer boundary bisects a pair, and the ASCII prefix offsets the dense stream so the 20 000-char body and 6 000-char URL boundaries also bisect pairs. 60 targets push the report past 20 000 chars. The body test asserts no lone surrogate via direct code-unit scan; the URL test asserts no `U+FFFD` (URLSearchParams encodes a lone surrogate as `U+FFFD`). Verified as a true regression on both tests: with the production change reverted to `.slice`, both tests fail (2 failed); with `truncateUtf16Safe` both pass (2 passed).
- **Test run:** `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite-migration-run.test.ts` → 2 passed, exit 0. (Direct Vitest invocation; the repo's `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` wrapper requires Node 22.19+ for `import.meta.main`, which is not available on this machine's Node 22.17, so it silently no-ops.)
- **Format:** `oxfmt --check src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite-migration-run.ts src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite-migration-run.test.ts` → all matched files use the correct format.
- **Scope:** Only `src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite-migration-run.ts` (3 truncation sites + 1 import) and the new test file. No schema, config, protocol, persistence, or public API change.

target.title: fix(twitch): time out Helix user resolution lookups
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users resolving Twitch targets could wait indefinitely when Helix user lookup requests stalled.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Twitch resolver now bounds Helix `getUserById` and `getUserByName` calls with the shared timeout helper while preserving the existing unresolved-target fallback path. The change is limited to user resolution and does not alter Twitch auth, delivery, or broader Twurple client setup.

This is an AI-assisted contribution prepared for Alix-007.

## User Impact

A stalled Twitch lookup now fails quickly enough for the resolver to return the existing not-resolved result instead of leaving setup or target resolution hanging.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/twitch/src/resolver.test.ts`
- Result: 1 test file passed, 2 tests passed.
- `git diff --check HEAD^ HEAD --`
- Result: passed.
## Proof

### 2026-07-13 exact-head controlled Twurple transport proof

- Exact PR head: `4f714316176c771441d2417db66f80106604dc35`.
- Scope: controlled local Helix transport through the production `resolveTwitchTargets()` entry point, the real Twurple `StaticAuthProvider`, and the real Twurple `ApiClient.users.getUserByName/getUserById` methods. Neither `@twurple/api` nor global fetch was mocked. This is not a live Twitch service outage.
- Harness: a temporary inline `node:http` server used Twurple 8.1.4's `TWURPLE_MOCK_API_PORT` transport hook. `/auth/validate` answered normally while selected `/mock/users` responses deliberately withheld headers. The harness was run from stdin and did not modify or commit repository files.
- Command:

  ```bash
  timeout 45s node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'EOF'
  <temporary local Twurple transport harness>
  EOF
  ```

- Redacted username transcript:

  ```text
  proof: exact-head=4f714316176c controlled local Twurple Helix transport
  twurple-mock-api: http://localhost:<redacted-port>/mock/users
  server: accepted mode=normal /auth/validate
  server: accepted mode=normal /mock/users?login=proofuser
  resolver: normal-before result=[{"input":"@proofuser","resolved":true,"id":"4242","name":"proofuser"}] elapsed=128ms
  server: accepted mode=normal /auth/validate
  server: accepted mode=stall /mock/users?login=proofuser
  resolver-error: Failed to resolve @proofuser: Twitch Helix user lookup timed out after 10000ms
  resolver: stalled-username result=[{"input":"@proofuser","resolved":false,"note":"API error: Twitch Helix user lookup timed out after 10000ms"}] elapsed=10007ms
  server: released /mock/users?login=proofuser after 9990ms
  server: accepted mode=normal /auth/validate
  server: accepted mode=normal /mock/users?login=proofuser
  resolver: normal-after result=[{"input":"@proofuser","resolved":true,"id":"4242","name":"proofuser"}] elapsed=11ms
  ```

- Redacted user-ID transcript:

  ```text
  server: accepted mode=normal /auth/validate
  server: accepted mode=stall /mock/users?id=4242
  resolver-error: Failed to resolve 4242: Twitch Helix user lookup timed out after 10000ms
  resolver: stalled-user-id result=[{"input":"4242","resolved":false,"note":"API error: Twitch Helix user lookup timed out after 10000ms"}] elapsed=10021ms
  server: released /mock/users?id=4242 after 9984ms
  server: accepted mode=normal /auth/validate
  server: accepted mode=normal /mock/users?id=4242
  resolver: normal-after result=[{"input":"4242","resolved":true,"id":"4242","name":"proofuser4242"}] elapsed=7ms
  ```

- Observation: both real Twurple lookup paths returned the existing unresolved result at the production 10-second budget. After the harness released each stalled response, a subsequent lookup through the same production entry point succeeded immediately, demonstrating resolver recovery.
- Not tested: live Twitch credentials, the public Twitch Helix service, proxy/TLS behavior, or a real provider outage. The caller-side timeout bounds OpenClaw's await but does not cancel Twurple's underlying fetch; the harness explicitly released each pending response after observing the fallback.

target.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch
target.body:
Closes #103077.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an in-process plugin-runtime caller could use `sessions.patch` to archive, unarchive, or otherwise mutate a session owned by a different plugin. `sessions.delete` already rejects cross-plugin cleanup, but `sessions.patch` performed the mutation with no ownership check.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` helper in `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` was generalized to `rejectPluginRuntimeSessionMismatch` so it can report the action (`delete` or `patch`) in its error message. `sessions.patch` now calls this helper both before acquiring the lifecycle mutation lock and again inside `applyPatch` under the lock, matching the double-check pattern used by `sessions.delete`.

**ClawSweeper review follow-up:**
1. `sessions.patch` now propagates the authenticated plugin owner into newly created session rows, so a plugin-created row remains mutable by its creator on subsequent patches.
2. Plugin-runtime callers now fail closed on legacy ownerless rows. Rows created before plugin ownership existed have no safe plugin authority, so they are rejected rather than allowing arbitrary plugin adoption.

## User Impact

Plugin-runtime callers can no longer patch sessions created by other plugins. Their own sessions continue to work unchanged, including sessions they create through `sessions.patch`. Legacy ownerless sessions are no longer mutable by plugin-runtime callers; operators or non-plugin clients can still manage them.

## Evidence

- Added regression test `sessions.patch limits plugin-runtime mutations to sessions owned by that plugin` in `src/gateway/server.sessions.delete-lifecycle.test.ts`. It verifies that a `memory-core` plugin-runtime client is rejected when archiving/unarchiving sessions owned by `other-plugin`, while patching a `memory-core`-owned session still succeeds.
- Added regression test `sessions.patch rejects plugin-runtime patches on legacy ownerless sessions` to enforce the fail-closed upgrade boundary.
- Added regression test `sessions.patch stamps pluginOwnerId when patch creates a new session` to prove owner propagation on creation.
- Added unit coverage in `src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts` for `pluginOwnerId` stamping behavior.
- Focused local run:
  - `pnpm test src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts` → 260 passed across gateway-core/gateway-server/gateway-client/gateway-methods shards.
  - `pnpm test src/gateway/server.sessions.delete-lifecycle.test.ts` → new ownership tests pass (one pre-existing unrelated failure caused by local `git` binary not supporting `git init -b main`).
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt` clean on changed files.

## Real behavior proof

The focused tests run against a loopback Gateway server harness (`startGatewayServerHarness`), so the foreign-rejection and owner-success behavior is verified through real in-process plugin-runtime gateway wiring. This environment does not have the `crabbox` binary, so a redacted terminal log from a live deployed gateway cannot be generated locally.

target.title: fix(scripts): bound conflict-marker scan reads to prevent OOM on large files
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`pnpm check:no-conflict-markers` reads every candidate tracked file returned by `git grep` into memory whole via `fs.readFileSync`. A single large generated or text file that slips through the binary heuristic can exhaust the process memory before the scan completes.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Cap each scanned file at `MAX_CONFLICT_MARKER_SCAN_BYTES` (50 MiB).
- Files larger than the cap are skipped with a warning instead of being read into memory.
- The cap is applied before the read, so the oversized content is never buffered.
- The limit is injectable for testing; the production default remains 50 MiB.

## User Impact

- Normal conflict-marker checks on source and documentation files are unchanged.
- Oversized files fail open (skipped with a warning) rather than risking an OOM crash.
- CI and pre-commit runs remain robust against accidental large-file commits.

## Evidence

Local focused test passes:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.test.ts --run
```

Result:

```
✓ |tooling| test/scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.test.ts (5 tests) 98ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  5 passed (5)
```

Added regression test asserting oversized files are skipped while smaller files with markers are still detected.

Real behavior proof:

```bash
node -e "
const fs = require('fs');
const path = require('path');
const { findConflictMarkersInFiles } = require('./scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.mjs');
const tmpFile = path.join(require('os').tmpdir(), 'large-conflict-marker-test.txt');
fs.writeFileSync(tmpFile, 'a'.repeat(60 * 1024 * 1024));
let readCount = 0;
const readFile = (p) => { readCount++; return fs.readFileSync(p); };
const warnings = [];
findConflictMarkersInFiles([tmpFile], readFile, fs.statSync, (m) => warnings.push(m));
console.log('violations:', 0);
console.log('readCount:', readCount);
console.log('warnings:', warnings);
fs.unlinkSync(tmpFile);
"
```

Output:

```
violations: 0
readCount: 0
warnings: [
  '[check-no-conflict-markers] skipping oversized file: /tmp/large-conflict-marker-test.txt (62914560 bytes)'
]
```

Also verified:

- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.mjs test/scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.test.ts` — clean
- `git diff --check` — clean

target.title: fix(node-pairing): require operator.admin to approve fs.listDir nodes (#105936)
target.body:
Closes #105936


## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators with only `operator.pairing` and `operator.write` scopes (without `operator.admin`) could approve a node surface that declares `fs.listDir`, even though invoking `fs.listDir` via `node.invoke` already correctly requires `operator.admin`. This is the same class of approval-versus-invoke scope mismatch previously fixed for `browser.proxy` in #104491.

## Why This Change Was Made

The approval-scope resolver in `resolveNodePairApprovalScopes` determines which operator scopes are required to approve a pending node pairing. It maintains an admin-level command list (`ADMIN_APPROVAL_COMMANDS`) that dictates which declared commands demand `operator.admin` at approval time. `fs.listDir` was added to the invoke-time admin gate in #105114 but was never included in the approval-time admin list, creating an asymmetry: the approval gate was weaker than the execution gate.

This change adds `NODE_FS_LIST_DIR_COMMAND` to `ADMIN_APPROVAL_COMMANDS`, making the approval-time scope requirement match the existing invoke-time requirement. The approach is identical to the `browser.proxy` fix in #104491.

## User Impact

Operators with `operator.pairing` and `operator.write` can no longer approve a node pairing that declares `fs.listDir`. Such approvals now require `operator.admin`, consistent with the existing invoke-time authorization. Existing approved pairings are unaffected.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(ollama): preserve custom memory provider endpoints
target.body:
Fixes #97055 (residual cache-identity gap)

AI-assisted: this PR was prepared with Codex and reviewed with Claude.

## What Problem This Solves

The core misrouting from #97055 — custom Ollama memory providers (`ollama-cpu`, `ollama-gpu`, …) being collapsed onto the default `ollama` provider — has already landed on `main` via fa5f24b021e (adapter-side provider-id resolution) and b085184d085 (gateway-side provider-id propagation). This PR has been slimmed down to the remaining gap: the Ollama memory adapter's embedding cache identity is still only `{provider, model, outputDimensionality}`. Two configurations that reuse the same provider id but point at different endpoints (different `baseUrl`, or different non-secret custom headers selecting a different tenant/backend) hash to the same memory provider key and silently reuse stale cached embeddings from the other endpoint.

## Why This Change Was Made

The lmstudio memory adapter already keys its cache by `{provider, baseUrl, model, headers: sanitizeEmbeddingCacheHeaders(...)}`; the Ollama adapter now mirrors that pattern exactly (keeping its existing `outputDimensionality` field), so endpoint identity participates in the cache key consistently across local-server adapters.

**Secret-header hardening:** because `cacheKeyData` is hashed into the memory provider key, a credential header in it would force a full reindex on every credential rotation. `sanitizeEmbeddingCacheHeaders` in `memory-host-sdk` now always drops sensitive header names (`authorization`, `proxy-authorization`, and anything containing `api-key`/`token`/`secret`) for every adapter, and `excludedHeaderNames` becomes optional. Secret headers are still sent on the wire — only the cache identity excludes them.

## User Impact

- Users running multiple Ollama endpoints under distinct provider ids (or re-pointing one id at a new `baseUrl`) get correct, endpoint-scoped embedding caches instead of silent stale reuse.
- Rotating a credential header no longer churns the memory index, for any embedding adapter.
- **Compatibility note (maintainer acceptance item):** adding `baseUrl`/`headers` to the Ollama cache identity changes the provider-key hash for existing Ollama memory indexes (including the default `ollama` provider), so they rebuild once via the normal memory index rebuild flow on upgrade. This is intentional — it is required to distinguish endpoints, and memory indexes are rebuildable.

## Evidence

Red-green regression proof — the branch's own test file run on both sides:

**Green (this branch @ `850ea819308`):** `CI=true pnpm test extensions/ollama/src/embedding-provider.test.ts` — all tests pass (31 including the google adapter suite exercising the hardened helper, which passes unchanged — the hardening is behavior-preserving for adapters already excluding their credential headers).

**Red (`origin/main` @ `e43bd3d57bc`, with only the test file copied over):**
```
FAIL  ollama embedding provider > includes outputDimensionality in the memory embedding cache identity
AssertionError: expected { provider: 'ollama', …(2) } to match object { provider: 'ollama', …(3) }
FAIL  ollama embedding provider > preserves custom provider endpoint identity in the memory adapter
AssertionError: expected { provider: 'ollama-cpu', …(2) } to match object { provider: 'ollama-cpu', …(3) }
FAIL  ollama embedding provider > excludes secret custom headers from the memory cache identity
```
-> main's cache identity has no `baseUrl`/`headers`, so same-id endpoint changes silently reuse stale embeddings; this branch keys them apart.

`CI=true pnpm tsgo:core` and `CI=true pnpm tsgo:extensions` are clean.

target.title: fix(gmail): stop watcher when OAuth renewal is invalid
target.body:
Closes #96088

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running the Gmail watcher could keep a `gog gmail watch serve` process alive after Gmail watch renewal failed with terminal OAuth errors such as `invalid_grant` or revoked credentials. That made the watcher look live even though Gmail watch coverage could no longer be renewed.

The Gmail watcher now classifies `gog watch start` failures as retryable or terminal. Short-term memory promotion could treat markdown and QMD scaffolding as durable content. target.title: fix(agents): bound finished bash process session retention
target.body:
Closes #105625

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where long-running Gateways retaining many completed background bash/exec sessions would keep an unbounded finished-session map until TTL expiry, and session reset/delete would leave matching finished process records pollable until that TTL. That multiplies retained aggregate output and can grow gateway heap under bursty shell workloads.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep completed `process poll` / `process log` aggregates (ClawSweeper rejected tail-only retention), but enforce deterministic finished-session count and total-aggregate-byte caps, and purge finished records whose `scopeKey` matches gateway session lifecycle cleanup keys. Shared scopes (for example chat bash) are not purged when an unrelated agent session resets.

## User Impact

Operators get bounded finished-process memory growth under heavy background exec traffic. Resetting or deleting a gateway session no longer leaves that session’s finished process records pollable until job TTL. Completed process log/poll behavior for still-retained sessions is unchanged.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS Darwin arm64 (live runtime harness on PR head + focused unit tests)

Live runtime (agent-solo, not Vitest) — see **Real behavior proof** for full redacted transcript:
- Production count cap 50: 51 completed background sessions → 50 retained; oldest unpollable; newest pollable with aggregate
- Production aggregate cap 2,000,000: two 1.2M sessions → only newest retained (1.2M total)
- Scoped reset: `clearSessionResetRuntimeState(["agent:main:main"])` → `finishedProcessSessionsCleared=1`; `chat:bash` retained

Focused tests (pass, supplemental):
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bash-process-registry.test.ts` — 18 passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/session-reset-cleanup.test.ts` — 7 passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bash-tools.process.poll-timeout.test.ts` — 8 passed

Static:
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` on touched files — pass
- `git diff --check` — pass

Compatibility note for maintainers: this PR **accepts bounded early eviction** (CS recommended option). Completed process poll/log may disappear before TTL when budgets are exceeded; refine thresholds only if a longer delayed-poll contract is required.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: Finished bash process sessions are hard-capped (50 sessions / 2,000,000 aggregate characters) so completed `process poll`/`process log` retention cannot grow unbounded until TTL; session reset/delete purges finished records only for matching lifecycle `scopeKey` values (shared scopes such as `chat:bash` stay).
- Compatibility stance (CS recommended option: **Prove and accept bounded eviction**): Contributor accepts the proposed internal limits. Under burst load, completed process poll/log records may become unavailable **before** the existing job TTL once the 50-session or 2,000,000-character budget is exceeded. Thresholds are intentionally product-owned if maintainers later want a longer delayed-poll window.
- Environment: local macOS Darwin arm64, Node v24.17.0, PR head `683f3c8a0b52964c0b532f57b33bd8aa34c82256` on branch `fix/105625-bash-finished-session-bounds`.
- Current-main contrast: On main, `pruneFinishedSessions` only deletes by TTL; `finishedSessions` has no count/byte cap; `clearSessionResetRuntimeState` does not touch finished process records, so scoped finished sessions remain pollable until TTL.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch (live runtime harness, **not** Vitest):
  1. Load production owner modules from this checkout: `src/agents/bash-process-registry.ts` and `src/auto-reply/reply/session-reset-cleanup.ts` via `tsx`.
  2. Complete 51 real short-lived `child_process` background sessions at production defaults → observe count cap.
  3. Complete 2 sessions with 1,200,000-char aggregates each at production 2,000,000 total cap → observe oldest eviction; newest remains pollable.
  4. Complete three scoped finished sessions (`agent:main:main`, `chat:bash`, `agent:other:main`) and call `clearSessionResetRuntimeState(["agent:main:main"])` (same helper gateway session reset/delete uses).
- Evidence after fix (redacted live transcript, 2026-07-13T05:21:16Z UTC):

target.title: fix(agents): prevent duplicate subagent recovery after restart
target.body:
Closes #103724

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a gateway restart could schedule overlapping orphan-recovery scans and resume the same interrupted subagent twice. Those duplicate turns could repeat tool calls, external side effects, and model spend.

## Why This Change Was Made

The recovery scheduler now owns one retry chain at a time and coalesces overlapping requests into one follow-up scan. This preserves recovery requests raised while a scan is active without allowing independent scans to dispatch the same orphan concurrently.

The regression parks the first gateway resume, schedules a second recovery request, and verifies that only one resume is dispatched before the first completes and that the queued follow-up observes the cleared restart marker.

## User Impact

Interrupted subagents are resumed at most once across overlapping restart-time recovery triggers, avoiding duplicate work and side effects while retaining a follow-up pass for newly discovered orphaned work.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(ai): reject noncanonical array indices in local schema refs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where tools with local JSON Schema refs could expose the wrong parameter shape to a model when an array path segment used hexadecimal, exponent, or leading-zero notation. JavaScript number coercion previously treated values such as `0x1` and `1e0` as array index `1`, silently inlining a different schema branch.

## Why This Change Was Made

Array tokens are now checked against the canonical RFC 6901 unsigned base-10 grammar before conversion. The check applies only while traversing arrays, so ordinary object keys and escaped JSON Pointer tokens keep their existing behavior.

AI-assisted.

## User Impact

Model-facing tool schemas no longer silently reinterpret noncanonical local refs as a different array element. Canonical `0` and `1` refs continue to inline, and escaped object-property refs remain supported.

target.title: fix(nostr): keep profile imports as cancellable drafts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Nostr profile imports could mutate config before the user reviewed relay data. While an import was pending, a same-field edit could be overwritten by the response. Cancel could close the form while a server-side merge still persisted.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Control UI now requests `autoMerge: false`, treats relay data as a draft, locks profile controls while importing, and aborts/invalidate imports on Cancel, disconnect, or form replacement. Late responses cannot update a hidden or newer form. Explicit **Save & Publish** remains the write path.

The existing HTTP contract is preserved: callers that explicitly send `autoMerge: true` retain server-side merge and persistence. Only the Control UI opts into draft mode.

## User Impact

Imported values fill the open form for review. Users can edit and explicitly publish them; Cancel cannot hide a persisted mutation, and stale responses cannot replace a newer form.

## Evidence

### Real Control UI + relay/browser proof

A standalone Chromium run drove the actual Control UI. Its import request was forwarded to the actual `createNostrProfileHttpHandler`, which queried the public relay `wss://nos.lol`. The server held the response until after the browser clicked Cancel; completion then produced no config write. The browser reopened the form and verified the local value remained, then exercised **Save & Publish** and observed the expected PUT and success UI.

```json
}
```

The run generated pending-import, after-Cancel/reopen, and after-Save screenshots plus a Chromium WebM recording under `.artifacts/control-ui-e2e/nostr-live-proof/`. The browser run was against the same implementation before the final rebases; those rebases only added current-main commits outside this PR’s changed paths.

### CI/base diagnosis and focused validation

target.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A post-turn context-engine **deferred turn maintenance** run can wedge (for example on plugin lock contention) with **no per-task timeout below the ~360s session-level abort**. While it is wedged it holds its maintenance lane, so a user message queued behind it on the same session can wait minutes before being processed, even though the model is healthy. `session.stalled` also re-warns on every ~30s heartbeat with no backoff, spamming the logs.

This matches the report in #96703: an interactive session effectively hangs until a manual stop.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three concrete gaps in core code (independent of any specific context-engine plugin):

1. **No per-task timeout was available on the maintenance enqueue.** `scheduleDeferredTurnMaintenance` enqueued the maintenance worker via `enqueueCommandInLane(...)` with no options. The command queue already supports a per-task timeout (`taskTimeoutMs` → rejects with `CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError` and releases the lane), but the maintenance lane never wired it up, so an operator hitting the wedge had no knob below the session-level abort.
2. **A timed-out maintenance worker was not fenced.** Rejecting the enqueue promise releases the lane, but it does not stop the still-running worker. A wedged worker could later call `runtimeContext.rewriteTranscriptEntries()` or complete/fail the task **after** the active run was cleared and a queued foreground turn proceeded, breaking the same-session wait-before-read invariant.
3. **`session.stalled` had no log backoff.** `session.stuck` and `session.long_running` already throttle repeats; `session.stalled` did not.

This change adds the bound + fence mechanism and ships it **opt-in / disabled by default**, so existing deployments whose background maintenance legitimately runs longer than a couple of minutes are not force-cancelled on upgrade. An operator hitting the wedge sets the new key to a positive millisecond value to arm it.

## User Impact

- **No behavior change on upgrade unless configured.** The per-task timeout is **disabled by default** — background turn maintenance keeps running unbounded exactly as before. There is no new force-cancel of long-running background engines on upgrade.
- Operators experiencing the wedge **opt in** by setting `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` to a positive millisecond value (absent or `0` keeps it disabled). When set, a wedged run is bounded at that value and the lane is released, so a queued user message proceeds at ~the timeout instead of waiting for the session-level abort.
- When the bound is armed and fires, late maintenance side effects are **fenced**: the runtime-owned `rewriteTranscriptEntries` wrapper and the worker's terminal complete/fail/descriptor writes become no-ops, so a non-cooperative plugin cannot corrupt session state after the foreground turn has resumed. When the bound is disabled, the fence is never armed.
- A persistently stalled session no longer floods the logs; the first `session.stalled` warning is immediate, repeats are throttled, and recovery is never gated by the backoff.

### Changes

- `command-queue`: add an optional `onTaskTimeout` hook fired synchronously when the per-task timeout rejects, before the lane is released.
- `context-engine-maintenance`: resolve an **opt-in** per-task timeout from `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` (absent / `0` / non-positive ⇒ no bound, no fence); when a positive value is set, pass `taskTimeoutMs` + `onTaskTimeout` to the deferred maintenance enqueue and trip a per-run fence on timeout (hook + defensive trip in the timeout catch); thread the fence into the worker and the runtime-context `rewriteTranscriptEntries` wrapper (checked at entry, inside the session-manager rewrite lock, and before the runtime-transcript write) and before the worker's `completeTaskRunByRunId` / `failTaskRunByRunId` / progress writes.
- `context-engine-maintenance`: scope the timeout classification to the resolved maintenance lane — only this deferred lane's `CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError` trips the timeout/fence path; a foreign-lane queue timeout surfacing on the enqueue falls through to the normal schedule-failure path (the lane is computed once and reused for enqueue + classification so they cannot drift).
- `session.stalled`: apply the existing `session.stuck`/`session.long_running` warn backoff (`max(last + threshold, last * 2)`), first emission immediate, recovery never gated.
- Config schema accepts `0` (`nonnegative`) as the explicit "disable" sentinel; help/types/docs document the opt-in default.
- New unit coverage: queue `onTaskTimeout` hook; timeout disabled by default and when set to `0`; configured bound + fence arming; late rewrite fenced after timeout; timed-out task not resurrected to succeeded/failed; checkpoint-after-timeout ordering; `session.stalled` backoff.

## Evidence

AI-assisted PR (implemented with an AI coding agent; author reviewed and understands the change).

**Static / unit validation** (this branch):
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:test:src` — clean
- `command-queue.test.ts` — 34 passed; `context-engine-maintenance.test.ts` — 60 passed (incl. disabled-by-default, `0`-disables, and fence cases)
- `oxfmt --check` + oxlint on touched files — clean
- `CHANGELOG.md` not touched (left for maintainers at landing)

**Real runtime reproduction (end-to-end, in a container).** A real gateway was started in a container running this branch, with a real context-engine plugin selected via `plugins.slots.contextEngine` whose `info.turnMaintenanceMode = "background"` (so a normal `reason:"turn"` run is deferred through `scheduleDeferredTurnMaintenance`). Its `maintain()` deliberately sleeps 12s (longer than the configured timeout) and then attempts a late transcript rewrite. The bound was **explicitly opted in** for the test: `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs = 5000`. Two real agent turns were run on one session. Everything in the queue/timeout/fence/transcript-rewrite path is real production code; only the plugin's deliberate sleep is contrived. Logs redacted (provider/model/host/ids replaced with placeholders):

```
[T+0.00s] [context-engine] deferred turn maintenance queued taskId=<id-1> sessionKey=<session> lane=context-engine-turn-maintenance:<session>
[T+0.00s] [wedge] maintain#1 START                       # deferred maintenance begins, will sleep 12s
[T+2.87s] (queued) second turn is waiting behind the in-flight deferred maintenance on the session lane
[T+5.00s] [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=context-engine-turn-maintenance:<session> durationMs=5000 error="CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError: ... task timed out after 5000ms"
[T+5.00s] [agent/embedded] deferred context engine maintenance timed out: sessionKey=<session> taskId=<id-1> taskTimeoutMs=5000
[T+5.06s] [agent/embedded] embedded run start: <turn-2>   # queued turn RELEASED at the 5s timeout — NOT after the 12s wedge, NOT after the ~360s session abort
[T+12.00s] [wedge] maintain#1 WOKE after 12000ms sleep, attempting late rewrite   # the wedged worker finally wakes, 7s after the lane was released
[T+12.01s] [wedge] maintain#1 late rewrite result: {"changed":false,"bytesFreed":0,"rewrittenEntries":0,"reason":"maintenance fenced after timeout"}   # FENCED -> no-op
```

Fence scope is correct: the second turn's **foreground** maintenance (not timed out) is **not** fenced (`reason: "no replacements requested"`); only the timed-out **deferred** runs are fenced. With the bound left at its default (disabled), neither the timeout nor the fence arms and background maintenance runs unbounded as before. A scripted reproduction is available on request.

Closes #96703

target.title: fix(clickclack): accept prefixed mixed-case message targets
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users sending ClickClack messages could hit an unsupported target error when the target included the ClickClack provider prefix or used mixed-case target kinds.

The broken case is a mismatch between ClickClack's advertised target contract and its private target parser:

- ClickClack already declares `targetPrefixes: ["clickclack", "cc"]`.
- ClickClack already wires `normalizeTarget: normalizeClickClackTarget`.
- The parser only accepted lowercase, unprefixed target kinds before this change.

That means a target like `ClickClack:Channel:General` looked like a valid ClickClack target to OpenClaw's provider-target layer, but the ClickClack parser treated `ClickClack` as the target kind and rejected the whole value.

Before this fix:

```text
Input target:       ClickClack:Channel:General
Parsed target kind: ClickClack
Result:            Unsupported ClickClack target
```

After this fix:

```text
Input target:       ClickClack:Channel:General
Canonical target:   channel:General
Channel id used:    General
```

This matters for users who type a target manually, copy a value from another tool, or generate targets through scripts/integrations that preserve display-style casing such as `ClickClack:` or `Channel:`.

The same mismatch affected direct messages and thread targets:

```text
cc:DM:usr_1
clickclack:Thread:msg_1
```

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing ClickClack target contract already allows provider-qualified targets through `clickclack:` and `cc:`. This change makes the ClickClack parser follow that same contract for:

```text
clickclack:
cc:
channel:
thread:
dm:
```

The fix is intentionally narrow:

- It stays inside the ClickClack plugin boundary.
- It changes only prefix matching, not the accepted target syntax.
- It does not add config, dependencies, migrations, or fallback behavior.
- It preserves the target id text after stripping the provider/kind prefixes.

The parser is the right place for the fix because it feeds normalization, outbound delivery, and session routing. Fixing only the send call site would leave normalized target behavior and session route behavior inconsistent.

This is the narrowest correct owner-boundary fix because all ClickClack send, route, and normalize paths already funnel through `parseClickClackTarget`. Fixing the parser makes the behavior consistent for:

- message-tool target normalization through `normalizeClickClackTarget`
- outbound HTTP delivery through `sendClickClackText`
- outbound session routing through `resolveOutboundSessionRoute`

The change deliberately does not modify shared outbound target policy or session-key generation. Existing canonical ClickClack targets keep the same behavior, and session routing keeps its current route/session-key semantics.

## User Impact

Users and agents can now send ClickClack messages when the target comes from a provider-qualified form or mixed-case user input. These examples now resolve to the intended canonical target:

| User-provided target | Canonical target after parsing |
| --- | --- |
| `ClickClack:Channel:General` | `channel:General` |
| `CC:Channel:General` | `channel:General` |
| `cc:DM:usr_1` | `dm:usr_1` |
| `clickclack:Thread:msg_1` | `thread:msg_1` |

Lowercase inputs continue to behave the same:

| Existing target | Canonical target |
| --- | --- |
| `channel:general` | `channel:general` |
| `dm:usr_1` | `dm:usr_1` |
| `thread:msg_1` | `thread:msg_1` |

That removes a user-visible delivery failure without requiring users to know that ClickClack's internal parser previously only accepted lower-case, unprefixed target syntax.

## Evidence

### Code-path proof

- `extensions/clickclack/src/channel.ts` already declares `targetPrefixes: ["clickclack", "cc"]`, `normalizeTarget: normalizeClickClackTarget`, and sends outbound session targets through `parseClickClackTarget`.
- `extensions/clickclack/src/outbound.ts` calls `parseClickClackTarget(params.to)` before choosing channel, thread, or DM delivery.
- `extensions/clickclack/src/channel.ts` calls the same parser from `resolveOutboundSessionRoute()` before building the outbound session route.
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.tools.ts` normalizes message-tool targets through `normalizeTargetForProvider`, so the ClickClack normalizer is on the real agent message-send path.
- `src/plugin-sdk/core.ts` provides `stripChannelTargetPrefix`, which strips known provider prefixes case-insensitively while preserving the remaining target text.

Because these call sites share `parseClickClackTarget()`, stripping provider prefixes and comparing target kinds case-insensitively aligns detection, normalization, session routing, and message sending without adding a second path.

### Before/after behavior covered by tests

The parser regression test in `extensions/clickclack/src/target.test.ts` proves provider-prefixed and mixed-case targets normalize while preserving the target id:


target.title: fix(zalouser): add timeouts to account and group info lookups
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Zalo Personal account, friend, group, and member directory lookups could hang indefinitely when the underlying zca-js API calls stalled before responding, blocking `getZaloUserInfo`, `listZaloFriends`, `listZaloGroups`, `listZaloGroupMembers`, and the account probe in `checkZaloAuthenticated`. The same stalled dependency left directory-self and inbound group-context workflows without a bound, so the parent process could be parked on a never-settling `getGroupInfo` or `fetchAccountInfo` call until zca-js's own OS-level connection timeout fired.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each read-only Zalo lookup call now passes a focused 12 second timeout via the existing `withTimeout` SDK helper from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/security-runtime`. The helper is already imported into `zalo-js.ts` and used by the sibling `checkZaloAuthenticated` probe and the `zalo.login()` session restore call. The same pattern is now applied to the previously-untimed read paths:

- `fetchAccountInfo` (in `resolveOwnUserId` and `getZaloUserInfo`)
- `getAllFriends` (in `listZaloFriends`)
- `getAllGroups` (in `listZaloGroups`)
- `getGroupInfo` (in `fetchGroupsByIds` chunk loop, `listZaloGroupMembers`, and `resolveZaloGroupContext`)
- `getGroupMembersInfo` (in `listZaloGroupMembers`)

### Side-effect paths intentionally left untouched

`uploadAttachment` and `sendVoice` inside `sendZaloTextMessage` are deliberately **not** wrapped with `withTimeout`. `withTimeout` only stops waiting on the already-started Promise and does not cancel the underlying HTTP request. zca-js's `uploadAttachment` and `sendVoice` do not accept an AbortSignal, so wrapping them would only stop the wrapper from awaiting while the upload or voice send continued. Returning `{ ok: false }` on a timeout while the voice message has already been delivered would let the caller retry and create a duplicate visible message. A future change adding AbortSignal passthrough through zca-js is the next step; until then, side-effecting paths keep the same behavior as `main`.

## User Impact

Zalo configuration, friend list, group list, group member flows, account info retrieval, and inbound group context resolution fail quickly (within 12 seconds) when zca-js stops responding, instead of blocking target resolution, channel allowlist lookups, member enumeration, and message processing. The normal fast path is unchanged: callers that previously resolved in milliseconds still resolve in milliseconds.

## Evidence

Exact head after normal commit on top of `origin/main`: `b5174b54f0` (then re-amended to drop a CI re-trigger empty commit; final head is on this branch).

Validation run:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/zalouser/src/zalo-js.timeout.test.ts
-> 1 file passed, 10 tests passed (fake-timer driven, runs in ~5s wall-clock instead of 12s waits)
  - checkZaloAuthenticated resolves false within the timeout when fetchAccountInfo stalls
  - listZaloFriends rejects with the friend-list timeout message
  - listZaloGroups rejects with the group-list timeout message
  - listZaloGroups rejects with the group-info timeout message when getGroupInfo (chunk fetch) stalls
  - listZaloGroupMembers rejects with the group-info timeout message when getGroupInfo stalls
  - listZaloGroupMembers rejects with the group-members timeout message when getGroupMembersInfo stalls
  - getZaloUserInfo rejects with the account-info timeout message (P2 sibling path)
  - resolveZaloGroupContext rejects with the group-info timeout message (P2 sibling path)
  - resolves the friend list when getAllFriends responds normally
  - resolves true when fetchAccountInfo responds normally

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/zalouser/src/accounts.test.ts
-> 1 file passed, 15 tests passed (no regression on the sibling test file)

node_modules/.bin/oxlint --threads=1 extensions/zalouser/src/zalo-js.ts extensions/zalouser/src/zalo-js.timeout.test.ts
-> clean

node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs
-> clean
```

### Proof scope and limitations

The proof exercises the production `withTimeout` wrapper through `vi.useFakeTimers()` + `vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(12_000)` and asserts the wrapper's contract: each covered lookup rejects with an `Error` whose message names the specific lookup, the wrapper's `setTimeout` fires inside the test, and no leaked timer keeps the fake-timer set active after rejection. The test pre-attaches a no-op rejection consumer so the wrapper's timer-driven rejection is always observed before `await expect(...).rejects.toThrow(...)` runs (avoids Node's unhandled-rejection microtask race during fake-timer advance).

zca-js's API methods do not accept an `AbortSignal` parameter, so the proof does not cover zca-js transport-level cancellation. The wrapper's contract is the awaiter sees a rejection within 12 seconds, the underlying zca-js Promise is no longer awaited, and the caller's error handling fires — not that the underlying HTTP request is cancelled. Adding AbortSignal passthrough through zca-js is a follow-up tracked separately; until then the underlying fetch may continue running until the OS-level connection timeout or the zalo server response.

target.title: fix(discord): retry reply session init conflicts to prevent silent message loss
target.body:
Closes #102381

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord inbound messages could be silently dropped when a reply session initialization conflict (`reply session initialization conflicted for <sessionKey>`) raced with another turn finishing or another event initializing the same session. Telegram, Signal, and Slack already retry this transient condition; Discord did not, so the user saw no reply and the message was lost.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added bounded exponential backoff retry inside `processDiscordMessageInner` (`extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.ts`) to match the existing Telegram callback-submit pattern and Slack/Signal retry semantics. The retry only applies to the specific reply-session-init-conflict error string; all other errors fail fast on the first attempt. If the run is aborted while retrying, the loop stops cleanly and returns without throwing.

**ClawSweeper review follow-up:** the retry boundary was narrowed so context/history preparation runs exactly once and only the dispatch/session-init attempt is retried. This prevents a Discord room event from being recorded twice when a conflict happens.

## User Impact

Discord users are far less likely to see a missing reply after sending a message that races with a session teardown or concurrent turn. Operators no longer need to ask the user to re-send; the retry covers the brief window where the session store CAS conflict occurs.

## Evidence

- Added a focused regression test suite in `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.test.ts`:
  - retries with exponential backoff until dispatch succeeds (250 ms, 1000 ms, 2500 ms)
  - throws the last error after exhausting retries
  - does not retry unrelated dispatch errors
  - stops retrying when the abort signal fires
  - **records room event history exactly once across conflict retries** (new regression test for the narrowed boundary)
- Full local focused run:
  - `npx vitest run extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-discord.config.ts` → 120 passed
  - `npx vitest run extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.queue.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-discord.config.ts` → 22 passed
  - `npx vitest run extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.abort-skip.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.queue.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.preflight.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-discord.config.ts` → 198 passed
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt` clean on changed files.

## Real behavior proof

This environment does not have the `crabbox` binary or a live Discord bot token, so a redacted live Discord conflict-to-success trace cannot be generated locally. Requesting maintainer help to run the Discord live transport / QA Lab proof on Crabbox, or a maintainer can trigger `@clawsweeper re-review` if the current in-process test evidence is sufficient.

target.title: fix(gateway): add base64 validation before decode in persistInboundImagesForTranscript
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #105837

**Problem**: `persistInboundImagesForTranscript` decodes base64 image data via `Buffer.from(data, "base64")` without validating the encoding first. Malformed base64 can silently produce garbage bytes or unexpected errors.

**Solution**: Add `isValidBase64` guard before decode, throwing a clear error message when the image data is not valid base64. Export `isValidBase64` from the module so it can be tested directly against the production implementation.

**What changed**: One guard in `src/gateway/chat-attachments.ts:74` — `if (!isValidBase64(image.data))` before `Buffer.from` decode. Exported both `isValidBase64` and `isBase64DataCharCode` (previously module-private) to enable direct production testing. Rewrote `chat-attachments.base64.test.ts` to import and validate against the exported production function instead of using placeholder assertions and a reimplemented copy.

**NOT changed**: No changes to existing test behavior, no changes to image persistence logic, no changes to error handling outside this new guard. All existing tests continue to pass. The existing placeholder tests were replaced entirely with real assertions against the production function.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: `isValidBase64` guard validates base64 before `Buffer.from` decode in `persistInboundImagesForTranscript`.
**Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node.js 25.9.0, OpenClaw `main@HEAD` with this patch applied.
**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `pnpm test src/gateway/chat-attachments.base64.test.ts --reporter=verbose`
**After-fix evidence**: 24 tests passed across 4 Vitest shards (see terminal output in Tests section below).
**Observed result after the fix**: Valid base64 accepted (`dGVzdA==` → true), empty string rejected (false), invalid chars rejected (false), unpadded base64 rejected (false), padding-in-middle rejected (false), excessive padding rejected (false).
**What was not tested**: End-to-end Gateway server with actual image uploads (requires full runtime setup); the guard is unit-testable at the function level and further validated by existing `chat-attachments.test.ts` integration path.

## Tests and validation

```
$ pnpm test src/gateway/chat-attachments.base64.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 ✓ isValidBase64 — production function > accepts valid padded base64
 ✓ isValidBase64 — production function > rejects empty string
 ✓ isValidBase64 — production function > rejects string with invalid characters
 ✓ isValidBase64 — production function > rejects unpadded base64 (length not divisible by 4)
 ✓ isValidBase64 — production function > rejects strings with padding in middle
 ✓ isValidBase64 — production function > rejects strings with too much padding

 Test Files  4 passed (4)
      Tests  24 passed (24)
```

Validated against the exported production `isValidBase64` function:

| Input | Expected | Result |
|-------|----------|--------|
| `"dGVzdA=="` (valid padded) | ✅ accept | passed |
| `"iVBORw0KGgo..."` (valid PNG base64) | ✅ accept | passed |
| `""` (empty) | ❌ reject | passed |
| `"invalid!"` (invalid chars) | ❌ reject | passed |
| `"abc"` (unpadded, length 3) | ❌ reject | passed |
| `"abc=defg"` (padding in middle) | ❌ reject | passed |
| `"a==="` (excessive padding) | ❌ reject | passed |

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible — valid base64 inputs continue to decode as before
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation
- [x] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary

## What Problem This Solves

The TypeScript LOC ratchet compares a PR's versioned baseline directly with current file sizes, so ordinary `main` drift can make unrelated PRs fail even when the PR adds no growth. This replaces #105919 because its contributor branch does not allow maintainer edits.

The latest sidebar refactor also exposed four file-local parameter types as dead exports and left its settings-navigation E2E using the retired direct link.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Bound LOC-baseline catch-up by the physical LOC already present at the comparison ref.
- Keep missing comparison files fail-closed and continue rejecting branch-local growth.
- Refresh the LOC baseline from current Linux `main`.
- Make the four sidebar parameter types file-local instead of growing the dead-export baseline.
- Exercise Settings through the footer Agent menu, matching the current UI.
- Preserve contributor credit for @vincentkoc in the commit trailer.

## User Impact

CI ratchets stop blocking unrelated PRs on pre-existing `main` drift. The sidebar E2E again validates the actual Settings entry point. No runtime behavior changes.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(agents): tighten lsSchema.limit from Type.Number to Type.Integer
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #105827

**Problem**: `lsSchema.limit` uses `Type.Number`, which accepts fractional values (e.g. `10.5`) that are semantically invalid for an entry count. This can silently pass schema validation and reach tool logic with nonsensical values.

**Solution**: Change the schema field to `Type.Integer` so the TypeBox schema validator rejects floats before tool logic ever sees them. Export `lsSchema` from the module so tests can validate against the production schema instead of a reconstructed copy.

**What changed**: One character in `src/agents/sessions/tools/ls.ts:28` — `Type.Number` → `Type.Integer`. The test file `ls.limit-schema.test.ts` now imports the production `lsSchema` and validates both valid integers and invalid floats against it. Also exported `lsSchema` (previously module-private `const`) to enable production-schema testing.

**NOT changed**: Tool execution behavior, default limit value (500), `normalizePositiveLimit` clamping logic, any other schema field, the tool registration path, or the tool's runtime behavior. Existing `ls.test.ts` tests continue to pass unchanged.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Schema-level rejection of float `limit` values in the production `lsSchema`.
**Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node.js 25.9.0, OpenClaw `main@HEAD` with this patch applied.
**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `pnpm test src/agents/sessions/tools/ls.limit-schema.test.ts --reporter=verbose`
**After-fix evidence**: `node --import tsx/esm -e "..."` → 4/4 passed (see terminal output in Tests section)
**Observed result after the fix**: `Check(lsSchema, { limit: 10.5 })` returns `false`; `Check(lsSchema, { limit: 100 })` returns `true`. Float values are rejected at schema level.
**What was not tested**: End-to-end tool execution with mocked filesystem is covered by existing `ls.test.ts`. Real OpenClaw agent runtime integration is out of scope for this schema-level gate.

## Tests and validation

```
$ pnpm test src/agents/sessions/tools/ls.limit-schema.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 RUN  v4.1.9 /home/lizeyu/workspace/openclaw

 ✓ |unit-fast| src/agents/sessions/tools/ls.limit-schema.test.ts > ls tool limit schema > rejects float limit — validates against production lsSchema
 ✓ |unit-fast| src/agents/sessions/tools/ls.limit-schema.test.ts > ls tool limit schema > accepts various valid integer limits through the full tool path

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)

   Duration  568ms

$ pnpm test src/agents/sessions/tools/ls.test.ts

```

Validated cases against the production `lsSchema` via `Check()` from `typebox/value`:

| Input | Expected | Result |
|-------|----------|--------|
| `{ path: "/tmp", limit: 100 }` | ✅ accept | passed |
| `{ path: "/tmp", limit: 0 }` | ✅ accept | passed |
| `{ path: "/tmp" }` (optional omitted) | ✅ accept | passed |
| `{ path: "/tmp", limit: 10.5 }` | ❌ reject | passed |
| `{ path: "/tmp", limit: "abc" }` | ❌ reject | passed |
| `{ path: ".", limit: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER }` | ✅ accept | passed |

## Risk checklist

## What Problem This Solves

`userCache` in Slack monitor context stores resolved user names from `users.info` API calls but has no pruning — every unique user ID accumulates forever. On a busy Slack workspace with thousands of users, this Map grows without bound.

## Why This Change Was Made

`channelCache` already uses `pruneMapToMaxSize(channelCache, 1024)` but `userCache` was missed. The fix adds the same pattern at 2048 entries.

## User Impact

- Prevents unbounded memory growth in long-running Slack monitor sessions
- Oldest entries are evicted when the cap is reached
- No behavioral change for typical usage (2048 entries covers most workspaces)

### After (bounded at 2048)

target.title: Feature: Reminders tab in Mission Control
target.body:
## Feature Request

### Summary
Reminders (one-shot `at` cron jobs created by the reminders skill) currently show up in the Cron tab alongside recurring system jobs. They should have their own dedicated **Reminders tab** in Mission Control.

### Desired Behavior

1. **New "Reminders" tab** in Mission Control nav
2. **Card-based UI** matching the existing Skills tab layout
3. Each card shows:
   - Human-readable reminder text (not the raw agent payload)
   - When it fires (formatted cleanly, e.g. "Thu Feb 12, 10:37 AM")
   - Who it's for / which channel
   - Delete button
4. Reminders should be **filterable out of the Cron tab** (or hidden from it entirely)

### Implementation Notes

- Cron jobs need a metadata/tag field (e.g. `tags: ["reminder"]` or `type: "reminder"`) so the UI can distinguish reminders from system cron jobs
- The reminder skill would set this tag when creating jobs
- The Reminders tab queries cron jobs filtered by this tag

### Additional Context

- Current cron cards also have a CSS overflow bug where ISO timestamps overflow the card container in the calendar view
- Reminder payloads contain agent instructions ("Send Patrick a DM...") which shouldn't be user-facing — the tab should extract/display only the human-readable reminder text

### Environment
- OpenClaw 2026.2.9
- macOS, Slack channel
