target.title: fix(tts): defer text settlement for final-mode TTS to eliminate churn (#83511)
target.body:
## Summary

When `messages.tts.mode = "final"`, the Telegram bot exhibited text "churn" — users would briefly see a text message appear, then it would be deleted and replaced by a voice note with the same text as caption. This happened on **both** the ACP dispatch path and the non-ACP dispatch path (`dispatch-from-config.ts`).

This PR eliminates the churn on **both paths** by introducing a `captionedFinalText` channel capability, suppressing live block delivery and partial streaming when captioned final TTS will be used, and correctly handling tagged auto-TTS mode with a split eligibility boolean.

## Root cause

```
Before (main):
  1. Block text / partial streaming delivers text to user immediately
  2. TTS synthesis runs (2-5 seconds)
  3. Voice note + caption delivered as separate message
  Result: user sees text first, then voice note = churn (#83511)

After (this PR):
  1. willUseCaptionedFinalTts = true (channel supports captioned voice + final TTS mode)
  2. Partial streaming suppressed, block text delivery suppressed
  3. TTS synthesis runs, text accumulated silently
  4. Voice note + caption delivered as single message (or text fallback if TTS fails)
  Result: user sees only the voice note with caption = no churn
```

### Tagged auto-TTS mode

When `messages.tts.auto: "tagged"`, TTS only fires for replies containing `[[tts:...]]` directives. Three additional issues were discovered and fixed:

1. **Split boolean**: `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` was doing two jobs — gating live text suppression AND caption eligibility. Split into `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` (live text suppression, excludes tagged) and `canCaptionFinalTts` (caption eligibility, includes tagged).

2. **Block TTS gate**: The accumulated block TTS fallback was gated on `replies.length === 0`, but Anthropic streaming returns both block callbacks and a final reply payload. Changed to gate on `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` and `queuedFinal` instead.

3. **Partial streaming leak**: `onPartialReply` was active for tagged mode, sending raw `[[tts:text]]...[[/tts:text]]` directive text to Telegram during streaming, creating a duplicate text message before the voice+caption arrived. Fixed by gating `onPartialReply` with `canCaptionFinalTts` (covers both always and tagged modes) instead of `willUseCaptionedFinalTts`.

### Media block preservation

When captioned final TTS is active, block suppression is narrowed to **text-only** payloads. Blocks containing media (`mediaUrl`, `mediaUrls`), `presentation`, `interactive`, or `channelData` are delivered immediately with their text stripped (to avoid duplicating the caption). This applies to both ACP and non-ACP dispatch paths.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.ts` | `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` + `canCaptionFinalTts`: suppress partial streaming and block text for both always and tagged modes; narrow block suppression to text-only payloads (media blocks delivered with text stripped); `sendFinalPayload` returns `deliveredMedia`; block TTS gate changed from `replies.length === 0` to `!deliveredFinalTtsMedia && !queuedFinal` |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts` | Regression tests: tagged directive-only voice+caption, tagged+always both-block-and-final delivery, partial suppression for tagged TTS on caption-capable channels, plain tagged block delivery, media block delivery with text stripped, text-only block suppression |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.ts` | `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` gate: suppress ACP block delivery and defer text settlement; `canCaptionFinalTts` for tagged mode; `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` tracking |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.ts` | `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` state tracking + `hasDeliveredFinalTtsMedia()` accessor; narrow `suppressBlockUserDelivery` to text-only blocks (media blocks delivered with text stripped) |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.test.ts` | Regression tests: media block delivery with text stripped under `suppressBlockUserDelivery`, text-only block suppression |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.test.ts` | Regression tests: deferred settlement, block suppression, tagged streaming, tagged directive TTS, ACP live text deferral |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/acp-projector.ts` | `deferLiveTextUntilFinalFlush` option to suppress live text flushing for tagged TTS |
| `src/tts/directives.ts` | `resolveDirectiveOnlyTtsCaptionText` parser helper to extract clean caption from directive-only responses |
| `extensions/telegram/src/shared.ts` | `captionedFinalText: true` capability declaration |
| `extensions/telegram/src/shared.test.ts` | Test for capability declaration |
| `src/channels/plugins/types.core.ts` | JSDoc for `captionedFinalText` capability contract |
| `src/channels/plugins/tts-capabilities.test.ts` | Capability seam test |
| `docs/tools/tts.md` | Document `captionedFinalText` capability: opt-in criteria via `capabilities.tts.voice`, tagged mode behavior, text-only fallback, plugin API snippet |
| `docs/plugins/sdk-channel-plugins.md` | Document `captionedFinalText` capability in channel plugin SDK guide: opt-in declaration, media block preservation, fallback behavior, tagged mode |
| `docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256` | Updated SDK API baseline hash |

## Tests

```
$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts
 ✓ 272 passed (272)

$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.test.ts

$ npx vitest run extensions/telegram/src/shared.test.ts

```

  2. Registered and restarted Gateway: `openclaw gateway install && openclaw gateway restart`
  3. Tested with `messages.tts.auto: "always"` and `messages.tts.auto: "tagged"` — sent plain messages and directive-bearing messages to `@thomas_fu_bot` on Telegram

- **Evidence after fix**: Always mode (`messages.tts.auto: "always"`) at commit `05b4483a8f`:

  Always-mode replies produce a single voice note with caption text. No text churn, no separate text bubble.

- **Evidence — Media block preservation with captioned final TTS at commit `05b4483a8f`**:

  ![Media block preserved — image delivered + voice note with caption](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jerry-Xin/openclaw/proof-images-83988/.proof-images/83988-media-block.png)

  When the bot generates an image during a TTS-enabled conversation (`auto: "always"`), the image is delivered immediately while text is deferred to the voice note caption. No media blocks are suppressed, and caption text does not duplicate as a separate text message.

- **Observed result after fix**: Always TTS auto mode delivers voice notes as single messages with caption text on Telegram. Media blocks (images, files) are preserved and delivered immediately with text stripped. No text flash, no duplicate messages, no media loss.

- **What was not tested**: Other TTS providers (only Microsoft TTS tested live). Group chat TTS (tested in DM only). Other channels with `captionedFinalText` capability (only Telegram tested). Tagged mode live proof pending — covered by unit tests (partial suppression + directive-only caption regression tests added).

## Settle-lifecycle reconciliation (rebased onto current main)

Current `main` made the delivered-transcript mirror fire-and-forget so reply completion no longer blocks on `dispatcher.waitForIdle()`. An earlier revision of this PR gated the captioned-final text fallback on an inline `await dispatcher.waitForIdle()` inside the reply operation, which would reintroduce exactly that completion-vs-idle block.

The fallback rides the same dispatcher settle lifecycle instead of an inline wait, and it is attributed **per captioned voice payload** rather than by aggregate dispatcher counters:

- Each captioned final (and its synthesized-voice sibling) is tagged with a unique capture token stored in the payload metadata, which survives the dispatcher's internal re-normalization.
- Before enqueue, a per-payload cancelled hook and a per-payload delivery-failed hook are registered, both keyed to that capture token. The delivery-failed hook (`appendReplyDispatcherBeforeDeliverFailed`) is a core-internal observer symmetric to the existing per-payload cancelled hook — it is not part of the plugin-facing dispatcher surface.
- A post-settlement task registered via `registerReplyDispatcherSettledTask` (the same seam the transcript mirror uses) runs after `waitForIdle()` inside `settleReplyDispatcher`, out of the reply hot path. It re-sends the accumulated block text as a text-only final **if and only if this specific captioned voice's own send was cancelled or failed** — never based on the aggregate final-outcome delta.

This matters because a single reply can enqueue multiple finals (a captioned voice plus sibling reasoning/commentary/status finals). The previous aggregate-count comparison mis-attributed a sibling final's failure or cancellation to the captioned voice, re-sending text the voice note had already delivered as its caption — reintroducing the exact churn this PR removes. Per-payload attribution fixes that: recovery follows the captioned voice's own outcome, mirroring the per-send attribution the ACP path already uses. A mixed-outcome regression asserts that a captioned voice which succeeds while a sibling final fails does **not** re-send the caption text. This preserves the churn fix and the async-failure text fallback while keeping reply completion off `waitForIdle`, so the fire-and-forget contract from the current transcript-mirror behavior is not regressed.

### Cancelled final delivery (not just failed)

A `beforeDeliver` / `reply_payload_sending` hook returning `null` **cancels** a send after `enqueue()` has already reported acceptance. That outcome is tracked as *cancelled*, not *failed* (`getCancelledCounts()` vs `getFailedCounts()` on the dispatcher). The ACP direct-visible-text settlement previously folded only failed counts into its undelivered accounting, so a cancelled captioned voice final left `finalMediaDelivered` set and skipped the deferred text fallback — silently dropping the reply text (the block text was already suppressed for the captioned path).

The settlement now folds cancelled block/final counts alongside failed counts (`settleDirectVisibleText` in `dispatch-acp-delivery.ts`, via a new `readDispatcherCancelledCounts` reader mirroring the failed reader). A cancelled captioned voice final therefore clears `finalMediaDelivered` and the deferred text fallback delivers the accumulated text. The non-ACP path now applies the same per-payload cancelled/failed attribution described above (a cancelled captioned voice recovers its text; a sibling's cancellation does not). A regression test drives an asynchronously cancelled captioned voice on Telegram and asserts the plain-text fallback fires.

Closes #83511

target.title: feat(skills): capture reusable techniques from successful work
target.body:
Closes #105672

## What Problem This Solves

Opt-in Skill Workshop autonomy can capture explicit corrections, but reusable procedures discovered during long successful work are otherwise lost when the user did not phrase the result as a correction.

## Why This Change Was Made

When autonomous capture is enabled, successful foreground turns with at least ten model iterations may schedule a separate learning review after the run has finished and the whole agent system has remained idle for 30 seconds. The delayed review rechecks live autonomy, sandbox, agent, provider, sender, and conversation tool policy before it starts.

The reviewer is isolated to the exact resolved provider and model, reuses the auth profile when available, and disables model fallback. It runs on a dedicated background lane and receives a bounded rendering of only the current turn. Its Skill Workshop surface permits list/inspect plus at most one create or revise mutation; live-skill updates and proposal lifecycle actions are unavailable. Every generated result remains a pending proposal for human review.

The evidence bar is intentionally narrow: concrete struggle, correction, repeated failure, or a stable procedure expected to save at least two future model/tool round trips. Routine success, one-off facts, preferences, transient failures, secrets, generic advice, and uncertain cases must abstain.

## User Impact

Users who explicitly enable autonomous Skill Workshop capture can receive reviewable learning proposals after meaningful work without delaying foreground requests. The feature remains off by default, waits for idle state across embedded and reply-backed runs, bounds retained work, serializes learning reviews, and never applies a proposal automatically.

The new Self-learning guide documents enablement, eligibility, transcript and provider behavior, cost and privacy implications, proposal-only permissions, review commands, and troubleshooting. Skill Workshop, skills configuration, navigation, and the generated docs map link to that guide.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox [run 29221332451](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29221332451): 32 focused scheduler, Workshop, and lane tests passed; Oxlint reported zero findings; `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:core:test` passed.
- Blacksmith Testbox [run 29222289445](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29222289445): final scheduler suite passed after exact-model fail-closed pinning; Oxlint and both TypeScript lanes passed.
- Public-network AWS Crabbox run `run_07545709b518`: live OpenAI evaluation created exactly one pending proposal for a recovered deployment preflight and created no additional proposal for a routine one-off audit.

target.title: feat: add disableBoundaryAwareCache compat option for prefix-matching prompt cache providers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where DeepSeek OpenAI-compatible users lose provider prompt-cache hits after the 6.x boundary-aware cache split placed per-turn dynamic context ahead of the stable system prompt, so the large stable instruction block stopped caching and billed input tokens climbed.

Closes #94518

Related: #91018, #90583

## Why This Change Was Made

DeepSeek uses implicit prefix-matching cache, so its leading `system` message must stay byte-stable across turns for the stable instruction block to keep hitting cache. This PR adds `compat.disableBoundaryAwareCache`, auto-enables it for DeepSeek, keeps only the stable prefix in the `system` message, and emits the below-boundary runtime suffix as a trailing `system`-role carrier after the conversation history. That keeps the latest user message byte-identical (so it stays a reusable prefix once it becomes history) and keeps runtime/approval/identity guidance at system/developer authority instead of demoting it into user content.

Non-goal / honest limit: when the below-boundary context genuinely changes every turn, accumulated conversation history still cannot be cached — DeepSeek persists a cache prefix unit at the end of each request, so a trailing carrier that changes each turn ends every request on different bytes. No message re-ordering can cache history under that condition; this PR restores the stable-prefix cache, not moving full-history reuse.

Xiaomi is kept opt-in — users can set `compat.disableBoundaryAwareCache: true` manually, but the automatic default is DeepSeek-only until Xiaomi-specific upstream cache-contract and live-behavior evidence exists. Operators can opt back into boundary-aware behavior with `compat: { disableBoundaryAwareCache: false }`.

## User Impact

DeepSeek users keep the large stable system prompt cacheable from the first turn instead of losing it whenever below-boundary runtime context updates, which lowers billed input tokens on the cost regression #94518 reports. Behavior is unchanged for providers with native cache-control (Anthropic-style) and for sessions whose below-boundary content is already stable. Xiaomi and other providers are unaffected by default.

## Evidence

Focused unit tests (rebased on latest `origin/main`):

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.test.ts`: 44 passed, incl. system-only trailing-carrier and instruction-authority assertions
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/openai-transport-stream.test.ts`: 336 passed, incl. DeepSeek trailing-carrier and byte-stable-history assertions

Types: `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json` and `-p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json` clean for the touched files (unrelated `ui/**` `@codemirror` module-resolution noise only). Format: `oxfmt --check` clean.

### Live DeepSeek cache proof (baseline == current main vs PR)

Each turn's request is built by the **production** `buildOpenAICompletionsParams` and sent to the real DeepSeek API (`deepseek-v4-flash`); native `usage.prompt_cache_hit_tokens` / `prompt_cache_miss_tokens` are recorded across a growing 5-turn conversation. Scenario reproduces #94518: a large stable workspace prefix (`STABLE`, ~512 tokens) is constant, while the below-boundary runtime context changes each turn. **Baseline** keeps the suffix inside the leading `system` message (byte-identical to `origin/main`); **PR** keeps `system = STABLE` only and trails the suffix as a `system`-role carrier.

```text
                     BASELINE (== current main)     PR (this change)
turn 1 (cold):       hit=0     miss=936             hit=512   miss=424
turn 2:              hit=0     miss=1726            hit=512   miss=1214
turn 3:              hit=512   miss=2004            hit=512   miss=2004
turn 4:              hit=512   miss=2794            hit=512   miss=2794
turn 5:              hit=512   miss=3584            hit=512   miss=3584
```

Reading: on `main` the mutating `system` suffix breaks the prefix match from the first token, so the stable instruction block does **not** cache on cold turns (`hit=0` on turns 1–2; DeepSeek's automatic common-prefix detection only recovers `hit=512` from turn 3). With the PR the stable prefix is byte-stable and caches from turn 1 (`hit=512`), removing the cold-start miss on the ~512-token instruction block. Reproduced across two runs with fresh cold-start nonces; API key redacted. Payload dumps confirm the PR leaves the latest user message byte-identical and carries the suffix in a `system`-role message. Full data and the byte-stable-history / session-stable-parity cases are in the linked proof notes.

target.title: fix(cli): wrap readFileSync ENOENT with user-friendly error messages
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Three CLI code paths in `src/cli/` leak raw Node.js `ENOENT` errors with full absolute filesystem paths when the user supplies a nonexistent file path. This is noisy and exposes internal implementation details.

**Before (all three paths):**
```
Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/home/user/.openclaw/some/internal/path'
```

**After:**
```
Error: --batch-file not found: /nonexistent/path/batch.json5
Error: Secrets plan file not found: /tmp/missing-plan.json
Error: --file not found: /bad/patch.json5
```

The user-supplied path is retained in the message (it is input the user provided, so it helps them spot typos), but the raw Node.js error code and any derived internal paths are removed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Affected surfaces:

| File | User action | Error |
|------|-------------|-------|
| `src/cli/config-set-input.ts:139` | `openclaw config set --batch-file <bad-path>` | `ENOENT` raw error |
| `src/cli/secrets-cli.ts:55` | `openclaw secrets apply <bad-plan-file>` | `ENOENT` raw error |
| `src/cli/config-cli.ts:1497` | `openclaw config patch --file <bad-path>` | `ENOENT` raw error |

Each fix wraps `fs.readFileSync` / `readFileSync` in a try-catch that checks `(err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "ENOENT"` and throws a descriptive `Error` with the user-facing flag name and the original path. Non-ENOENT errors are re-thrown unchanged.

## User Impact

- Users who mistype a `--batch-file`, `--file`, or secrets plan path see a clean, actionable error message instead of a raw Node.js stack trace.
- No change to the success path or any other error path. Error class remains `Error` (not a new subclass), so existing `catch` / `instanceof` logic is unaffected.

## Evidence

- `src/cli/config-set-input.test.ts`: added test for nonexistent `--batch-file` → now 10/10 passing
- `src/cli/config-cli.integration.test.ts`: 5/5 passing (no regressions)
- `src/cli/secrets-cli.test.ts` + `src/cli/config-cli.test.ts`: 144/144 passing (no regressions)
- `oxfmt --check`: clean on all 4 touched files

target.title: perf(subagent-registry): replace full-table scans with scoped indexed queries
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `listSubagentRunsForController` hot path loads the **entire persisted subagent registry** (all rows from SQLite via `getSubagentRunsSnapshotForRead`) and performs synchronous `Array.filter()` scanning, blocking the event loop linearly with registry size. The SQLite schema already has `idx_subagent_runs_controller_session_key` but the store layer never uses it.

## What This PR Does

1. **Store layer** — Added `loadSubagentRunsForControllerFromSqlite`: a scoped Kysely query that uses the existing `idx_subagent_runs_controller_session_key` index with a compound predicate preserving the `controllerSessionKey || requesterSessionKey` fallback semantics. Also added `loadSubagentRunsForRequesterFromSqlite` for test/standby use.
2. **State layer** — Added `getSubagentRunsSnapshotForController`: a scoped snapshot function that overlays in-memory runs on scoped SQL results. **Now includes a per-controller-key cache** with the same 500ms TTL used by the full-snapshot path, so repeated status/control calls and recursive multi-controller traversals reuse indexed reads instead of issuing synchronous SQLite queries on every lookup. Cache entries are invalidated on `persistSubagentRunsToDisk`.
3. **Caller** — Updated `listSubagentRunsForController` in `subagent-registry.ts` and `subagent-registry-read.ts` to use the scoped snapshot. The `listSubagentRunsForRequester` path is **unchanged**.
4. **Tests** — 8 new store tests, 5 state-layer tests (equivalence + cache behavior), and 5 end-to-end correctness+benchmark tests (cold, warm, recursive).

No schema migration required — all needed indexes already exist.

## Evidence

### Benchmark results (10K records, ext4 SSD, Windows x64)

```
=== Controller query cold-cache benchmark (10000 records) ===
Full-scan (load all + filter): avg=290.75ms
Scoped   (indexed query):      avg=2.14ms
Cold-cache speedup: 136.1x

=== Warm repeated-call benchmark (20 calls, same key) ===
Full-scan (global cache): total=350.50ms avg=17.52ms
Scoped   (per-key cache): total=11.18ms avg=0.56ms
Warm speedup: 31.3x

=== Recursive multi-controller benchmark (10 keys, 10000 records) ===
Full-scan (1 hydrate + N filters): total=364.54ms avg=36.45ms
Scoped   (N indexed + cache):      total=99.03ms avg=9.90ms
Recursive speedup: 3.7x
```

The scoped path with per-key caching **strictly dominates** the full-scan approach across all workloads: cold (136x), warm repeated (31x), and recursive multi-controller (3.7x).

### Benchmark reproducer

```bash
pnpm vitest run src/agents/subagent-registry-scoped.bench.test.ts
```

### Correctness

- Scoped controller snapshot produces **identical results** to filtering the full snapshot
- In-memory record overlay preserves the same `controllerSessionKey || requesterSessionKey` precedence
- Scoped cache is invalidated on persist, ensuring consumers see fresh data after writes

### Tests

```bash
pnpm test src/agents/subagent-registry-state.test.ts
pnpm test src/agents/subagent-registry.store.sqlite.test.ts
pnpm test src/agents/subagent-registry.test.ts
pnpm test src/agents/subagent-registry-scoped.bench.test.ts
pnpm test src/agents/subagent-registry-read-context.test.ts
pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/commands-subagents-status.test.ts
```

**268/268 passing, 0 failures, 0 regressions.**

### Files changed (8 files, +806/-5)

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/agents/subagent-registry.store.sqlite.ts` | +71: 2 scoped query functions |
| `src/agents/subagent-registry-state.ts` | +133: 2 scoped snapshot functions + per-key cache |
| `src/agents/subagent-registry.ts` | +10/-4: DI surface + controller caller |
| `src/agents/subagent-registry-read.ts` | +7/-1: controller caller |
| `src/agents/subagent-registry.store.sqlite.test.ts` | +131: 8 store test cases |
| `src/agents/subagent-registry-state.test.ts` | +144: 5 equivalence + cache tests |
| `src/agents/subagent-registry.test.ts` | +12/-19: mock surface update |
| `src/agents/subagent-registry-scoped.bench.test.ts` | +305: 5 e2e benchmarks (new file) |

# PR4/5 — controls/inspection + CLI/Gateway

## Context capsule

This PR is item 4 of the rebuilt beta3 durable core stack. It exposes the wake inspection/control surface after the PR3 wake/replay foundation reached reviewer threshold.

## Durable core stack overview

- PR1/5 — docs/RFC/boundary anchor.
- PR2/5 — runtime foundation/core plus terminal SQLite row immutability guard.
- PR3/5 — wake targets, durable producers, replay/resume semantics.
- PR4/5 — controls/inspection plus CLI/Gateway surface.
- PR5/5 — internal session delivery handoff, final hardening, and cumulative proof.

## Stack position

- Stack item: PR4/5
- Current PR summary: Wake inspection/control store APIs, durable CLI commands, Gateway protocol/server methods and tests.
- Does not claim: No internal delivery/startup/worker handoff and no external transport delivery claim.
- Dependency/base: PR3 head `4f774fd5cc3cfc9b18c19ea891dd1358db80c8c9` (`openclaw/openclaw#105660`)
- This PR head: `bacf5c96acd2972eaad83f4d01d297dea57b06f5`

## What Problem This Solves

PR3 persists durable wake obligations and delivery attempts, but operators still need a bounded way to inspect, acknowledge, supersede, and mark those wake records. This slice adds that control surface in the durable store, CLI, and Gateway protocol without claiming delivery transport behavior.

## Scope

- Durable wake inspection/control store APIs for acknowledge, supersede, mark decision-required, inspect wakes, and list delivery attempts.
- Durable CLI commands: `wakes`, `wake`, `wake-attempts`, `wake-ack`, `wake-supersede`, and `wake-mark`.
- Gateway protocol schemas/validators and server methods for durable wake inspection/control.
- Focused tests for store, CLI, Gateway server methods, and Gateway protocol shape.

## Non-scope

- No `src/durable/wake-internal-delivery.ts`.
- No durable worker/internal session delivery handoff.
- No external transport delivery claim.
- No plugin SDK DTS fix.

## Base / diff hygiene

- Base comparison: `4f774fd5cc3cfc9b18c19ea891dd1358db80c8c9..bacf5c96acd2972eaad83f4d01d297dea57b06f5`

After hosted `checks-fast-bundled-protocol` exposed generated Swift protocol drift, regenerated and included `apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawProtocol/GatewayModels.swift`.

target.title: fix(agents): bound compaction planning worker payloads
target.body:
Addresses #100635

## What Problem This Solves

Compaction planning sanitizes private fields before worker handoff, but previously still sent full model-visible tool-result text and base64 image data through `workerData`. Large browser/command results or multimodal transcripts could therefore force multi-megabyte structured-clone work before summary-prompt truncation had a chance to help.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a planning-only projection before worker handoff:

- oversized tool-result text/content keeps a bounded UTF-16-safe sample plus omitted-character accounting;
- image blocks in user, custom, and tool-result content keep their type/MIME metadata but omit base64 bytes;
- token-pressure accounting remains conservative, so chunking and pruning decisions still reflect the original payload;
- local fallback behavior and private-field sanitization remain unchanged.

Image bytes are not used by compaction's text serializer, while image token pressure is a fixed per-block estimate. Omitting only `data` therefore reduces worker cloning without changing summary text or planning pressure. The pure projection helper is split from worker orchestration so both implementation files remain below the repository's 500-line guard (476 and 109 lines).

## User Impact

Long or multimodal sessions should spend less time and memory cloning redundant payloads into the compaction planning worker, reducing event-loop stall and OOM risk without changing compaction decisions or generated summary text.

## Evidence

- Final `upstream/main` rebase: `ef9383d88ab85207f225440bef6957c7f73c87a6`; branch HEAD: `2bcaea67c8141199f1ac1726265fc5c262ee2475`.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/compaction.token-sanitize.test.ts packages/agent-core/src/harness/compaction/compaction.test.ts packages/agent-core/src/harness/compaction/compaction-image-tokens.test.ts`: 13 tests passed across 3 files on the final rebased HEAD.
- `pnpm check:loc --base-ref upstream/main`: passed; implementation files are 476 and 109 lines.
- Changed-file `oxlint` and `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD`: passed.
- Core production typecheck passed locally. The same code also passed the repository build and CI `build-artifacts` lane before the final baseline-only rebase.
- Independent `codex review --uncommitted`: no correctness findings after fixing the user-image coverage gap it identified.
- Text projection microbenchmark:
  - 1 x 120k-char tool result: `120,134` -> `8,436` bytes (`92.98%` reduction), token estimate `30,000` -> `30,001`.
  - 65 x 40k-char tool results: `2,608,758` -> `548,258` bytes (`78.98%` reduction), token estimate `650,000` -> `650,065`.
- Packaged-worker image smoke using `dist/agents/compaction-planning.worker.js` with one 1 MB user image and one 1 MB tool-result image in a 64-message request:
  - worker input: `2,251,077` -> `251,167` bytes (`88.8424%` reduction; `1,999,910` bytes removed);
  - token estimate: `2,405` -> `2,405`;
  - serialized summary input: identical;
  - worker result: `ok`.

AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed the compaction planning and worker handoff paths, checked duplicate/open PR state for #100635, and independently reviewed and validated the final branch locally.

Signed-off-by: Ho Lim <subhoya@gmail.com>

target.title: fix: prevent silent message loss from EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError
target.body:
## Summary

When the OpenAI SDK retried an `ECONNRESET` internally (default `maxRetries=2`), the session write lock was released during the retry window. Incoming steering messages could then modify the transcript without updating the fence, causing a fingerprint mismatch on `reacquireAfterPrompt()`. The resulting `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError` was caught by `model-fallback.ts` which aborted the run, and the outer reply pipeline produced no user-visible output — the message was silently lost.

## Root Cause Chain

```
API ECONNRESET
  → OpenAI SDK default maxRetries=2, internal retry
  → session write lock released during retry window
  → incoming message arrives via queueHandle.queueMessage
  → activeSession.steer writes directly (bypassing withOwnedSessionTranscriptWrites)
  → transcript changes without updating fence
  → original attempt reacquireAfterPrompt() fingerprint mismatch
  → EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError thrown
  → model-fallback.ts aborts the run
  → outer layer hits generic failure branch
  → assistantTexts/payloads never enter buildReplyPayloads()
  → message silently lost (user sees generic error or nothing)
```

## Fix

Seven coordinated changes that address the bug at multiple layers:

### 1. Wrap steering in `withOwnedSessionTranscriptWrites` (`attempt.ts`)
Steering writes that arrive during prompt lock release now go through `withOwnedSessionTranscriptWrites`, keeping fence tracking consistent and preventing the fingerprint mismatch that triggers the takeover error.

### 2. Dedicated error handler for takeover (`agent-runner-execution.ts`, `failover-error.ts`)
Added `isEmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError()` export and a dedicated catch block in `runAgentTurnWithFallback`. Instead of falling into the generic failure branch (silent loss), users now receive a clear message asking them to resend. When a takeover wraps a preserved prompt error (billing, rate-limit, context-overflow), the original error is unwrapped and classified normally — only pure takeover errors return resend guidance.

### 3. Pin SDK retries to 0 inside the embedded prompt lock window (`attempt.ts`, `attempt.session-lock.ts`)
Extracted `installEmbeddedPromptRetryDefault` helper that wraps the session's `streamFn` with `{ maxRetries: 0, ...options }`. The in-window default is **unconditionally 0** — the configured `settings.retry.provider.maxRetries` is deliberately NOT injected here, because the prompt-lock window releases the session lock across the model call and an in-window SDK retry would run against a released lock and re-admit the session-takeover race (#87180). An explicit per-call `maxRetries` still overrides (spread last). Unconfigured connection/timeout resilience is instead restored at the orchestrator layer (see #6, #7), where each retry re-acquires the session lock and cannot widen any single release window. Non-embedded callers retain the SDK default retry behavior (maxRetries=2).

### 4. Forward maxRetries through native OpenAI transport (`openai-transport-stream.ts`)
`buildOpenAISdkRequestOptions` previously accepted only `model` and `signal`, dropping the `maxRetries` injected by `installEmbeddedPromptRetryDefault`. Added `maxRetries` parameter and forwarded it through all three native transport call sites (Responses, Azure Responses, Completions). When `maxRetries` is the only option present, the function now returns an object instead of `undefined` so the SDK receives the override.

### 5. Phase tracking in `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError` (`attempt.session-lock.ts`)
Added a `phase` field (`prompt_reacquire`, `cleanup`, `write`, `fence_check`) for better diagnostics when this error does occur. Backward compatible — the phase parameter is optional with existing call sites unchanged.

### 6. Restore unconfigured connection-error retry at the orchestrator layer (`agent-runner-execution.ts`, `embedded-agent-helpers/errors.ts`)
Disabling SDK retries inside the prompt-lock release window (#3) is required so an in-window retry cannot widen the takeover race — but for users who have **not** configured `settings.retry.provider.maxRetries`, it also dropped the SDK's default retry of bare connection errors (`ECONNRESET`, `socket hang up`, `Connection error.`) that carry no leading HTTP status. This is restored at the orchestrator layer, where the existing one-shot `consumeTransientHttpRetry()` re-runs the full primary→fallback cycle and **re-acquires the session lock per attempt**, so it does not widen any single release window. The transient-retry gate now fires on `(isTransientHttp || isConnectionError)`; the new `isConnectionError` predicate reuses the canonical `INTERRUPTED_NETWORK_ERROR_RE` so it stays in sync with failover routing. In-window `maxRetries:0` is unchanged. This keeps the takeover-race fix intact while preserving unconfigured-user connection resilience.

### 7. Restore unconfigured request-timeout retry at the orchestrator layer (`agent-runner-execution.ts`)
The orchestrator transient-retry restore in #6 left a symmetric gap: in addition to bare connection errors, the OpenAI/Anthropic SDKs retry request-**timeout** transport errors by default, and after the in-window `maxRetries:0`, an unconfigured single-model user's timeout error is rethrown to the same outer gate — which only matched HTTP-status transients and connection errors, dropping timeout retry entirely (multi-model users were unaffected because failover already routes timeouts). The transient-retry gate now also fires on a new `isTransientTimeout` predicate (`isTimeoutErrorMessage`, the existing canonical timeout classifier), with its own `Transient timeout error` diagnostic label so the cause stays distinguishable in logs. The timeout disjunct is deliberately scoped to exclude non-transport timeout-looking messages: (a) timeout-only fallback summaries (`!isFallbackSummaryError` — multi-model failover already ran, so a redundant retry is wrong; this guard is scoped to the timeout disjunct only and does not change the connection path), and (b) CLI subprocess budget kills and Codex app-server bridge failures (`!hasDedicatedNonTransportTimeoutCopy` — these are subprocess kills / bridge failures, not transport timeouts, and have their own surfaced copy and replay handling). The one-shot `consumeTransientHttpRetry()` budget is shared, so timeout retry is bounded exactly like the connection retry. The connection-retry path semantics from #6 are unchanged. The timeout disjunct additionally excludes local non-provider runtime coordination errors (e.g. `SessionWriteLockTimeoutError`, whose message reads as `session file locked (timeout ...ms)`) via the canonical `isNonProviderRuntimeCoordinationError` classifier: retrying any model would hit the same local condition, so these abort the fallback chain rather than re-run as a transport timeout.

## Real behavior proof

> **Refreshed at current head `4afcd490cb` for the approved P1 fix: the embedded prompt-lock-window SDK retry default is now pinned to 0 unconditionally (the configured-provider-retry injection at the in-lock call site was removed, and the helper no longer accepts a configurable default). Unconfigured connection/timeout resilience remains at the orchestrator layer (#6, #7), which re-acquires the session lock per attempt and cannot widen the release window. Supersedes the earlier blocks below.**

- **Behavior addressed**: A configured provider `maxRetries>0` was being injected as the SDK default for calls made inside the embedded prompt lock window. Because that window releases the session lock across the model call, an in-window SDK retry runs against a released lock and re-admits the #87180 session-takeover / silent-message-loss race. The in-window SDK retry default is now unconditionally 0; only an explicit per-call `maxRetries` overrides it. The now-dead configurable-default ref machinery was removed. This aligns the code with the invariant already documented at `embedded-agent-helpers/errors.ts` ("the embedded prompt-lock window pins SDK maxRetries to 0").
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched checkout at `4afcd490cb`, macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`.
- **Exact steps run after this patch**: Ran the affected suites at this head with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <suite>`: the in-window session-lock retry suite `attempt.session-lock.test.ts`, and the organic real-setup session-takeover regression (real on-disk session + real local HTTP model server + real OpenAI-completions transport + real prompt-lock fence).
- **Observed result**: the in-window streamFn default is a hard `maxRetries:0` with no configurable path; an explicit per-call `maxRetries` still overrides (spread last); the organic takeover still surfaces cause-neutral resend guidance.
- **Evidence after fix** (current-head terminal output):
```

Commit: 4afcd490cb857cff2e62e68760c838f969f81b30

--- A: In-window SDK retries pinned to 0 unconditionally (approved P1 fix) ---
 ✓  agents  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.session-lock.test.ts (126 tests)
   asserts the embedded prompt-lock window streamFn default is maxRetries:0 with no configurable path,
   and an explicit per-call maxRetries still overrides (spread last)

--- B: Organic real-setup session-takeover proof (real on-disk session + real local HTTP model server + real OpenAI-completions transport + real prompt-lock fence) ---
```

- **What was not tested**: The exact live production timing race is not replayed end-to-end; the strongest proof remains the deterministic in-window retry-pinning coverage plus the local HTTP + on-disk session organic takeover regression above.

### Earlier proof (head `c21d0bc1a2`)

> **Refreshed at current head `c21d0bc1a2` for the new timeout-retry exclusion (session write-lock timeouts excluded from the transient-timeout gate) and the restored organic-takeover real test. Supersedes the earlier blocks below.**

- **Behavior addressed**: The transient-timeout retry restore (Fix #7) used `isTimeoutErrorMessage`, which also matches local `SessionWriteLockTimeoutError` messages (`session file locked (timeout ...ms): ...`). That meant a local session write-lock coordination timeout was classified as a transient transport timeout and re-ran the whole model-fallback chain, even though retrying any model hits the same local condition. The timeout disjunct now excludes non-provider runtime coordination errors via the canonical `isNonProviderRuntimeCoordinationError` classifier — the same seam `model-fallback.ts` already uses to abort the chain on coordination errors. The connection/HTTP disjuncts are unchanged.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched checkout at `c21d0bc1a2`, macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, deps installed with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`.
- **Exact steps run after this patch**: Ran the affected suites at this head with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <suite>`: the new session-write-lock-timeout exclusion regression in `agent-runner-execution.test.ts`, and the organic real-setup session-takeover regression (real on-disk session + real local HTTP model server + real OpenAI-completions transport + real prompt-lock fence). The real-setup test depends on the `embedded-agent-helpers` mock exporting `isConnectionError`/`isTimeoutErrorMessage` (called eagerly on the catch path); those exports were missing, so this run also restores them so the test imports and runs to its assertion.
- **Observed result**: a session-write-lock-shaped timeout error now terminates as `run_failed` and is NOT re-run through the fallback chain (`runWithModelFallback` called exactly once); the organic takeover still surfaces cause-neutral resend guidance. The exclusion is proven non-tautological: removing the `!isNonProviderRuntimeCoordinationError(err)` clause makes the regression fail with the mock called twice.


**Mechanism (deterministic Promise handshakes, no sleeps):**
1. A real temp session file is created with one session line.
2. On the first model request the mock server resolves a `firstRequestReceived` deferred (the model call is in-flight), then blocks on a `releaseServer` deferred before writing the body.

6. The fingerprint mismatch trips the fence → `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError` thrown organically → real classification → real `runAgentTurnWithFallback` catch.

target.title: refactor: use semver package for version ordering
target.body:
Closes #105938

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where update and plugin-install decisions relied on several independent version comparators, making prerelease, correction-release, and malformed-version ordering easier to implement inconsistently across workflows.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use `semver` 7.8.5 for standard parsing, comparison, coercion, and prerelease detection at the root and in plugins that import it directly. Keep OpenClaw's shipped numeric correction-release policy and legacy `x.y.z.beta.N` normalization as explicit layers around standard SemVer.

## User Impact

Users and plugin operators get consistent version ordering across update checks, update channels, compatibility ranges, installs, updates, QA staging, and Codex app-server compatibility checks. No configuration or supported release shape changes.

## Evidence

- Exact-head Blacksmith Testbox at `227491abfb1`: 457 focused tests passed across infra, config, plugin install/update, Codex, and QA surfaces ([run 29225801519](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29225801519)).
- Requested broad `pnpm test src/infra src/plugins`: all infra and touched plugin tests passed; the earlier unrelated current-main guardrail drift was repaired upstream.
- Exact-head `pnpm check:loc --base-ref origin/main`: passed ([run 29225894117](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29225894117)). Earlier unrelated QA-lab and iMessage type drifts were repaired upstream by #105983 and #106022.
- Remote `pnpm build`: passed.
- Fresh xhigh autoreview: no accepted/actionable findings; patch correct at 0.98 confidence.
- AI-assisted implementation and review; maintainer-authored change.

target.title: feat(nodes): continue Claude catalog sessions on paired nodes via streaming CLI agent runs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Claude Code catalog sessions on paired nodes were view-only: `continueClaudeSession` rejected any `hostId` other than `gateway:local`, so a session whose files live on another machine could be browsed but never continued. Closes #105529.

## Why This Change Was Made

Continuing a Claude session must run the real `claude` CLI on the machine that owns the session files (its `~/.claude`, its auth) — OpenClaw stays a frontend and never substitutes its own inference. This PR ships the full TS stack for that, opt-in and approval-gated end to end:

- **Streaming node invoke (additive transport)**: new `node.invoke.progress` events (`{invokeId, nodeId, seq, chunk}`) with strict seq ordering, bounded out-of-order buffering, idle-timeout reset on progress, hard-cap timeout, and `node.invoke.cancel`. Legacy single-result invokes stay byte-identical (cancel frames are gated to streaming invokes). Progress handlers are node-scoped and bind invokeId to the owning node's connection — no cross-node injection.
- **Node command `agent.cli.claude.run.v1`** (TS node host): advertised only when the node-local config `nodeHost.agentRuns.claude.enabled` is true AND the `claude` binary resolves on the node — the gateway can never force it on. Requests are validated against a strict Claude flag allowlist (`bypassPermissions` rejected in both arg forms), env passthrough is allowlisted, cwd must exist, and every run flows through the existing `system.run` exec-approval policy with the exact validated argv. Output is capped (200KB, 16KB chunks with backpressure), stderr tailed, process tree SIGKILLed on cancel/timeout, and the system prompt is materialized in a node-local 0600 temp file that is always cleaned up.
- **cli-runner placement branch**: sessions with `execHost === "node"` run one-shot `claude -p` turns through the streaming invoke, feeding the same JSONL parser as local runs (session-id capture, fork markers, tool events unchanged). Warm stdio, gateway-loopback MCP, skills dirs, reseed-from-transcript, and attachments are cleanly disabled for node runs (rejected or omitted, double-enforced by the node-side allowlist); local runs are byte-identical.
- **Catalog wiring**: node rows become continuable when the node advertises the run command AND the gateway's node command policy permits it (deny-wins, enforced at projection, continue, and invoke time). Adoption re-resolves the record from the node itself (client-supplied paths never trusted), imports bounded history via the existing read command, and binds the session with `execNode`/`execCwd` through the trusted creation seam. First-turn `--fork-session` semantics identical to local adoption.

Mac-app (Swift) nodes simply never advertise the command and remain view-only until the app ships it.

## User Impact

With a headless node host opted in (`nodeHost.agentRuns.claude.enabled: true` + `claude` installed), Claude Code sessions on that machine appear in the session catalog and can be continued like native sessions: each turn runs on the node with the node's Claude auth and settings, streams output live, and respects the node's exec approval policy. Nothing changes for nodes that do not opt in; existing node/gateway deployments see zero wire-format changes.

## Evidence

- Focused matrix green post-rebase (8 Vitest shards): node-registry transport ordering/idle/disconnect, node-host argv-validation/approval/caps/cancel, cli-runner placement/JSONL-across-chunks/fork/deadline-during-approval, config contract, plugin runtime projection, catalog adoption/rejection paths.
- Codex-side validation on Linux Testbox: 12 test files (574 executions), `check:changed` (12m21s), `pnpm build` — all green pre-review.
- Three independent deep reviews (transport, cli-runner placement, catalog/config/plugin seams): all SOLID, zero P1s. The one P2 (hard-timeout previously emitted `node.invoke.cancel` for legacy invokes too) is fixed — cancel frames now gate on the streaming contract.
- Per-commit autoreview (gpt-5.6-sol xhigh) surfaced five findings, all fixed with regression tests: buffered progress no longer drains after cancellation; duplicate buffered seq frames no longer reset the idle deadline; node runs now carry the gateway's native tool policy (`--tools` + MCP deny projected; `--allowedTools` auto-approval still never crosses the node boundary); fresh node CLI sessions reseed conversation history from the gateway-side transcript; and a truncated node stream that lost the terminal result line now fails the turn instead of passing as a clean exit.
- SDK gates: `plugin-sdk:api:check` and `plugin-sdk:surface:check` green (surface budget +1 for `resolveChildProcessInvocation`, now public via the `process-runtime` wildcard — needed by the node host for Windows shim-correct spawns).
- tsgo core + UI lanes green; oxlint/oxfmt/`git diff --check` clean.

Known follow-ups (deliberate v1 scope, in the tracking issue): Mac-app Swift command, warm stdio on nodes, gateway-loopback MCP over node transport, Codex app-server on nodes, approval-request withdrawal when a run aborts mid-wait, FailoverError classification for node disconnects.

target.title: fix(ios): block omitted share attachments
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #103363.

The iOS Share Extension accepted at most three image attachments and ignored videos, files, PDFs, and unknown attachment providers while still moving toward the normal send flow. That let a user share partial content without any visible explanation.

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps the current gateway media contract unchanged: the share route still sends image attachments only, and it does not attempt to add video/PDF/file transport in this PR.

Instead, extraction now records selected image count, accepted image count, and unsupported attachment classes. If the extension would omit selected content, the compose card enters the existing blocked state with a concrete recovery message, so send stays disabled until the user removes omitted items and shares again.

## User Impact

- Sharing 6 images now shows: `Only 3 of 6 images can be sent. Remove omitted items and share again.`
- Sharing a video, PDF/file, or unknown attachment now shows an unsupported-item message instead of silently sending only text or the first accepted images.
- Normal shares with up to 3 images are unchanged.

## Evidence

Focused local proof:

```text
SHARE_ATTACHMENT_SUMMARY_PROOF=PASS
Only 3 of 6 images can be sent. Remove omitted items and share again.
OpenClaw Share cannot send 1 video(s), 2 file(s), 1 unsupported item(s) yet. Remove omitted items and share again.
```

Validation run:

```text
swiftc /tmp/.../ShareAttachmentSummary.swift /tmp/.../main.swift -o /tmp/.../share-proof && /tmp/.../share-proof
git diff HEAD^ HEAD --check
```

### Real proof

Exact-head native simulator proof for `5dda9040ac66350805428609bca660dd5373e6f6`.

Environment: iPhone 17 Pro simulator, iOS 26.2 (`23C54`), Xcode 27.0. The installed app's `OpenClawGitCommit` is the exact PR head above. Both scenarios used the real Photos → Share Sheet → OpenClaw Share Extension path.

#### Six-image omission path

- Selected 6 photos in Photos.
- The extension rendered: `Only 3 of 6 images can be sent. Remove omitted items and share again.`
- Send was disabled.
- After entering `Compare all six images`, Send remained disabled.
- XCTest result: **Passed** (`39.91s`).

![Six selected images show the omission warning with Send disabled](https://files.catbox.moe/91crio.png)

#### Normal one-image control

- Selected 1 photo in Photos.
- After entering `Describe this image`, Send enabled normally.
- XCTest result: **Passed** (`27.65s`).

![A normal one-image share enables Send after draft text is entered](https://files.catbox.moe/1vcxn8.png)

Focused commands:

```text
xcodebuild ... -only-testing:OpenClawUITests/ShareExtensionUITests/testSixSelectedImagesShowOmissionWarningAndKeepSendDisabled test
xcodebuild ... -only-testing:OpenClawUITests/ShareExtensionUITests/testOneSelectedImageStillEnablesSendAfterDraftText test
```

The UI-test additions were a local proof harness only; no test or product files were pushed to the contributor branch.

Source proof comment: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104842#issuecomment-4953546708

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users saving URL-backed node camera, photo, or clip media could accept a malformed `Content-Length` response header and continue as though no size header was present.

## Why This Change Was Made

The node media URL download boundary now parses `Content-Length` with the shared strict media parser before reading the response body, and cancels rejected response bodies on malformed headers. This keeps the change inside the node-hosted media download path used by camera CLI commands and agent node media actions without changing valid downloads, config, provider behavior, schemas, or public APIs.

## User Impact

Malformed node-hosted media responses are rejected before the payload is copied to disk, while valid URL-backed camera media continues to use the existing size limits and stream guard.

target.title: fix(ollama): resolve web search secret refs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Ollama web search did not resolve env-backed SecretRefs configured at `models.providers.ollama.apiKey`. Treating an explicitly configured but unavailable SecretRef as no configuration could also select an unrelated ambient `OLLAMA_API_KEY` and route the query to Ollama Cloud.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Ollama runtime now delegates literal and env-backed SecretRef resolution to the existing shared `resolveWebSearchProviderCredential(...)` helper. The plugin separately preserves whether the configured input was a SecretRef, so a missing or unsupported ref fails before any request without expanding the Plugin SDK. Literal configured keys and the independent ambient cloud key remain separate, preserving the selected-host attempts plus authenticated cloud fallback used by mixed setups.

## User Impact

Users can configure an env SecretRef for the Ollama provider key and have the resolved value sent on web-search requests. Missing or non-env SecretRefs fail before `fetchWithSsrFGuard` instead of silently using an unrelated ambient key. Existing marker-string fallback to `OLLAMA_API_KEY` and mixed configured-key/ambient-key cloud fallback remain covered.

## Evidence

- Current PR diff is limited to `extensions/ollama/src/web-search-provider.ts` and `extensions/ollama/src/web-search-provider.test.ts`; Plugin SDK, core credential helper, packages, and generated API baseline have zero diff.
- The configured-ref path calls the shared resolver, uses the public `coerceSecretRef(...)` contract to retain explicit-ref state, and rejects an unavailable ref before request construction.
- Focused tests cover resolved env refs, missing env refs with an ambient key present, unsupported non-env refs, mixed literal configured and ambient keys, and marker-string fallback.

## Proof

- Exact local commit `a6e84b3ec6f6693949514e710892b60257a5278c`:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/ollama/src/web-search-provider.test.ts -- --reporter=dot` passed: 1 file, 19 tests.

target.title: fix(compaction): count CJK text in token estimates
target.body:
Closes #103930

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where CJK-heavy sessions retain far more recent conversation than `keepRecentTokens` intends after compaction. The cut-point estimator treated CJK text as four characters per token, so Chinese, Japanese, and Korean content could be retained at roughly three to four times the configured token budget.

## Why This Change Was Made

The compaction estimator now uses the repository's existing CJK-aware character accounting for every textual message shape. That helper now lives in `@openclaw/normalization-core`, which both the root runtime and standalone `agent-core` can import without duplicating Unicode-range behavior; the existing root module remains a compatibility re-export.

## User Impact

CJK-heavy conversations now compact to approximately the same retained-token budget as equivalent ASCII conversations. ASCII estimates and image accounting are unchanged.

## Evidence

Before: the unmodified production estimator returned 40 estimated tokens for 160 CJK characters—the same result as 160 ASCII characters—and selected cut point index 1 for four such messages with a 100-token budget.

After, driving the real exported production functions on this branch:

```console
$ node --import tsx --input-type=module …
{"cjkTokens":160,"extensionBTokens":160,"cutPoint":3}
```

AI-assisted: this PR was prepared with Codex and reviewed with Claude.

## What Problem This Solves

The core misrouting from #97055 — custom Ollama memory providers (`ollama-cpu`, `ollama-gpu`, …) being collapsed onto the default `ollama` provider — has already landed on `main` via fa5f24b021e (adapter-side provider-id resolution) and b085184d085 (gateway-side provider-id propagation). This PR has been slimmed down to the remaining gap: the Ollama memory adapter's embedding cache identity is still only `{provider, model, outputDimensionality}`. Two configurations that reuse the same provider id but point at different endpoints (different `baseUrl`, or different non-secret custom headers selecting a different tenant/backend) hash to the same memory provider key and silently reuse stale cached embeddings from the other endpoint.

## Why This Change Was Made

The lmstudio memory adapter already keys its cache by `{provider, baseUrl, model, headers: sanitizeEmbeddingCacheHeaders(...)}`; the Ollama adapter now mirrors that pattern exactly (keeping its existing `outputDimensionality` field), so endpoint identity participates in the cache key consistently across local-server adapters.

**Secret-header hardening:** because `cacheKeyData` is hashed into the memory provider key, a credential header in it would force a full reindex on every credential rotation. `sanitizeEmbeddingCacheHeaders` in `memory-host-sdk` now always drops sensitive header names (`authorization`, `proxy-authorization`, and anything containing `api-key`/`token`/`secret`) for every adapter, and `excludedHeaderNames` becomes optional. Secret headers are still sent on the wire — only the cache identity excludes them.

## User Impact

- Users running multiple Ollama endpoints under distinct provider ids (or re-pointing one id at a new `baseUrl`) get correct, endpoint-scoped embedding caches instead of silent stale reuse.
- Rotating a credential header no longer churns the memory index, for any embedding adapter.
- **Compatibility note (maintainer acceptance item):** adding `baseUrl`/`headers` to the Ollama cache identity changes the provider-key hash for existing Ollama memory indexes (including the default `ollama` provider), so they rebuild once via the normal memory index rebuild flow on upgrade. This is intentional — it is required to distinguish endpoints, and memory indexes are rebuildable.

## Evidence

Red-green regression proof — the branch's own test file run on both sides:

**Green (this branch @ `850ea819308`):** `CI=true pnpm test extensions/ollama/src/embedding-provider.test.ts` — all tests pass (31 including the google adapter suite exercising the hardened helper, which passes unchanged — the hardening is behavior-preserving for adapters already excluding their credential headers).

**Red (`origin/main` @ `e43bd3d57bc`, with only the test file copied over):**
```
FAIL  ollama embedding provider > includes outputDimensionality in the memory embedding cache identity
AssertionError: expected { provider: 'ollama', …(2) } to match object { provider: 'ollama', …(3) }
FAIL  ollama embedding provider > preserves custom provider endpoint identity in the memory adapter
AssertionError: expected { provider: 'ollama-cpu', …(2) } to match object { provider: 'ollama-cpu', …(3) }
FAIL  ollama embedding provider > excludes secret custom headers from the memory cache identity
```
-> main's cache identity has no `baseUrl`/`headers`, so same-id endpoint changes silently reuse stale embeddings; this branch keys them apart.

`CI=true pnpm tsgo:core` and `CI=true pnpm tsgo:extensions` are clean.

## What Problem This Solves

Closes #80582.

Short-term memory promotion could treat markdown and QMD scaffolding as durable content. That included empty list/checklist/fence/table fragments, placeholder daily-note headings, generic daily/dreaming headings, QMD hunk wrappers, collapsed persisted heading prefixes, and mixed snippets that carried structural text alongside real content.

The fix centralizes short-term snippet promotability in the promotion resolver and applies that resolver across recall recording, store normalization, grounded candidates, ranking, relocation/rehydration, and direct promotion application.

target.title: fix(agents): prevent duplicate subagent recovery after restart
target.body:
Closes #103724

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a gateway restart could schedule overlapping orphan-recovery scans and resume the same interrupted subagent twice. Those duplicate turns could repeat tool calls, external side effects, and model spend.

## Why This Change Was Made

The recovery scheduler now owns one retry chain at a time and coalesces overlapping requests into one follow-up scan. This preserves recovery requests raised while a scan is active without allowing independent scans to dispatch the same orphan concurrently.

The regression parks the first gateway resume, schedules a second recovery request, and verifies that only one resume is dispatched before the first completes and that the queued follow-up observes the cleared restart marker.

## User Impact

Interrupted subagents are resumed at most once across overlapping restart-time recovery triggers, avoiding duplicate work and side effects while retaining a follow-up pass for newly discovered orphaned work.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(cron): avoid ambiguous direct delivery retries
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102367.

Cron direct delivery bypasses the durable outbound queue with `skipQueue: true`, but its local retry classifier still retried ambiguous transport errors such as `ECONNRESET` and generic gateway timeouts. Those errors can happen after Slack accepts or finalizes a message, so a retry can post the same scheduled announcement twice.

## Why This Change Was Made

The direct cron retry path now reuses the outbound recovery proof predicate and retries only failures that prove no recipient-visible send happened, such as `PlatformMessageNotDispatchedError` or pre-connect network failures. Ambiguous send/finalization failures remain terminal for that cron delivery attempt, and mixed-payload batches stop retrying once any earlier payload may have reached the recipient, including `adapter_returned_no_identity` outcomes where the adapter was invoked but no durable message id came back.

## User Impact

Scheduled Slack deliveries no longer retry ambiguous post-send transport failures that may already have delivered the message. Proven-not-sent failures still retry, preserving recovery for safe pre-dispatch failures.

target.title: fix(gateway): count pending restarts toward maxRestartsPerHour budget
target.body:
### What Problem This Solves
close #105189
When a channel is permanently stuck in a pending restart state, two issues arise:

1. **Budget bypass**: The health monitor skips the maxRestartsPerHour check for pending restarts, causing infinite restart attempts.
2. **No completion pass**: Even after counting pending restarts toward the hourly budget, a recovery that consumed the last slot cannot finish — it hits the cap on the next tick.
3. **Rollover starvation**: After the completion pass is exhausted, old restart records eventually fall out of the 1-hour window — but `completionPassAllowed` stays `true`, silently starving the channel forever.

### Why This Change Was Made

Issue 1: The `continuingPendingRestart` guard prevented both the rate-limit check and the restart record update for pending restarts. Once a channel entered a permanently-pending state, every monitor tick would attempt another restart without counting it against the hourly budget.

Issue 2: With the cap applied uniformly, a pending recovery that used the last hourly slot would be blocked on the very next check, preventing it from ever completing.

Issue 3 (rollover): `completionPassAllowed` is set to `true` once the completion pass is granted, and only reset when a new restart record is pushed. After the hourly window rolls over and old records are pruned, the flag remains `true`, so the channel is stuck with zero budget — even though capacity has reopened.

### What Changed

- Pending restarts count toward `maxRestartsPerHour` — the rate limit guard no longer skips for pending restarts
- Pending restarts are recorded in `restartsThisHour` — the record update no longer skips for pending restarts
- **One completion pass**: When a pending recovery hits the hourly cap, it gets one extra pass to finish, without pushing a new restart record. A `completionPassAllowed` flag tracks this — reset on each new restart record
- **Rollover reset**: `pruneOldRestarts` now resets `completionPassAllowed` when pruning old entries reopens budget capacity (`before >= maxRestarts && after < maxRestarts`)
- The cooldown check (fresh-restart throttle) still correctly skips for pending restarts, since they continue an already-begun recovery

### Does one pending completion attempt exceed the configured recorded maximum?

**Yes, by 1.** The `maxRestartsPerHour` config limits *recorded restart slots* in the rolling window. A continuing pending restart that consumes the last slot gets one extra recovery attempt (a *completion pass*) without recording a new slot. In practice this means:

- Normal channels: capped at exactly `maxRestartsPerHour` restarts per hour (all recorded)
- Stuck pending channels: capped at `maxRestartsPerHour + 1` calls per hour (the extra call is the unrecorded completion pass)
- After the hourly window rolls over and old records are pruned, `completionPassAllowed` resets, allowing the same pattern in the fresh window

This is intentional: the completion pass prevents a stuck pending channel from being permanently starved after consuming its last budget slot, while still preventing infinite restart loops. The completion pass does not count toward the recorded restart history, so it does not extend the window.

### Evidence

#### Regression Tests

`src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.test.ts:569` — caps pending recovery restarts at the configured maxRestartsPerHour with one completion pass: Simulates a channel where every restart transitions to pending, configures maxRestartsPerHour=2, runs 30 seconds of health checks, and asserts startChannel is called exactly 3 times (2 budgeted + 1 completion pass).

`src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.test.ts:607` — grants one completion pass for a pending recovery that consumed the last hourly slot: Tick-by-tick verification proving the completion pass is exactly one.

`src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.test.ts:945` — resets completion-pass flag when pruning reopens hourly budget: Exhausts budget (3 calls), confirms capped, then advances time just past the 1-hour prune point. Proves the first post-rollover pending attempt consumes a fresh budget slot (call 4 → 5 → 6 with completion pass), then caps again.

`src/gateway/live-rollover.test.ts` — continuous, timestamped, redacted gateway log capture covering the full lifecycle across one hourly rollover boundary (see output below).

#### Live Gateway Logs — Scenario 2: Permanent pending retries cap correctly


#### Live Gateway Logs — Scenario 3: Continuous rollover lifecycle (full hour)

Continuous, timestamped, redacted test output covering the capped state → 1-hour rollover → renewed attempts → completion pass → second cap:

target.title: fix(config): warn on JSON5 comment loss after successful config write
target.body:
#### What Problem This Solves

Close #105683

Fixes silent JSON5 comment loss when `openclaw.json` is written back to disk. OpenClaw parses user configurations with JSON5 (supporting `//` and `/* */` comments), but the canonical write path serializes with `JSON.stringify`, which irreversibly strips all user-authored comments, documentation, and commented-out settings on every automatic config mutation (onboarding, plugin install, model updates).

#### Why This Change Was Made

Previous attempt (#105727) added a regex-based detector with a pre-commit warning. ClawSweeper review identified two defects:

1. **Incomplete JSON5 line continuation handling** — the regex only recognized LF/CR/CRLF as escaped line continuators, missing U+2028 (line separator) and U+2029 (paragraph separator) which JSON5 also permits. A valid string containing `\ //` would trigger a false positive warning.
2. **Warning emitted before write commit** — if any later stage (blocking-reason checks, runtime preflight, atomic replacement) rejected the write, users were told comments would be lost while the original file remained untouched.

This fix:
- Replaces the regex with a **character-by-character lexical scanner** that correctly tracks every JSON5 string escape, including U+2028/U+2029 line continuations
- Moves the warning into `logConfigOverwrite()`, which only fires after `replaceFileAtomic` succeeds (`configCommitted = true`)
- Includes recovery guidance pointing to the pre-write backup saved by `maintainConfigBackups`

#### User Impact

- Users with JSON5 comments in `openclaw.json` now see a post-write warning after any automatic config mutation
- The warning includes instructions to diff against the pre-write backup to recover commented-out settings
- False positives eliminated: URLs, `//` in strings, and all JSON5 line-continued strings are correctly ignored
- Plain JSON configs produce no warning

#### Evidence

- **Type check:** `tsgo` passes with no errors
- **Tests:**
  - `io.parse.test.ts` — 11 tests pass (+9: `hasJSON5Comments` covers line comments, block comments, double-quoted strings, single-quoted strings, plain JSON, empty input, escaped quotes, U+2028/U+2029 continuations, LF/CR/CRLF continuations)
  - `io.audit.test.ts` — all tests pass (no regression)
  - `io.write-config.test.ts` — 103 tests pass (no regression)
- **Change scope:** 2 files, +125 lines
  - `src/config/io.ts` — +68: `hasJSON5Comments()` lexical scanner + warning in `logConfigOverwrite` closure (post-commit)
  - `src/config/io.parse.test.ts` — +57: 9 focused tests
  - No new dependencies, no config/CLI/SDK/docs/changelog surface affected
- **Live proof:** standalone script exercising the lexical scanner:

```
=== JSON5 Comment Detection — Proof ===

[Group 1] Line comments outside strings
  ✓ line-start //
  ✓ inline //
  ✓ trailing //

[Group 2] Block comments outside strings
  ✓ block comment
  ✓ inline block
  ✓ multi-line block

[Group 3] Comment markers inside strings — ignored
  ✓ URL in string
  ✓ // in double-quoted
  ✓ /* */ in double-quoted
  ✓ // in single-quoted
  ✓ /* */ in single-quoted

[Group 4] Escaped quotes inside strings
  ✓ escaped quote in string
  ✓ escaped backslash + real comment

[Group 5] JSON5 line continuations (U+2028 / U+2029)
  ✓ U+2028 line separator continuation
  ✓ U+2029 paragraph separator continuation
  ✓ LF line continuation
  ✓ CR line continuation

[Group 6] Plain JSON — no false positives
  ✓ simple object
  ✓ nested
  ✓ empty object
  ✓ empty string
  ✓ whitespace only

[Group 7] Edge: single / not part of comment
  ✓ path with single / in string
  ✓ single / inside string

[Group 8] Contract: detection is boolean, no side effects
  ✓ idempotent
  ✓ no side effects

=== Results: 26 passed / 0 failed ===
```

target.title: fix(cli): rewriteUpdateFlagArgv corrupts positional values containing --update
target.body:
Fixes #105923

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `openclaw --update` was rewritten to `openclaw update` even when `--update` appeared after the `--` terminator or as a positional value for another command (for example, `openclaw config set some.key --update`). This silently corrupted user input.

## Why This Change Was Made

`rewriteUpdateFlagArgv` used `argv.indexOf("--update")`, which matches `--update` anywhere in the argument list. The intended behavior is to preserve the legacy root-level `--update` spelling only when `--update` is the first non-root-option token and appears before `--`. The fix scans past root options (`--profile`, `--log-level`, `--container`, `--dev`, `--no-color`), stops at `--`, and only rewrites the first matching `--update`.

## User Impact

Users can now safely pass `--update` as a literal value to CLI commands or after `--` without it being rewritten to the `update` subcommand. Root-level `openclaw --update` and `openclaw --profile p --update` continue to work as before.

## Evidence

Focused tests added to `src/cli/run-main.test.ts`:

- `does not rewrite --update after the -- terminator`
- `does not rewrite --update when it is a positional value for another command`

Before the fix:

```ts
rewriteUpdateFlagArgv(["node", "entry.js", "config", "set", "foo", "--", "--update"]);
// => ["node", "entry.js", "config", "set", "foo", "--", "update"]

rewriteUpdateFlagArgv(["node", "entry.js", "config", "set", "update.channel", "--update"]);
// => ["node", "entry.js", "config", "set", "update.channel", "update"]
```

After the fix:

```ts
// both leave --update unchanged
```

Validation run:

- `pnpm test src/cli/run-main.test.ts --run` → 38/38 passed
- `pnpm test src/cli --run` → 157 files, 2924 tests passed

target.title: fix(goals): preserve durable owner across completion wakes
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Completion wakes can execute under a transient run-session key even though a session goal is owned by the durable user-facing origin route, such as a Telegram topic. Goal tools previously preferred the transient `runSessionKey`, so `get_goal` could return `null` while the goal still existed on the durable owner session.

## Why This Change Was Made

Goal tool scope resolution now prefers a concrete `agentSessionKey`, which represents the durable owning thread, and uses the run-session key only for legacy `global` contexts or when no owner key exists. This keeps completion wakes and recovered runs attached to the same goal without adding a channel-specific rule or changing the persisted goal shape.

The change is intentionally limited to core goal owner resolution, its focused regression coverage, and the directly coupled goal documentation.

## User Impact

`get_goal`, `create_goal`, and `update_goal` continue to resolve the durable thread goal when execution temporarily runs under another session key. Existing structured goals require no migration.

Compatibility limitation: legacy goals containing only an objective plus an external Markdown checklist do not contain a structured executable phase ledger. This lookup fix cannot infer missing phase identities or automatically launch missing phases; durable multi-phase scheduling still requires a task or flow controller that persists phase state.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(xai): apply request policy to video generation requests

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users generating video with xAI could configure provider request policy, such as custom headers or proxy settings, but xAI video generation requests ignored that policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

The xAI video provider now sanitizes `cfg.models.providers.xai.request` and passes it into the existing provider HTTP resolver used by the create, poll, and download flow. The poll and download flow now always uses the guarded provider fetch path; private-network access is enabled only when explicitly configured. The change leaves generation parameters, polling semantics, idempotency headers, and media parsing unchanged.

## User Impact

Users can create a session from an agent row or the Claude Code catalog header, retain the normal folder, worktree, and execution-node controls, and see Claude Code sessions only under Claude Code.
