target.title: docs: respect configured Crabbox provider for agent tests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's agent-testing guidance hardcoded Blacksmith Testbox for ordinary trusted validation. That caused agents to override an existing explicit Crabbox choice such as `CRABBOX_PROVIDER=local-container`, even though the wrapper already supports that environment override before the repository's Blacksmith default.

## Why This Change Was Made

The testing and Crabbox skills now tell trusted agent workflows to omit `--provider` unless a specific proof or safety route requires one. This preserves the existing wrapper selection contract:

1. an explicitly requested/command-line provider;
2. platform routing such as automatic Azure selection for Windows/WSL2;
3. `CRABBOX_PROVIDER`;
4. the repository `.crabbox.yaml` default (`blacksmith-testbox`).

The skills distinguish the configured environment/repository provider reported by `crabbox config show --json` from the actual backend selected for a command. The wrapper's emitted `[crabbox] ... provider=...` diagnostic is authoritative for actual provider attribution, including explicit overrides and automatic platform routing.

The skills also distinguish a Crabbox-managed `local-container` run from direct host testing and avoid inferring AWS from the shared `cbx_...` lease prefix.

ClawSweeper correctly identified that `crabbox config show --json` does not create a user-config preference above repository config. The PR was narrowed accordingly: it does not change `scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs`, adds no merged-config precedence contract, and adds no new fail-closed startup behavior.

AI-assisted: this change was agent-tested with Claude through `acpx`, reviewed with Codex autoreview, and revised in response to ClawSweeper.

## User Impact

Developers who explicitly set `CRABBOX_PROVIDER` can run ordinary trusted agent validation on that backend without agents forcing Blacksmith Testbox. Developers without an explicit override continue to use the repository's Blacksmith Testbox default.

A configured local container still executes tests inside a Crabbox-managed Docker lease; it does not silently downgrade to host-local execution. Remote, cross-platform, untrusted-source, and Testbox-specific proof requirements continue to select their required backend explicitly.

## Evidence

- Blind `acpx claude` validation independently resolved the inherited `CRABBOX_PROVIDER=local-container`; the prompt did not name the expected provider.
- The first agent attempt exposed a guidance defect by running the focused test directly on the host. That result was rejected, and the skills were clarified to require wrapper-managed Docker execution for `local-container`.
- Post-fix Claude runs correctly provisioned local-container Docker leases, ran the focused wrapper suite inside the containers, and cleaned up their leases.
- Provider-attribution probe: configured provider `local-container`; wrapper invoked with explicit `--provider aws` emitted `provider=aws`, confirming why wrapper output must be authoritative.
- Final post-rebase proof:
  - base: `upstream/main` at `161525d43c4c0157a8fd4feceb2bf96cb4db5900`;
  - provider/runtime: `provider=local-container`, `runtime=docker`, Crabbox `0.37.1`;
  - lease: `cbx_29a3dd41d47d` / `brisk-crab-d2c5`, explicitly deleted after the run;
  - command: `node scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs run --id cbx_29a3dd41d47d --timing-json -- corepack pnpm test test/scripts/crabbox-wrapper.test.ts --reporter=default`;
  - result: 1 test file passed; 192/192 tests passed.
- Final diff relative to `upstream/main`: two skill files only; zero wrapper/test code diff.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --stream-engine-output` on `e0bb1c889ae` changes — clean, no accepted/actionable findings.

target.title: fix: surface stalled-session interruptions
target.body:
Closes #103905

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a stuck-session recovery could remove a channel's streamed draft without sending a terminal notice. A non-cooperative tool could also keep running after the owning turn was aborted, leaving the caller blocked until it eventually settled.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reply-operation terminal state now preserves `run_stalled` as a user-visible interruption while explicit user and restart cancellations keep their existing behavior. Tool execution races the existing cooperative `AbortSignal`, so an aborted run stops waiting while late tool settlement remains observed. Risk note: external side effects cannot be undone; the tool still receives the abort signal and its late promise is deliberately drained rather than delivered into the terminated run.

## User Impact

Users whose stalled turn is recovered now receive a clear interruption message instead of losing all visible trace of the turn. Plugin tools that honor cancellation can stop promptly, and tools that do not no longer hold the aborted turn open.

## Evidence

Focused regression proof drives the real reply-run registry expiry path into the production runner: `expireStaleReplyOperation()` records `run_stalled` and aborts the same operation before both terminal projections run. The tool abort proof exercises `wrapToolWithAbortSignal` with a non-cooperative handler. Negative control used the real pre-fix sources via `git show HEAD^ -- <files>`. 

Before (pre-fix abort wrapper): caller stays blocked after run abort while the non-cooperative tool keeps running.

```text
=== abort promptness ===
{
  "result": { "kind": "timeout", "ms": 523.063467 },
  "toolSettled": true,
  "signalAborted": true
}
Error: abort promptness FAIL: {"kind":"timeout","ms":523.063467}
```

Before (pre-fix reply runner): stalled recovery leaves an empty success outcome, so the channel-facing draft can disappear with no interruption notice.

```text
{
  "result": { "kind": "failed", "code": "run_stalled" },
  "outcome": {
    "kind": "success",
    "runResult": { "payloads": [], "meta": {} }
  }
}
pre-fix stalled path: no interruption notice (bug reproduced)
```

After (fixed branch): abort returns in ~21ms, and stalled recovery surfaces the interruption payload.

```text
=== abort promptness ===
{
  "result": {
    "kind": "rejected",
    "err": { "name": "AbortError" },
    "ms": 21.162068000000545
  },
  "toolSettled": true,
  "signalAborted": true
}
abort_promptness: PASS

=== stalled interruption ===
{
  "result": { "kind": "failed", "code": "run_stalled" },
  "outcome": {
    "kind": "final",
    "payload": {
      "text": "⚠️ This turn was interrupted because it stopped making progress. Please try again.",
      "isError": true
    }
  }
}
stalled_interruption: PASS
ALL PASS
```

Focused local verification:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution.test.ts -t "stalled reply operation"
2 passed | 246 skipped

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-tools.abort.test.ts
1 passed

pnpm tsgo:core:test
passed
```

What was not tested: no live Slack Socket Mode round-trip of a 15-minute blocked tool. The proven boundary is the channel-facing reply projection and tool-wrapper abort race before outbound send, which is where the silent draft deletion and blocked caller originate.

AI-assisted: Codex/Cursor; focused proof run manually.

target.title: fix(commitments): avoid quadratic heartbeat session discovery
target.body:
Related: #105787

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes heartbeat commitment fan-out latency when many due commitments belong to one session. The existing path loads and expires the JSON store while holding the queue/file lock, releases that lock, then scans the returned in-memory records. For every qualifying due record it rescans the complete store to count recent sent commitments. The quadratic scan is outside the lock, but it delays heartbeat processing and increases heartbeat latency. Reported isolated medians were approximately 191 ms at 1,000, 847 ms at 2,000, and 2.28 s at 4,000 records.

## Why This Change Was Made

The commitments store now builds the rolling 24-hour sent-count map once per agent and reuses it for due-session discovery and single-session due selection. Due-window, snooze, expiry, daily-cap, ordering, limit, agent-scope, queue, and cross-process file-lock behavior remain on the existing path.

This is intentionally an interim JSON-store fix. OpenClaw's shared SQLite state schema already contains a commitments table and indexes, but making it canonical requires a separate JSON-to-SQLite migration/doctor contract and broader persistence coverage. That migration remains a follow-up rather than expanding this focused latency fix.

## User Impact

Heartbeat commitment discovery changes from repeated full-store counting to one aggregation pass plus the existing due-record scan. Large concentrated sessions therefore scale linearly with store size instead of quadratically, without changing which sessions are eligible for delivery.

## Evidence

- Store correctness coverage includes due windows, snoozes, rolling daily caps, agent scope, deterministic session-key ordering, expiry, and concurrent file-store updates.
- The concentrated-session regression uses 8,000 due records in one session and a production-like `limit: 10`, so the base implementation repeatedly rescans the store while the fixed implementation reuses one count map.
- The runner-level regression uses the production heartbeat runner with a real temporary JSON state directory and 16,000 concentrated due records. The model and channel boundaries are stubbed there for deterministic CI coverage.
- Focused validation, using the linked-worktree local fallback:
  ```text
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commitments/store.test.ts src/infra/heartbeat-runner.commitments.test.ts --reporter=verbose
  11 store tests passed; 14 heartbeat-runner tests passed.
  ```

### Real Gateway heartbeat proof

I reran the actual built `dist/index.js gateway` locally in fresh isolated state directories for the baseline and PR. Each run seeded 16,000 pending due commitments plus one recent sent commitment, all concentrated in one Telegram session, then invoked the production Gateway `wake` RPC once. The Gateway scheduler, heartbeat runner, JSON store, due-session selector, Telegram plugin dispatch, and delivery/status updates were real. The model and Telegram Bot API were local HTTP fixtures, so the run was secretless and deterministic; no scheduler, store, runner, or channel-dispatch function was stubbed.

The baseline used main checkout `43901be298`, a descendant of the PR base `6c884691105b`; there were no changes under `src/commitments/` or `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts` between those refs. The PR run used `fcb249f4953485071e123b7cd2fce31f32ea96da`. The redacted terminal output below is one matched run per revision:

```text
baseline 43901be298:
REAL_GATEWAY_HEARTBEAT_PROOF {"store":"json","commitmentCount":16000,"seededDueSessionKeys":["agent:main:telegram:proof"],"channelSendCount":1,"sentRequestBodies":1,"elapsedMs":21510,"pendingAfterRun":15998,"lastHeartbeat":{"status":"sent","to":"telegram:12345","durationMs":1947}}

PR fcb249f495:
REAL_GATEWAY_HEARTBEAT_PROOF {"store":"json","commitmentCount":16000,"seededDueSessionKeys":["agent:main:telegram:proof"],"channelSendCount":1,"sentRequestBodies":1,"elapsedMs":13990,"pendingAfterRun":15998,"lastHeartbeat":{"status":"sent","to":"telegram:12345","durationMs":2267}}
```

Selection and delivery behavior matched: both runs discovered the same session key, sent exactly one Telegram request to the same target, reported `sent`, and left the same 15,998 commitments pending. Wake-to-delivery elapsed time was 21.5 s on the baseline and 14.0 s on the PR. This is representative real-process behavior proof, not a statistically stable benchmark; cold Gateway startup and local fixture variance affect timing. The durable scaling proof remains the concentrated-session regression.

### Direct DigitalOcean proof status

I attempted the requested direct DigitalOcean route with the token supplied through the environment and never printed it:

```text
provider: digitalocean
lease: cbx_1d0ec418e4bc
head binding: fcb249f4953485071e123b7cd2fce31f32ea96da
warmup: succeeded
sync: exact head verified remotely
result: dependency install on s-1vcpu-1gb was killed with exit 137 (1 GB memory)
cleanup: lease deleted
```

The DO lease did not reach Gateway execution, so the local run above is the accepted narrow fallback rather than DigitalOcean proof. No Blacksmith lease was used.

- `git diff --check`, `oxfmt --check`, and `oxlint` passed for the changed source/tests.
- Correctly invoked autoreview:
  ```sh
  .agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local
  .agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main
  ```
  Local mode reported no uncommitted changes; the committed branch review reported no accepted/actionable findings.
- Current PR-head GitHub checks have no failures, and the Real behavior proof check passed. The branch remains behind current `origin/main`; no rebase or code churn was introduced.

## AI-Assisted Disclosure

This PR was prepared with Codex and is AI-assisted. I reviewed the implementation, its callers, sibling selection path, persistence/locking behavior, tests, and the SQLite/Kysely storage contracts.

target.title: fix(ai): reject noncanonical array indices in local schema refs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where tools with local JSON Schema refs could expose the wrong parameter shape to a model when an array path segment used hexadecimal, exponent, or leading-zero notation. JavaScript number coercion previously treated values such as `0x1` and `1e0` as array index `1`, silently inlining a different schema branch.

## Why This Change Was Made

Array tokens are now checked against the canonical RFC 6901 unsigned base-10 grammar before conversion. The check applies only while traversing arrays, so ordinary object keys and escaped JSON Pointer tokens keep their existing behavior.

AI-assisted.

## User Impact

Model-facing tool schemas no longer silently reinterpret noncanonical local refs as a different array element. Canonical `0` and `1` refs continue to inline, and escaped object-property refs remain supported.

## Evidence

### Real registered-tool → model request proof

Validated on exact pushed head `dd9b70c4a99c1d4706dca264b24b6301303988b5`, rebased onto `c808b01a042b9c6b6751890bf8f58661d7941e4c`.

The temporary fixture was packaged and installed through the real plugin lifecycle, then exercised by a real local agent turn:

```text
$ pnpm openclaw plugins install npm-pack:<fixture.tgz> --force
Installed plugin: pr-105922-schema-proof

$ pnpm openclaw plugins inspect pr-105922-schema-proof --runtime --json
"status": "loaded"
"toolNames": ["pr_105922_schema_probe"]

$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --agent main \
    --session-id pr-105922-schema-proof \
    --model openai/gpt-5.6-luna \
    --message "Return PR_105922_MODEL_PATH_OK without calling tools." \
    --thinking off --timeout 60 --json
[model-fetch] POST http://127.0.0.1:<mock-port>/v1/responses
[model-fetch] response status=200
"finalAssistantVisibleText": "PR_105922_MODEL_PATH_OK"
```

The repository mock OpenAI HTTP server captured the actual `/v1/responses` payload emitted by the production plugin loader, embedded agent runtime, tool policy, OpenAI Responses projection, and provider transport. Only the remote model response was mocked; tool registration and model-facing request construction were real.

Redacted extraction of the registered tool from that one captured request:

```json
{
  "type": "function",
  "name": "pr_105922_schema_probe",
  "parameters": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "canonicalOne": { "type": "number" },
      "noncanonicalHex": { "$ref": "#/$defs/Choice/anyOf/0x1" },
      "escapedObjectKey": { "type": "boolean" }
    }
  }
}
```

This proves the real model-facing payload still resolves canonical array index `1`, leaves noncanonical `0x1` unresolved instead of exposing the wrong `number` branch, and preserves escaped object-key resolution.

### Focused regression and static checks

- Before fix on current main: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-tools.schema.test.ts` failed because `#/$defs/Choice/anyOf/0x1` became `{ type: "number" }` (45 passed, 1 failed).
- Exact refreshed head: the same command passes all 46 tests, covering canonical `0`/`1`, rejected `0x1`/`1e0`/`01`, and an escaped object-key control.
- `pnpm format:check -- packages/ai/src/providers/agent-tools-parameter-schema.ts src/agents/agent-tools.schema.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base upstream/main --stream-engine-output` — clean, no accepted/actionable findings; correctness confidence 0.98.

No external provider credential or user state was used; the proof ran with an isolated state directory and a dummy key accepted only by the local mock endpoint.

target.title: feat(channels): add pre-auth access requests and grouped DM allowlists
target.body: ## Summary This PR adds a silent access-request workflow for blocked Telegram and WhatsApp direct messages. - Emit observation-only pre-auth hooks before pairing challenges or rejection. - Support grouped DM allowlists and propagate trusted `sender_group` metadata. - Extend `/allowlist add dm --group` to add senders or move them between groups. - Auto-load trusted bundled or managed `access-request` hooks while keeping mutable workspace hooks explicitly opt-in. - Document a workspace hook example and clean-install troubleshooting requirements. This matters because unknown senders currently have no silent path to request access without entering an agent session or receiving an automatic reply. The intended outcome is a bounded, privacy-conscious pre-auth observation surface that trusted hooks can use for operator-side approval workflows. Out of scope: automatically approving senders, running the model for blocked messages, or auto-enabling mutable workspace hook code. Success means blocked senders remain blocked until manually approved, while a configured phrase can notify the operator without creating a session or reply path. Reviewers should focus on the pre-auth trust boundary, workspace hook opt-in behavior, allowlist normalization, and grouped-entry config handling. ## Linked context Which issue does this close? N/A - no linked issue. Which issues, PRs, or discussions are related? N/A. Was this requested by a maintainer or owner? No known maintainer or owner request. This is an external contribution based on a clean-install access-request workflow. ## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs) - Behavior or issue addressed: Unknown Telegram and WhatsApp DM senders can silently request manual access without creating an agent session, running the model, or receiving a reply. - Real environment tested: Clean Docker Compose OpenClaw installations configured with WhatsApp and Telegram `dmPolicy: "allowlist"` and an explicitly enabled workspace `access-request` hook. - Exact steps or command run after this patch: 1. Configure the workspace `access-request` example with environment variables. 2. Run `openclaw config set tools.profile messaging`. 3. Run `openclaw config set commands.config true`. 4. target.title: fix(agents): tighten bash-tools schema fields from Type.Number to Type.Integer
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`bash-tools.schemas.ts` uses `Type.Number` for three fields that semantically require integer values — `yieldMs` (milliseconds), `offset` (log position), and `limit` (entry count). Fractional values like `offset=10.5` or `limit=5.3` silently pass schema validation and reach tool logic with nonsensical values.

## Root Cause

`Type.Number` in TypeBox accepts any JavaScript number including floats. For fields whose semantics are inherently integer-valued, this means invalid input survives the schema gate.

## Fix

Change three `Type.Number` to `Type.Integer` in `src/agents/bash-tools.schemas.ts`:

- `yieldMs`: milliseconds before backgrounding (default 10000) — sub-millisecond yields are not a practical use case
- `offset`: log position offset — fractional byte positions make no sense
- `limit`: log entry count — fractional counts make no sense

This mirrors the same pattern already applied to `lsSchema`, `grepSchema`, `toolSearch`, `readSchema`, and `processSchema` (lzyyzznl #105827, #105822, #105567, #105564, #105560).

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/agents/bash-tools.schemas.ts` | 3× `Type.Number` → `Type.Integer` |

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof — Type.Integer rejects floats at the schema gate

TypeBox `Type.Integer` uses `Number.isInteger()` internally. Before the fix, `Check(schema, { offset: 10.5 })` returns `true` — the invalid value passes validation. After the fix, the same check returns `false` — the float is rejected before any tool logic runs.

### Vitest

Existing agent tool schema tests continue to pass. The change is a schema-level tightening that does not affect any runtime behavior for valid integer inputs.

target.title: fix(session): stop repeated restart recovery after retry budget
target.body:
Related: #95750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a gateway restart loop where the same interrupted main session can be accepted for automatic recovery on every boot. Supervisor backoff does not make the session healthy, so attempts separated by minutes or hours must still consume one durable recovery budget.

## Why This Change Was Made

Main-session restart recovery now has one canonical persisted fuse: `SessionEntry.mainRestartRecovery`.

- `main-session-recovery-state.ts` is the single pure interpreter for recovery state, lifecycle fences, foreground claims, reservations, tombstones, and health/reset transitions.
- `main-session-recovery-store.ts` commits those transitions atomically through the session accessor writer lock; callers submit closed domain commands instead of mutating recovery fields.
- `automaticAttempts` counts accepted or acceptance-uncertain automatic recoveries since the last non-aborted run settlement on the same session.
- The first three recoveries may dispatch. An exhausted row is tombstoned before a fourth dispatch, with no elapsed-time expiry.
- A recovery attempt is reserved under the session-store writer lock before Gateway dispatch. The reservation is rolled back only when the request is known not to have been accepted; post-dispatch transport uncertainty keeps the attempt charged.
- Gateway performs a non-consuming validation during its normal session transaction, then atomically admits the exact reservation only at the final acceptance boundary. Abort and foreground-owner races preserve a recoverable interrupted state without leaking run registries.
- Reservation cancellation follows the reservation identity if Gateway canonicalizes a legacy session key during admission.
- Foreground admissions use lifecycle-generation-scoped token sets to fence concurrent recovery scans. Shared ingress claims cover direct agent-command callers as well as Gateway RPC.
- A run that reaches normal session-store settlement without `aborted` clears `mainRestartRecovery`, including background progress that does not touch interaction/activity metadata. Session replacement and reset also clear it.
- `restartRecoveryRuns` remains lifecycle suppression only; it is not used to derive the durable retry budget.
- Subagent orphan recovery retains its separate policy: two attempts in the existing two-minute rapid re-wedge window.
- Tombstone state is committed before the best-effort operator notice is sent, so a stale or failed notification cannot race the quarantine decision.
- Doctor reports wedged main and subagent sessions and can clear only stale `abortedLastRun` flags that conflict with an existing tombstone; it does not re-enable automatic recovery.
- Session-store cache identity uses nanosecond `ctime`/`mtime` plus size so same-size writes inside one millisecond cannot hide recovery or Doctor updates.

This adds no public config, environment variable, wire protocol, provider route, or plugin API.

## User Impact

A wedged main session can no longer trigger unbounded automatic resume across Gateway restarts. After three accepted or acceptance-uncertain recovery attempts, OpenClaw quarantines the session before another automatic dispatch and asks the operator to inspect it and use `/new` or reset.

Healthy progress restores the full budget. The fuse does not expire merely because time passes.

target.title: fix(proxy-capture): honor response backpressure and client abort
target.body:
Closes #105701

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the debug proxy capture server would forward upstream response bodies without honoring `ServerResponse.write()` backpressure, and could crash or leave work running when a client aborted mid-stream. Operators and test fixtures using the debug proxy could see unbounded memory growth under slow clients and unhandled write errors on disconnect.

## Why This Change Was Made

The HTTP response forward path uses Node native `Readable.pipe()` for backpressure, keeps body-preview capture as an independent `data` observer, cancels upstream on client abort, and preserves pre-header 502 / post-header abort behavior on upstream errors. Existing partial-upstream-error behavior (complete 502 before headers / abort after headers) is preserved.

## User Impact

Debug proxy traffic capture remains available for local diagnostics and fixture recording, but slow clients no longer force unbounded buffering of upstream response data, and mid-response client aborts no longer leave the proxy in a fragile write-after-end state. No product config or user-facing channel behavior changes.

## Evidence

**Verification host:** local macOS (agent; CS option 1 follow-up)

Commands run after native-pipe refactor:

```text
pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/proxy-capture/proxy-server.ts src/proxy-capture/proxy-server.test.ts
# pass

pnpm exec oxlint src/proxy-capture/proxy-server.ts src/proxy-capture/proxy-server.test.ts
# 0 warnings / 0 errors

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/proxy-capture/proxy-server.test.ts
# 9/9 passed

# Real proxy process proof (origin + startDebugProxyServer in-process listeners,
# real HTTP clients over loopback — not unit Fake streams):
# slow client pause-after-first-chunk, mid-response abort, subsequent /healthy
```

Focused tests:
- native pipe backpressure + capture observer
- client abort destroys upstream
- mid-response abort + later healthy request through same proxy

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: Debug proxy forwards upstream bodies via Node native `Readable.pipe()` backpressure; preview capture is an independent `data` observer; client abort cancels upstream; later requests still succeed.
- Environment: local macOS, branch tip after CS follow-up commit, Node via `pnpm exec tsx` / `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`.
- Current-main contrast: main ignored `write()` false (no backpressure). First PR revision used a hand-written pause/drain controller; CS asked for native pipe + real-process proof.
- Exact steps after this patch:
  1. Refactor `pipeUpstreamBodyToClient` to `upstreamRes.pipe(res)` with capture observer + abort cancel.
  2. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/proxy-capture/proxy-server.test.ts` → 9/9.
  3. Real-process proof: start streaming origin + `startDebugProxyServer` listeners; HTTP client slow-read; abort after first chunk; GET `/healthy` on same proxy.
- Evidence after fix (redacted loopback ports):


target.title: fix(gateway): add base64 validation before decode in talk-realtime-relay
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #105846

**Problem**: Real-time relay audio frames use unpadded base64 encoding, but the `isValidBase64` guard from `chat-attachments.ts` requires length % 4 === 0, rejecting valid unpadded audio frames. This breaks relay clients sending standard unpadded base64.

**Solution**: Replace `isValidBase64` with a lenient `isValidRelayBase64` that accepts unpadded base64 while still rejecting empty strings, invalid characters, and misplaced padding. The key difference is removing the `length % 4 !== 0` requirement — relay audio frames from browser APIs commonly omit padding.

**What changed**: In `src/gateway/talk-realtime-relay.ts` — added `isValidRelayBase64` function (line 66-78) that checks characters without requiring length % 4 === 0. Changed the guard on line 1159 from `isValidBase64` to `isValidRelayBase64`. Also exports `isBase64DataCharCode` and `isValidBase64` from `chat-attachments.ts` (shared with PR #105837).

**NOT changed**: `isValidBase64` behavior in `chat-attachments.ts` — still rejects unpadded base64 for chat image attachments where padded base64 is expected. No changes to relay session lifecycle, audio processing, or any other gateway logic. The two validators coexist for their respective use cases.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Lenient base64 validation for real-time relay audio frames accepts unpadded base64 while still rejecting invalid input.
**Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node.js 25.9.0, OpenClaw `main@HEAD` with this patch applied.
**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `node --import tsx/esm -e "..."` (standalone validation against production `isBase64DataCharCode`)
**After-fix evidence**: 7/7 validation scenarios passed (see terminal output below).
**Observed result after the fix**: Valid padded base64 accepted (true), valid unpadded base64 accepted (true) — key difference from `isValidBase64`, empty string rejected (false), invalid characters rejected (false), padding-in-middle rejected (false).
**What was not tested**: End-to-end relay session with real audio provider (requires full Gateway runtime); the function-level validation is testable independently and mirrors the production `isValidBase64` guard pattern.

## Tests and validation

```
$ node --import tsx/esm -e "..."

=== Real behavior proof: isValidRelayBase64 (lenient) ===

The lenient validator accepts unpadded base64, unlike isValidBase64.

  PASS Valid padded: dGVzdA==: true (expected true)
  PASS Valid unpadded (lenient): dGVzdA: true (expected true)     ← key difference
  PASS Empty string: false (expected false)
  PASS Invalid chars: false (expected false)
  PASS Padding in middle: false (expected false)
  PASS Relay audio frame (unpadded): true (expected true)
  PASS Relay audio frame (padded): true (expected true)

7/7 passed
```

Comparison with `isValidBase64`:

| Input | `isValidBase64` | `isValidRelayBase64` |
|-------|----------------|---------------------|
| `"dGVzdA=="` (padded) | ✅ accept | ✅ accept |
| `"dGVzdA"` (unpadded) | ❌ reject | ✅ accept |
| `""` (empty) | ❌ reject | ❌ reject |
| `"invalid!"` | ❌ reject | ❌ reject |
| `"abc=defg"` (padding mid) | ❌ reject | ❌ reject |

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible — valid padded base64 continues to work; unpadded base64 is now also accepted as intended
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation
- [x] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary

target.title: fix(agents): skip model-override repair and visibility gate for locked sessions
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves When a session is model-selection-locked (e.g. Claude Code catalog adoption via the anthropic extension, or durable harness-owned sessions), multiple code paths could reject the locked model override as unrecognized, reset it to the agent's default model, or normalize it away — all of which tripped `ModelSelectionLockedError`. **Result:** Users who adopted a Claude Code session in the Control UI could see and preview the session, but sending any message would fail with "Model selection is locked for this session." ## Solution Six guard additions across two files: **`src/agents/agent-command.ts`:** 1. Skip the repair block for locked sessions (line 1610) 2. Allow locked overrides through the visibility-policy gate (line 1740) 3. Skip resolveSelection normalization for locked sessions (line 1799) 4. Clear legacy auto-fallback flags for locked sessions so the stored override is applied (line 1677) **`src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection.ts`:** 5. Skip stale/disallowed override reset for locked sessions (line 325) 6. Allow locked overrides through the visibility-policy gate (line 408) 7. Skip resolveSelection normalization for locked sessions (line 414) **`src/agents/agent-command.live-model-switch.test.ts` / `src/commands/agent.test.ts` / `src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection.test.ts`:** Updated three test expectations to reflect the new behavior where locked sessions proceed with their locked model instead of throwing. ### Why `isModelSelectionLocked` (not `isValidAgentHarnessSessionStoreEntry`) The repair block at line 1610 already guards with `!isValidAgentHarnessSessionStoreEntry(...)`, which covers durable harness-owned sessions (codex, etc.) but does _not_ cover CLI-backend-owned locked sessions (e.g. `plugin:anthropic:catalog-adopt:claude:...`). CLI-backend sessions carry `modelSelectionLocked: true` without an `agentHarnessId` or harness-shaped session key, so `isValidAgentHarnessSessionStoreEntry` returns `false` for them. Using `isModelSelectionLocked(sessionEntry)` directly is correct because: - `modelSelectionLocked` can only be set by a plugin via the `createSessionEntry` API. Ordinary user or UI sessions never carry this flag. - Every session that has this flag — harness-owned, CLI-backend-owned, or otherwise — was intentionally locked by its owning plugin and should not have its model overrides repaired, reset, or visibility-filtered by generic runtime paths. - The existing guard (`isValidAgentHarnessSessionStoreEntry`) already implies `modelSelectionLocked === true`; our change widens the exemption from "harness locks only" to "all durable locks," which is the correct invariant. ## User Impact - Users running Claude Code v2.x can adopt and continue Claude Code sessions from the OpenClaw Control UI without hitting a model-selection-locked error - The fix applies to all model-selection-locked sessions, not just Claude Code catalog adoption - No change to non-locked sessions ## Evidence - `pnpm build` — passed - `pnpm vitest run src/agents/agent-command.live-model-switch.test.ts` — 192/194 passed; 2 failures pre-existing (Windows path mismatch) - `pnpm vitest run src/commands/agent.test.ts` — 42/42 passed - `pnpm vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection.test.ts` — 61/63 passed; 2 failures pre-existing (Windows EPERM during temp dir cleanup) - `pnpm test:extension anthropic` — 17 test files, 219 tests, all passing - `pnpm test:contracts` — channel contracts: 426/426 passed; plugin contracts: 952/986 passed (34 EBUSY failures pre-existing on Windows) - `pnpm check` — all preflight guards passed (only pre-existing npm shrinkwrap staleness) - Screenshots (before/after): **Before** **After** > This PR was authored with AI assistance (Claude Code). Closes #105378

target.title: fix(slack): bound userCache growth with pruneMapToMaxSize
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`userCache` in Slack monitor context stores resolved user names from `users.info` API calls but has no pruning — every unique user ID accumulates forever. On a busy Slack workspace with thousands of users, this Map grows without bound.

## Why This Change Was Made

`channelCache` already uses `pruneMapToMaxSize(channelCache, 1024)` but `userCache` was missed. The fix adds the same pattern at 2048 entries.

## User Impact

- Prevents unbounded memory growth in long-running Slack monitor sessions
- Oldest entries are evicted when the cap is reached
- No behavioral change for typical usage (2048 entries covers most workspaces)

## Evidence

### Before (no pruning)
```typescript
userCache.set(cacheKey, entry);  // ← never removed
// userCache grows without bound as new users are resolved
```

### After (bounded at 2048)
```typescript
userCache.set(cacheKey, entry);
pruneMapToMaxSize(userCache, SLACK_USER_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES);  // evicts oldest
```

### Unit test (10/10 passed)
```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/slack/src/monitor/context.test.ts

 ✓ evicts the oldest user name when the bounded user cache fills (new test)
 ✓ ... (9 existing tests)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
```

### Lint + Format
```
$ npx oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json extensions/slack/src/monitor/context.ts  # No errors
$ npx oxfmt --check extensions/slack/src/monitor/context.ts              # Correct format
```

## What Changed

- extensions/slack/src/monitor/context.ts: +2 lines (SLACK_USER_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES + pruneMapToMaxSize)
- extensions/slack/src/monitor/context.test.ts: +15 lines (eviction test)

target.title: feat(cloud-workers): openclaw worker mode running the embedded loop on the box
target.body:
Part of #104294 (cloud workers, milestone 2, PR 9 — the composition PR). Builds on the four landed milestone-2 backend contracts: #104688 (worker role), #104809 (transcript commits), #105275 (live events), #105719 (inference proxy). Design: `docs/plan/cloud-workers.md` (openclaw worker mode).

## What Problem This Solves

The four backend RPCs exist on the gateway side, but nothing yet runs an agent session ON a worker box. This PR adds `openclaw worker` mode: the entry point + worker-side runtime that dials the gateway over the reverse tunnel, admits with the minted credential + handshake, and runs the embedded agent loop on the box — with its persistence, model, and streaming seams tethered to the gateway, and tools running locally. This is where a worker box becomes capable of running a real session driven from the gateway.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `openclaw worker` entry: restricted runtime (loadPlugins:"never", no channels, no gateway HTTP surfaces, throwaway mkdtemp 0700 state dir, in-memory empty auth storage — no local model auth profile read). Dials the tunnel-forwarded local socket, presents credential + handshake, attaches to its single assigned session. Fails closed on admission failure (with a bounded 120s admission deadline so a leased box can't burn forever on an unreachable gateway).
- Embedded runner rewired: session persistence -> transcript-commit RPC client (base-leaf CAS + runEpoch + seq, durable replay dedupe); model calls -> inference-proxy RPC client (provider/model reference strings only, streamed deltas + terminal, durable-replay resume); streaming -> live-event RPC client (monotonic seq, cumulative ACK, unacked-tail replay). Tools are the six coding tools (read/write/edit/apply_patch/exec/process), local-only, fail-closed availability check.
- Reconnect/resume: exact-frame transcript retry (ledger dedupe), cumulative live-ACK replay of the unacked tail, durable inference resume (single provider call, no double-bill). Owner-epoch supersession -> clean fenced exit. Oversized transcript messages fail closed producer-side.

## Deep-review fixes (a dedicated adversarial review found real concurrency/lifecycle bugs)

- **BLOCKER fixed:** stop() during an in-flight transcript commit spun forever (100% CPU hang on SIGINT/SIGTERM) because the terminal `stopped` state was indistinguishable from a transient interrupt and the commit retry loop treated it as retryable. Introduced a terminal WorkerConnectionStoppedError; retry loops now retry only transient interruptions and rethrow on any terminal state. Stop-in-flight and post-stop emit settle promptly.
- **Blast-radius fixed:** a gateway live-event window reset (a streaming-telemetry cursor reset) used to abort the entire run including a healthy in-flight inference turn. Now: satisfiable resyncs renumber the unacked tail from the gateway's expectedSeq (the gateway explicitly tolerates renumbered replay); an unrecoverable live-seam failure degrades to lossy preview streaming while inference/transcript continue. Live events are preview; they no longer kill the turn.
- **Dead-seam removed + contract documented:** the unused in-process resumeFromBase resync was removed (leaf-only rebasing is unsafe — an unseen transcript mutation means stale inference context). On stale-base-leaf the run fail-stops with an explicit lost-tail lifecycle error and no duplicate commit; relaunch-with-fresh-context is milestone-3 (placement) territory, now documented in docs/cli/worker.md.
- **Hardening:** the worker's session write path is now a real promise-chain mutex (was a pass-through relying on an unguarded serial-emission invariant); bounded admission deadline.

## User Impact

Opt-in only; dispatch/UI (target bar, placement) is milestone 3. This makes a worker box able to run a session end-to-end. No config/changelog/version-bump changes.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox: src/worker (runtime, RPC clients, launch), gateway worker-environments, CLI command policy, lint-suppressions — 744 tests green, including the deep-review regression tests (stop-during-commit, resync-below-cursor renumber, live-seam-failure-does-not-abort, stale-base-leaf fail-stop, epoch-flip mid-inference, reconnect-mid-stream single provider call).
- Dedicated adversarial correctness review verified the hard parts correct (CAS/seq/replay dedupe, live ACK math, inference resume/no-double-bill, epoch fencing under withLock, restriction invariants) and found the bugs above, all fixed.
- Clean build (rm -rf dist): public plugin-SDK declaration graph 5,077,853/5,100,000; no [INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]. Type-aware lint, check:test-types, madge + import cycles zero, protocol:check, docs:map:check all green. Codex fresh autoreview clean.

target.title: fix: keep yielded parent runs deferred until subagents settle
target.body:
## Summary

This change promotes yielded-parent semantics into a shared parent lifecycle classifier and routes the affected cron, subagent-registry, and Discord/source-message paths through that state instead of letting each consumer infer completion from terminal-shaped model-attempt events, missing final text, or abort-shaped control flow.

The shipped behavior is:

- yielded parent + active descendants is treated as waiting/deferred, not ordinary completion;
- yielded parent + no descendant is treated as diagnostic error;
- cron delivery waits for a real final outcome instead of counting the yielded attempt as `ok / not-delivered`;
- Discord/source-message progress remains parent-owned while the yielded parent is waiting;
- descendant settlement wakes/reconciles yielded parents through the existing continuation paths.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where parent-agent runs that spawned child sessions/subagents and then called `sessions_yield` could look finished before the parent task actually completed.

The most visible failures were:

- isolated cron `agentTurn` jobs with valid delivery targets could finish as `ok / not-delivered` because the yielded parent had no final payload yet;
- Discord source-message lifecycle could clear parent progress/done indicators while child work was still active or while the parent was waiting to reconcile final output;
- run history/status surfaces made yielded parent work look like delivery failure, ordinary success with no output, or completed source-message work instead of a paused/resumable parent lifecycle.

`session_yield` is supposed to end the current model turn, not the parent task. This PR makes that distinction explicit for the affected runtime consumers.

## User Impact / Intended Outcome

Operators and developers can now rely on `sessions_yield` after spawning child/subagent work without the parent run being misrepresented as complete at the cron or Discord lifecycle boundary.

Practically:

- autonomous development crons stop inflating misleading `ok / not-delivered` results for intentionally yielded runs;
- cron history exposes a distinct `deferred` state for yielded parent handoff;
- Discord progress no longer marks the parent source message done just because the parent yielded while children continue;
- yielded parent runs are resumed/reconciled when descendant work settles;
- debugging points to the parent/child lifecycle state instead of falsely implying delivery target resolution failed.

## Linked Context

- #95535 — `sessions_yield` isolated cron resumption/delivery gap.
- #92369 — subagent orchestration in isolated cron sessions needs reliable spawn/wait/aggregate semantics.
- #92116 — `sessions_yield` completion delivered as passive context can break orchestration loops.
- #86537 — subagent terminal reconciliation can expire suspended final delivery.
- #86538 — session write-lock timeouts can block subagent delivery lanes.
- #95833 — subagent abort-settle/session-lock failure can break session continuation.
- #92460 — isolated cron completion delivery gap around final controller return.
- #95604 — Discord subagent progress visibility.
- #94153 — durable queued subagent completion announcements.
- #95847 — requester-consumed descendant completion accounting.

## What Changes

### Shared parent lifecycle state

- Adds `src/agents/agent-lifecycle-parent-state.ts`.
- Classifies lifecycle events with explicit yielded/waiting vs terminal semantics.
- Exports the classifier through `openclaw/plugin-sdk/reply-runtime`.
- Routes subagent registry and Discord source-message handling through the classifier instead of local `yielded && paused` inference.

### Cron lifecycle and delivery

- Adds first-class cron run status `deferred`.
- Classifies yielded descendant handoff before delivery-mode branching, so text, structured payloads, `delivery.mode: none`, source-satisfied delivery, and normal direct delivery all share the same semantics.
- Prevents duplicate/interim parent announcements while descendants are active.
- Records yielded-without-descendant as explicit error diagnostic.
- Keeps deferred manual task runs active rather than failing them.
- Disables one-shot deferred cron jobs after handoff to avoid retry loops.

### Persistence, protocol, CLI, and UI

- Extends run-log JSON/SQLite encoding and status filtering for `deferred`.
- Extends Gateway protocol schemas and cron server filters.
- Extends CLI status/wait typing and docs.
- Extends hook-visible status typing.
- Adds Control UI status/filter labels and generated locale fallbacks.

### Parent/subagent reconciliation

- Tracks yielded/paused parents that still have pending descendants.
- Marks yielded parents with `wakeOnDescendantSettle` so they are resumed/reconciled when descendant work settles.
- Handles child success/failure settlement through existing subagent lifecycle recovery paths.
- Adds regression coverage for yielded parents being reconciled after child failure so diagnostics can wake the parent.

### Discord/source-message lifecycle

- Projects lifecycle events from agent execution into reply/channel handling.
- Uses the shared classifier to identify yielded/waiting parent state.
- Preserves in-progress/progress representation for yielded parents with active children.
- Avoids prematurely marking Discord status reactions done or clearing draft/progress state when the parent yielded and remains waiting.

### Concurrent user-message semantics

`docs/tools/subagents.md` documents the selected policy: if a human sends another message while a requester is yielded, the new message starts a normal turn for the same requester session. OpenClaw keeps the yielded run visible as waiting on descendant completion rather than converting it into a stale final reply; when descendant completion arrives, the completion event is handed back to the requester for synthesis.

## Implementation Notes

Implementation details are included in the What Changes section above; focused evidence and live behavior proof are preserved below.

## Tests / Verification

Focused test coverage plus type, docs, and formatting gates are preserved under Evidence below.

## Evidence

### Rebase/Squash/Proof

- Common upstream base: `13ecca5408cbc94e66105608bfe770d0fc660d76` (`origin/main`, `fix(telegram): back off session init spool retries`)
- Previous PR head: `c163d18fa610687e7dfb8585f1fe8f30b0c4185d`
- Current PR head: `73cff6aa1b0a3ab5786fdfc3a96c98f575e7fcc8`
- Rebased and squashed to one commit on the common base; pushed with `--force-with-lease`.

### ClawSweeper Requested Real Behavior Proof Coverage

ClawSweeper requested redacted live behavior proof for the yielded-parent/deferred lifecycle across the surfaces touched by this PR. This body currently includes the live cron/subagent deferred handoff proof below: a real Dev-01 cron run where the yielded parent remained `deferred` while a descendant was active, with redacted run output, child completion marker, and run/shared-state checks.

Remaining ClawSweeper-requested proof not present in this body yet:

- Redacted Discord visual status/progress/status-reaction proof showing a yielded parent with active descendants remains visibly in progress until descendant settlement.
- Best-effort cron yielded handoff proof/regression after the `deliveryBestEffort` bypass fix, showing best-effort delivery does not incorrectly bypass the yielded-parent deferred lifecycle.
- Migration/upgrade compatibility proof for the detected persistent data-model/status-contract changes.

Maintainer acceptance is still needed for the public `deferred` cron/status/SDK contract; that is a review decision, not something runtime proof alone can certify.

### Real / Live Behavior Proof

target.title: fix(agents): reject invalid bundled LSP framing
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: bundled LSP stdout framing accepts numeric prefixes such as `Content-Length: 12junk`, does not reject duplicate lengths, and has no header/body size bounds.
- Solution: parse the header boundary strictly and fail the affected LSP session immediately on the first framing violation.
- What changed: one runtime parser and its focused regression tests.
- What was not changed: outbound framing, bundle discovery/configuration, LSP request payloads, tool schemas, or the general request timeout.

## What Problem This Solves

The current regex is not anchored to a complete header value and `Number.parseInt` accepts a decimal prefix. A malformed frame can therefore be cut at the wrong byte boundary; an oversized unterminated header or declared body can also remain buffered indefinitely. Subsequent JSON-RPC responses no longer align with pending request ids, so users see a misleading generic 10-second timeout instead of the framing error.

## User Impact

A broken or adversarial bundled language server can stall every pending LSP tool request in its session and retain an ever-growing buffer. After this patch, the first invalid frame rejects pending requests with a specific LSP framing error and terminates the child process, while valid frames keep completing normally.

## Origin / follow-up

- **Follows / completes:** #85341, which internalized the bundled agent LSP runtime.
- **Gap this fills:** the internalized stdio parser still partially accepts malformed `Content-Length` values and lacks framing size limits.
- **Consistency:** this keeps framing ownership and session cleanup inside `agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.ts`; no discovery or tool-contract layer is changed.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

- **Linked PR(s):** #103046.
- **Gap in linked PR(s):** it overlaps on oversized bodies but does not reject suffixed or duplicate `Content-Length` fields or bound unterminated headers.
- **Why this patch is better/canonical:** it fails at the fatal header boundary without adding cross-chunk drain state, so pending requests receive the actual error immediately.
- **Local real behavior proof advantage:** the proof drives `createBundleLspToolRuntime` through a real spawned stdio executable that emits both the invalid frame and a canonical control frame.

## Merge risk

- **Why it matters / User impact:** invalid child-process output currently becomes session stalls, retained buffers, and misleading timeouts.
- **Risk labels considered:** compatibility / session-state / availability.
- **Risk explanation:** protocol-invalid or over-limit frames that were previously partially accepted, skipped, or buffered now close the affected LSP session.
- **Why acceptable:** the intentional compatibility change is limited to invalid framing; valid chunked and multibyte frames retain the existing byte-oriented path, and both focused tests and a real subprocess control cover it.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High — RED reproduces the permissive parser, the exact-head 18-test focused suite passes in sanitized AWS Crabbox, and the changed runtime path is exercised through both a real third-party language server and a malformed real subprocess.
- **Patch quality notes:** the production diff adds a broad `JSON.parse` catch only at the untrusted frame boundary; it narrows the caught value when formatting the terminal protocol error and does not swallow it. The related open PR scan found #103046 and is documented above. Automated large-diff/session/message warnings include unrelated commits that advanced `origin/main`; the actual three-dot PR diff is two files: the LSP runtime and its test.
- **Target test file:** `src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.test.ts`.
- **Root cause:** the canonical stdout parser uses an unanchored `Content-Length` regex followed by `Number.parseInt`; because prefix parsing accepts `12junk` as `12`, the framing invariant is broken before bytes enter session state, and missing size bounds let incomplete declarations wait indefinitely.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** the change replaces the permissive framing parser at the sole stdout trust boundary, before bytes enter session state or responses reach the pending-request consumer.
- **What did NOT change:** this patch changes only bundled LSP stdout parsing and its focused tests. It does not change public API, configuration schema, outbound protocol framing, provider/channel behavior, default LSP methods, unrelated session state, docs, formatting, or lockfiles.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** `src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.ts` is the canonical owner of bundled LSP stdio framing, buffer state, pending request settlement, and child cleanup. The invariant is enforced there once rather than downstream in each LSP tool.
- **Scenario locked in:** suffixed length, duplicate length, oversized declared body, and oversized unterminated header all fail immediately; a canonical frame still completes initialize/hover.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** one parser result carries either completed messages plus remaining bytes or completed messages plus a terminal framing error; the existing session failure and process-tree cleanup functions handle the rest.

## Evidence

- **Exact PR head:** `5386f8b22bf56ecb7eb46ad390ba00e161e6ced3`.
- **Environment:** sanitized direct AWS Crabbox, Linux / Node 24.15.0, public networking, no Tailscale, no hydration, immutable `--fresh-pr openclaw/openclaw#105460` checkout.
- **Focused suite:** Crabbox run `run_55379c4d977b` passed all 18 tests in `src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.test.ts`, including manifest-registry reuse, valid `Content-Type`, colonless headers, duplicate/suffixed lengths, size bounds, chunking, request failure, and process cleanup.
- **Real third-party server:** Crabbox run `run_f805f238ea53` installed `typescript-language-server@5.3.0` with `typescript@5.9.3`, loaded it through a temporary enabled Claude bundle manifest/registry, spawned it through `createBundleLspToolRuntime`, and completed a canonical `textDocument/hover` through the resulting OpenClaw tool.
- **Malformed subprocess:** the same run loaded a second real Node child through the same bundle/runtime path. It returned a valid initialize response, then a hover response containing a colonless header line. The pending request rejected immediately with `LSP framing error: header line must contain a colon`, and the child recorded `SIGTERM`.
- **Boundary crossed:** bundle manifest/config and prepared manifest registry → embedded-agent LSP runtime → real OS process spawn → stdin JSON-RPC → stdout LSP framing → pending request settlement → process-tree termination.
- **Rebase integration:** the branch was rebased onto `origin/main` at `afb282ee682`; current main later advanced to `e9e7d385e013ef9dd0daba614a263d334f02eac0` without any intervening changes to either touched LSP file. Current-main manifest-registry plumbing remains present in the PR head.
- **Proof artifact:** the harness was temporary and uncommitted; it asserted the immutable checkout SHA before running and removed its bundle/server artifacts afterward.

```text
{
  "proof_sha": "5386f8b22bf56ecb7eb46ad390ba00e161e6ced3",
  "real_server": "typescript-language-server@5.3.0 + typescript@5.9.3",
  "canonical_hover": "completed through OpenClaw runtime",
  "malformed_header": "LSP framing error: header line must contain a colon",
  "malformed_child_termination": "SIGTERM"
}
```

- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.
- **Remaining proof gap:** no non-Linux platform was exercised.

## Review findings addressed

- **RF-001:** N/A — this is a new follow-up PR; no review findings exist on this head.

## Regression Test Plan

```bash
pnpm test src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.test.ts
```

Sanitized exact-head AWS Crabbox run `run_55379c4d977b` passed all 18 focused tests. Exact-head real behavior run `run_f805f238ea53` passed the canonical third-party-server and malformed-subprocess scenarios above.

## Risk / Compatibility

Medium compatibility/availability risk at a narrow protocol boundary. Standards-compliant positive safe `Content-Length` frames at or below 64 MiB are unchanged. Invalid values, duplicate fields, headers above 8 KiB, bodies above 64 MiB, and invalid JSON bodies now terminate only the affected bundled LSP session instead of being accepted or left pending.

## What was not changed

- Public API / schema / protocol / defaults: no outbound or public contract changes.
- Channel/provider/session/security behavior outside the fixed path: no changes.
- Unrelated cleanup, docs, formatting, lockfiles: none in the three-dot PR diff.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** the framing boundary used an unanchored regex plus prefix-tolerant integer parsing and had no header/body bounds.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** strict line parsing and size invariants are applied before bytes can alter session framing state or pending-request matching.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High — failing reproduction, exact-head focused GREEN, and exact-head real-server/malformed-subprocess proof all bind commit `5386f8b22bf56ecb7eb46ad390ba00e161e6ced3`.
- **Patch quality notes:** the change reuses existing session failure and process cleanup paths; it adds no new mutable drain/session mode and no unrelated refactor.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** the guard is located in the canonical bundled LSP stdout parser, not in downstream hover/definition tools or generic timeout handling.


Fixes #105675

target.title: fix(gateway): always enforce path containment for session transcript archive
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `archiveSessionTranscriptsDetailed` used a single `dirname(storePath)` containment root after removing the opt-in `restrictToStoreDir` flag. This dropped valid custom transcript paths (when `storePath` is undefined) and cross-agent candidate paths, breaking the existing resolver contract.

**Solution**: Replace the single-root filter with multi-root containment matching the resolver's validated candidate boundary. The archive function now accepts candidates from the store directory, sibling agent sessions directories, and the legacy global sessions directory.

**What changed**: `archiveSessionTranscriptsDetailed` now uses a `containmentRoots` array built from the same inputs as `resolveSessionTranscriptCandidates`. Each candidate is accepted if it falls under any root. 4 new regression tests cover cross-agent, no-store custom, and poisoned path scenarios. Total: 396 tests passed.

**What did NOT change**: Function signatures remain the same (callers unchanged). Existing archive behavior for normal store-path sessions is preserved. The `restrictToStoreDir` parameter is kept as a no-op for backward compatibility. No changes to the resolver (`resolveSessionTranscriptCandidates`) or path validation logic (`resolvePathWithinSessionsDir`).

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Session transcript archive containment now matches the resolver boundary, preserving custom and cross-agent paths while rejecting poisoned paths.

**Real environment tested**: Linux 4.19.112, Node 22.19.0, pnpm 11.2.2

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
npx tsx /tmp/archive-proof.mjs
```
L2 real behavior proof: direct function call with real filesystem state.

**After-fix evidence**:
```
=== Before ===
storePath: /tmp/archive-proof-XXXX/agents/main/sessions/sessions.json
store transcript exists: true
cross-agent transcript exists: true

=== 1. Normal store-path archive ===
Archived: [proof-sess-1.jsonl.reset...]  archived file exists: true

=== 2. Cross-agent archive ===
Archived: 2 candidates archived file exists: true

=== 3. No-store custom path archive ===
Archived: [custom-transcript.jsonl.reset...]  archived file exists: true

=== 4. Reject poisoned non-jsonl sessionFile ===
Archived (should be empty): []

=== 5. Reject poisoned with storePath ===
Archived count (expected 1, valid fallback): 1

=== All scenarios verified ===
```

**Observed result after the fix**: All five scenarios pass. Normal store-path, cross-agent, and no-store custom transcript archives produce the expected archive files. Poisoned `/etc/passwd` paths are rejected both with and without storePath.

**What was not tested**: The full gateway archive/reset/delete HTTP flow with a running gateway server. The containment logic is exercised at the function level with real filesystem state, which directly validates the changed surface.

## Tests and validation

| Suite | Files | Tests | Result |
|-------|-------|-------|--------|
| session-utils.fs | 4 | 396 | All passed |
| Archive-specific | 4 | 24 focused | All passed |
| session-transcript-key | 4 | 24 | All passed |

## Risk checklist

**Risk level**: Low — containment boundary widened to match existing resolver contract, no new edge cases introduced.
**Mitigation**: 4 regression tests covering cross-agent, custom path, and poisoned path scenarios; real behavior proof with filesystem state.
**merge-risk**: Low — widens (not narrows) accepted paths; any previously working path preserved.

- [x] This change preserves backward compatibility
- [x] This change has been tested — 396 tests pass
- [x] Regression tests added for cross-agent, no-store custom, and poisoned paths
- [x] Breaking changes documented in Summary — none

target.title: fix(gateway): drain root work continuations before stop process exit
target.body:
#### What Problem This Solves

Close #105697

When a gateway process receives a direct stop signal (SIGTERM/SIGINT without a restart intent), any `session_end` plugin hooks that were already started by session reset/delete/compaction may be truncated before they complete. This happens because the session is removed from the shutdown tracker synchronously before the hook fires asynchronously via `runWithGatewayIndependentRootWorkContinuation`, and the direct-stop path (`handleStopAfterServerClose`) exits the process without waiting for these continuations to settle. Affected plugins may lose database writes, memory summaries, or external resource cleanups.

#### Why This Change Was Made

The existing shutdown drain (`drainActiveSessionsForShutdown`) only covers sessions still in the active-session tracker when shutdown begins. Sessions already finalized by reset/delete/compaction are deliberately excluded to avoid double-firing. Their `session_end` hooks already run as tracked gateway root work continuations — the only gap is that the direct-stop path never waits for the root work set to drain before exiting.

Instead of changing the `emitGatewaySessionEndPluginHook` signature (which would alter latency on every normal finalization path), this fix adds a bounded drain of the existing gateway root work set to the direct-stop path, matching the approach recommended by ClawSweeper in the issue review.

The drain uses a referenced `setTimeout` poll loop (not `.unref()`) so that the polling timer keeps the Node.js event loop alive during the wait. The 2-second timeout bound and the `exitProcess(0)` fallback in the caller guarantee that a stuck hook cannot block shutdown past the supervisor stop timeout.

#### User Impact

No visible impact under normal operation. On graceful gateway stop, pending `session_end` hooks now have up to 2 seconds to complete before the process exits, reducing the chance of lost plugin finalization writes. The wait is bounded and the force-exit watchdog remains armed, so a stuck hook cannot block shutdown past the supervisor stop timeout.

#### Evidence

- **Type check:** `tsgo` passes with no errors on changed files
- **Tests:**
  ```
  $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/process/gateway-work-admission.test.ts src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.test.ts

  ✓ |unit| src/process/gateway-work-admission.test.ts (17 tests)
  ✓ |cli|  src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.test.ts (45 tests)

  Test Files  2 passed (2)
       Tests  62 passed (62)
  ```
  - `gateway-work-admission.test.ts` — 17 tests pass (+4: `waitForGatewayRootWorkDrain` success / timeout / immediate zero-count / poll-and-release)
  - `run-loop.test.ts` — 45 tests pass (+2: direct-stop drains root work before exit; warns and still exits on drain timeout; +1 mock fix)
- **Change scope:** 4 files, +116 lines
  - `src/process/gateway-work-admission.ts` — new `waitForGatewayRootWorkDrain` helper (referenced poll, no `.unref()`)
  - `src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.ts` — drain call in `handleStopAfterServerClose` before `exitProcess(0)`
  - `src/process/gateway-work-admission.test.ts` — 4 new tests for drain helper
  - `src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.test.ts` — 2 new regression tests + mock fix
  - Directory scope: `src/cli`, `src/process` — no config, CLI, SDK, docs, or changelog surface affected
- **No new dependencies** — reuses existing `getActiveGatewayRootWorkCount`
- **ClawSweeper P1 fix:** removed `.unref()` from the drain poll loop (`src/process/gateway-work-admission.ts:312`). The referenced `setTimeout` keeps the event loop alive during the bounded wait, so Node cannot exit naturally before the next poll fires. The 2-second timeout and caller's `exitProcess(0)` guarantee no infinite hang.
- **Live proof:** ran standalone script exercising `gateway-work-admission` internals under the exact race scenario:

```
=== Gateway Stop Root Work Drain — Proof Log ===

[Case 1] No pending root work — immediate return
  drain returned: true (0.1ms)
  ✓ returns true immediately
  ✓ <10ms (no busy-wait)

[Case 2] Pending session_end hook (350ms) — drain waits
  ✓ root admission acquired
  ✓ root + continuation tracked
  [0.365s] root released, 1 continuation still active
  ✓ only continuation remains
  [0.365s] SIGTERM received → starting stop drain...
  [0.715s] session_end hook: DB write complete (351ms)
  drain returned: true (353ms)
  ✓ drained before timeout
  ✓ waited for hook (~353ms >= 350ms)
  ✓ no remaining work

[Case 3] Stuck hook — timeout, warn, exit anyway
  ✓ 1 stuck continuation
  drain returned: false (200ms)
  ✓ returns false on timeout
  → gateway: warn + exitProcess(0)

[Case 4] 3 concurrent hooks (150/250/350ms) — drain waits for slowest
  ✓ 3 active hooks
  [1.071s] hook #1 done (151ms)
  [1.172s] hook #2 done (251ms)
  [1.272s] hook #3 done (351ms)
  drain returned: true (351ms)
  ✓ all drained
  ✓ waited for slowest (351ms)
  ✓ clean

=== Results: 14 passed / 0 failed ===
```

- drain blocks while hook executes (~353ms), returns true immediately after hook completes
- fast path with empty queue: returns in <1ms
- stuck hook: returns false after timeout, process still exits
- multiple concurrent hooks: waits for slowest to finish

target.title: fix(agents): tighten lsSchema.limit from Type.Number to Type.Integer
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #105827

**Problem**: `lsSchema.limit` uses `Type.Number`, which accepts fractional values (e.g. `10.5`) that are semantically invalid for an entry count. This can silently pass schema validation and reach tool logic with nonsensical values.

**Solution**: Change the schema field to `Type.Integer` so the TypeBox schema validator rejects floats before tool logic ever sees them. Export `lsSchema` from the module so tests can validate against the production schema instead of a reconstructed copy.

**What changed**: One character in `src/agents/sessions/tools/ls.ts:28` — `Type.Number` → `Type.Integer`. The test file `ls.limit-schema.test.ts` now imports the production `lsSchema` and validates both valid integers and invalid floats against it. Also exported `lsSchema` (previously module-private `const`) to enable production-schema testing.

**NOT changed**: Tool execution behavior, default limit value (500), `normalizePositiveLimit` clamping logic, any other schema field, the tool registration path, or the tool's runtime behavior. Existing `ls.test.ts` tests continue to pass unchanged.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Schema-level rejection of float `limit` values in the production `lsSchema`.
**Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node.js 25.9.0, OpenClaw `main@HEAD` with this patch applied.
**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `pnpm test src/agents/sessions/tools/ls.limit-schema.test.ts --reporter=verbose`
**After-fix evidence**: `node --import tsx/esm -e "..."` → 4/4 passed (see terminal output in Tests section)
**Observed result after the fix**: `Check(lsSchema, { limit: 10.5 })` returns `false`; `Check(lsSchema, { limit: 100 })` returns `true`. Float values are rejected at schema level.
**What was not tested**: End-to-end tool execution with mocked filesystem is covered by existing `ls.test.ts`. Real OpenClaw agent runtime integration is out of scope for this schema-level gate.

## Tests and validation

target.title: fix(clickclack): deliver media and configurable model replies [AI-assisted]
target.body:
This PR is AI-assisted. I have personally verified all code and AI was used for syntax.

## Summary

Fix two ClickClack outbound failure modes:

1. Wire the channel's existing outbound surface to ClickClack's upload and attachment APIs so local files and supported remote media are delivered instead of silently degrading to text-only messages.
2. Replace the hard-coded model-reply limit with a configurable per-account `maxTokens` setting. When unset, ClickClack now defers to the selected runtime/model default; explicit values are bounded to 1–32768.

The patch also makes durable media retries idempotent, logs model-mode completions that produce no sendable text, documents the behavior and cost/latency tradeoff, and refreshes the generated channel-config metadata.

## What Problem This Solves

The ClickClack CLI accepted `--media` and reported delivery success, but the installed outbound adapter warned that `sendMedia` was missing, dropped the media URL, and created only a text message.

Separately, `replyMode: "model"` always called `llm.complete` with `maxTokens: 96`. In a live five-agent test, all five model calls completed, but two consumed the full 96-token budget and produced no sendable reply. Only three messages reached ClickClack, with no diagnostic explaining the skipped deliveries.

The first media implementation also created a new text message and upload on every durable retry. If attachment association failed after message creation, a queue retry could therefore duplicate the visible message. This revision derives a stable ClickClack message nonce from the durable delivery intent, reconciles attachment state, and retries association once with the same message/upload pair.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [x] Refactor required for the fix
- [x] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] API / contracts
- [x] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- No linked issue; discovered through live local ClickClack/OpenClaw integration testing.
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Evidence

- Behavior or issue addressed: ClickClack media was dropped while delivery was reported as successful; model-mode replies were capped at 96 tokens and empty results were silently skipped.
- Real environment tested: local OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node v24.14.1, local ClickClack server at `127.0.0.1:18082`, five named ClickClack bot accounts.
- Before media evidence:

```text
openclaw message send --channel clickclack --account blackbird \
  --target channel:<general-channel-id> \
  --message "File delivery E2E test from OpenClaw." \
  --media /tmp/clickclack-openclaw-file-e2e.txt --json

[outbound/deliver] Plugin outbound adapter does not implement sendMedia;
media URLs will be dropped and text fallback will be used
```

- Before model-reply evidence: one `Hello` event reached all five bot connections and all five `runtime.llm` calls completed. ClickClack persisted replies from Mustang, Clipper, and Nighthawk only. Blackbird and Dragon Lady both reached the hard-coded 96-token ceiling and emitted no outbound message request.
- Exact live media verification after this patch:

```text
node --import tsx --input-type=module -e '<invoke sendClickClackMedia with the Blackbird account and local file>'
{"messageId":"msg_01kxcc9khfgxs2y9d4b0ryrdf4"}
```

```text
POST /api/uploads                         201
POST /api/channels/{channel_id}/messages 201
POST /api/messages/{message_id}/attachments 200
GET  /api/uploads/{upload_id}             200 (51 bytes)
```

The persisted row linked message `msg_01kxcc9khfgxs2y9d4b0ryrdf4`, author `Blackbird`, filename `clickclack-openclaw-file-e2e.txt`, content type `text/plain`, and byte size `51`.

Live ClickClack channel view showing Blackbird's persisted message, attachment card, filename, size, and download control:

![Live ClickClack media delivery](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jjjhenriksen/openclaw/5d8fc6089ff37ab02f0baa56089c24ba0c0f7013/docs/images/clickclack-live-media-delivery.jpg)

Live ClickClack artifact viewer showing the same 51-byte attachment opened successfully with its exact contents:

![Live ClickClack media preview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jjjhenriksen/openclaw/5d8fc6089ff37ab02f0baa56089c24ba0c0f7013/docs/images/clickclack-live-media-preview.jpg)

- Retry-safety regression proof:

```text
first attach attempt -> simulated lost response
GET /api/messages/{message_id} -> reconcile persisted attachments
bounded retry -> same message id + same upload id
durable queue retry -> same nonce-keyed message; no duplicate upload when attached
```

The focused tests assert that a lost attachment response is reconciled, a transient failure retries the same `msg_out`/`upl_1` pair, a durable retry reuses the nonce-keyed message, and two failed association attempts still reject rather than reporting false success.

- Live model-mode verification after this patch, using the same five connected accounts and the same inbound channel:

```text
configured cap  persisted replies  observed result
512             0 / 5              all five calls reached the cap; warnings emitted
4096            3 / 5              Blackbird, Dragon Lady, Nighthawk persisted
8192            5 / 5              all five replies persisted in ClickClack
unset           5 / 5              runtime/model default; all five persisted
```

The final 8192-token run persisted one reply from every account:

```text
Clipper      msg_01kxch2yfh8909y554084fkq00  89 chars
Nighthawk    msg_01kxch2zaq9gymdpdfd6yxn8bc  78 chars
Blackbird    msg_01kxch36kp7gnerg4tsyczszez  113 chars
Mustang      msg_01kxch372rc6jv726t1cd6bewd  68 chars
Dragon Lady  msg_01kxch392ka50y2rkh864c1807  87 chars
```

This demonstrates that `maxTokens` is both honored per account and intentionally configurable: the appropriate ceiling depends on the selected model's reasoning/output behavior, with higher settings trading additional latency and provider usage for completion headroom.

The final unset-account regression used the patched plugin with `maxTokens`
absent from all five account configs. ClickClack persisted one reply from every
account, and the runtime reported no empty-response warnings:

```text
Blackbird    636 output tokens   msg_01kxcm57jqckqtqpwtjwq5cj90
Clipper      667 output tokens   msg_01kxcm57m9910swmt4t0bz8z35
Dragon Lady  1116 output tokens  msg_01kxcm57veataympk64zyrqz20
Nighthawk    340 output tokens   msg_01kxcm5bph2hcp3gn5yq71wr7w
Mustang      3352 output tokens  msg_01kxcm5bzhbxfvp94erj3z3c7e
```

- Automated checks on head `0e3fead61`:

```text
./node_modules/.bin/vitest run \
  extensions/clickclack/src/inbound.test.ts \
  extensions/clickclack/src/accounts.test.ts \
  extensions/clickclack/src/outbound.test.ts \
  extensions/clickclack/src/http-client.test.ts

Test Files  4 passed (4)
Tests       52 passed (52)
```

```text
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json \
  --incremental \
  --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions-test.tsbuildinfo
```

```text
node --import tsx scripts/generate-bundled-channel-config-metadata.ts --check
node scripts/format-docs.mjs --check
git diff --check
```

## Root Cause

- Media root cause: the ClickClack channel advertised text delivery only and did not connect the shared outbound adapter to the server's upload/create/attach sequence. Core therefore dropped `mediaUrl` and used its text fallback.
- Retry root cause: media message creation had no durable idempotency key, and attachment state was not reconciled after an ambiguous failure response.
- Model-reply root cause: `dispatchModelReply` hard-coded `maxTokens: 96` and returned silently when the resulting text was empty.
- Missing detection / guardrail: no live media-delivery test verified that an attachment was persisted and retrievable, no regression covered ambiguous attachment failures, and no warning identified empty model-mode completions.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- ClickClack bots can send attachments to channels, threads, and DMs through the normal OpenClaw media path.
- Media delivery is not reported complete until the upload is durably attached to the created message.
- Durable media retries reuse a nonce-keyed message, reconcile persisted attachments, and bound association retries to the same upload/message pair.
- Files are bounded to 64 MiB and retain OpenClaw's normal local/remote media access controls.
- `replyMode: "model"` omits a ClickClack-specific cap when `maxTokens` is unset, allowing the selected runtime/model default to apply.
- Each account can set `maxTokens` from 1 to 32768.
- Empty model-mode completions produce a warning with the account id and configured token budget.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes/No`): Yes
- Config/env changes? (`Yes/No`): Yes — optional `channels.clickclack.maxTokens` and per-account `maxTokens`
- Migration needed? (`Yes/No`): No
