target.title: fix(reply): strip newline/whitespace-separated leading NO_REPLY sentinel
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #103735. Follow-up to #30916 and #30955.

When a model emits `NO_REPLY` on its own line before the real reply body:

```
NO_REPLY

Wait — the user mentioned me directly. I should respond.

Hi! How can I help?
```

…the literal `NO_REPLY` token and any interstitial reasoning text are **delivered to the channel** alongside the real reply. The sentinel should be stripped (or the entire reply suppressed if nothing substantive remains).

## Root Cause

`startsWithSilentToken` (`tokens.ts:280`) uses `getSilentLeadingAttachedRegex` which requires the token to be **glued** to a letter or number via `(?=[\p{L}\p{N}])`. A newline/whitespace-separated leading token — the most common preamble shape — is not detected as a leading sentinel, so `stripLeadingSilentToken` is never called. The `stripSilentToken` fallback only handles **trailing** tokens (`\s*$`), so the leading token survives the mixed-content branch entirely.

The punctuation safe harbour (`NO_REPLY: explanation` and `NO_REPLY -- nope`) is preserved because punctuation after a token is not a sentinel — it is natural language.

## Fix

In the mixed-content branch of `normalizeReplyPayload`, add a targeted check: when the glued-attached detection fails, test whether the leading token is separated from real content by **whitespace followed by a word character** (`\s+[\p{L}\p{N}]`). This catches `NO_REPLY\n\nWait...` and `NO_REPLY  The answer...` without affecting the punctuation safe harbour.

```typescript
// After glued-attached check fails:
else if (text.length > silentToken.length) {
  const trimmed = text.trimStart();
  const afterToken = trimmed.slice(silentToken.length);
  if (
    trimmed.toLowerCase().startsWith(silentToken.toLowerCase()) &&
    /^\s+[\p{L}\p{N}]/u.test(afterToken)
  ) {
    text = stripLeadingSilentToken(text, silentToken);
  }
}
```

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof — verified with standalone Node.js script

Run `node proof-103735-sentinel.cjs`:

```
Test                       | Old (leaks)                           | New (fixed)
Newline-separated          | "NO_REPLY\n\nWait -- user..."          | "Wait -- user..."           <- FIXED
Space-separated            | "NO_REPLY  The answer is 42."          | "The answer is 42."         <- FIXED
Tab-separated              | "NO_REPLY\tThe answer is 42."          | "The answer is 42."         <- FIXED
Nl + trailing              | "NO_REPLY\n\nHello"                    | "Hello"                     <- FIXED
Glued leading              | "The user is saying hello"             | "The user is saying hello"  (unchanged)
Colon after (keep)         | "NO_REPLY: explanation"                | "NO_REPLY: explanation"     (unchanged)
Dash after (keep)          | "NO_REPLY—note"                        | "NO_REPLY—note"             (unchanged)
Sp+punctuation (keep)      | "NO_REPLY -- nope"                     | "NO_REPLY -- nope"          (unchanged)
```

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/auto-reply/reply/normalize-reply.ts` | 12 lines added in mixed-content branch |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-utils.test.ts` | 3 new regression tests |

## New Regression Tests

| Test | Input | Expected |
|------|-------|----------|
| strips newline-separated leading NO_REPLY | `"NO_REPLY\n\nWait — …\n\nHi!"` | `"Wait — …\n\nHi!"` (no token) |
| strips leading NO_REPLY separated by spaces | `"NO_REPLY  The answer is 42."` | `"The answer is 42."` (no token) |
| suppresses when stripping leaves only whitespace | `"NO_REPLY\n\n\n  "` | `null` (silent skip) |

Existing tests continue to pass — the punctuation safe harbour (`": explanation"`, `"—note"`, `" -- nope"`) is preserved.

target.title: [codex] active-memory default to configured agents
target.body:
## Summary

- Default Active Memory to configured OpenClaw agents when `plugins.entries.active-memory.config.agents` is omitted.
- Fall back to the implicit `main` agent for minimal configs that do not define `agents.list`.
- Preserve explicit empty `config.agents: []` as no targeted agents.
- Preserve explicit non-empty `config.agents` allowlist behavior.
- Document the targeting contract in the Active Memory docs and plugin config help.

This matters because omitting `config.agents` previously normalized to an empty list, so Active Memory was disabled for every agent. The intended outcome is that operators can enable Active Memory across configured agents without maintaining a duplicated allowlist, while minimal single-agent configs still target `main`.

Out of scope: changing chat type filtering, per-session toggles, memory indexing behavior, or the memory tools used by the Active Memory sub-agent.

Review focus: whether the fallback to `agents.list[].id`, then implicit `main`, is the right default, and whether explicit empty/non-empty `config.agents` remains unchanged.

## Linked context

Closes #

Related #82528

This came from running OpenClaw with multiple Telegram topics routed to separate agents and needing Active Memory to apply consistently without copying the same agent list into plugin config.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior addressed:
  Omitting `plugins.entries.active-memory.config.agents` normalized to an empty allowlist, so Active Memory skipped every agent instead of applying to configured agents.
- Real environment tested:
  OpenClaw 2026.6.5 on a Linux host with a systemd user gateway, Telegram group topics routed to `main`, `sementes`, `cloudfarm`, and `pedro-agenda`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  Applied the equivalent runtime change locally, removed `active-memory.config.agents`, restarted `openclaw-gateway`, then checked gateway status and memory search.
- Evidence after fix:

```text
openclaw gateway status --deep
Gateway version: 2026.6.5
Runtime: running
Capability: admin-capable
```

```text
journalctl --user -u openclaw-gateway --since "3 minutes ago"
[gateway] http server listening (12 plugins: active-memory, brave, browser, canvas, codex, device-pair, file-transfer, memory-core, openai, phone-control, talk-voice, telegram; 12.1s)
```

```text
openclaw memory search --query "Pedro SeedSearch Markus" --max-results 5
0.545 memory/pendencias-grupo.md:1-21
0.516 memory/2026-03-31.md:1-37
0.453 memory/dreaming/light/2026-06-05.md:43-72
```

- Observed result after fix:
  Active Memory no longer required a hardcoded `config.agents` list to apply across configured agents.
- What was not tested:
  A fresh live Telegram command round-trip was not captured on the final PR branch.
- Proof limitations or environment constraints:
  The production server was restored to upstream behavior after proof collection, using an explicit `config.agents` list until this PR is merged upstream.
- Before evidence:
  Reading the prior plugin implementation showed `normalizePluginConfig({}).agents` became `[]`, while `isEnabledForAgent` requires `config.agents.includes(agentId)`.

## Tests and validation

Commands run:

```text
pnpm docs:list
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/active-memory/index.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm exec oxfmt --check extensions/active-memory/index.ts extensions/active-memory/index.test.ts docs/concepts/active-memory.md extensions/active-memory/openclaw.plugin.json
pnpm exec oxlint extensions/active-memory/index.ts extensions/active-memory/index.test.ts
node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs/concepts/active-memory.md
node --import tsx scripts/generate-bundled-channel-config-metadata.ts --check
node --import tsx -e "import { testing } from './extensions/active-memory/index.ts'; const cfg={agents:{list:[{id:'main'},{id:'support'}]}}; console.log(JSON.stringify({ omitted: testing.normalizePluginConfig({}, cfg).agents, empty: testing.normalizePluginConfig({agents: []}, cfg).agents, explicit: testing.normalizePluginConfig({agents:['support']}, cfg).agents, implicitMain: testing.normalizePluginConfig({}).agents }, null, 2));"
git diff --check upstream/main -- docs/concepts/active-memory.md extensions/active-memory/index.ts extensions/active-memory/index.test.ts extensions/active-memory/openclaw.plugin.json
.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode commit --commit HEAD
```

Regression coverage added:

- `defaults to all configured agents when no active-memory agent allowlist is set`
- `preserves an empty active-memory agent allowlist`
- `defaults to the implicit main agent when no agent list is configured`
- `keeps an explicit active-memory agent allowlist`

CI after the latest push:

- Pending for commit `b7e75ed8eaa7`. Prior CI was green on `fdf408d1e55464aced878f0fee85201324590de3`.

Final-head normalization proof on `b7e75ed8eaa7`:

```json
{
  "omitted": [
    "main",
    "support"
  ],
  "empty": [],
  "explicit": [
    "support"
  ],
  "implicitMain": [
    "main"
  ]
}
```

Autoreview note:

- The final commit review still flags the omitted-`agents` default as a maintainer compatibility decision. That is the intended product change in this PR and remains called out below; the explicit empty-list finding has been addressed.

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes`)

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes`)

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`No`)

Highest-risk area:

Closes #103871

## Summary

- add a read-only `review` action to `skill_workshop`
- render create proposals as the complete canonical skill that would be applied and update proposals as unified diffs
- bound previews with line-aware pagination, proposal-version binding, and explicit drift/integrity outcomes
- keep presentation portable so channels can attach “View skill” / “View diff” actions without owning Skill Workshop policy

## Problem

Approval messages currently provide only a prose summary. Operators cannot inspect the exact skill that a create proposal will install or see additions and removals in an update before approving it.

## Design and safety

The review projection lives beside Skill Workshop validation and apply semantics. The service computes one canonical read-only result; the agent tool owns bounded presentation and pagination; channels only render portable actions.

An approval prompt describes a specific proposal snapshot, so its execution is deliberately bound to the resolved proposal ID and current version. This is fail-closed: if a proposal changes while the operator is reviewing it, the old approval cannot apply the newer content. A code-site invariant now documents this coupling. Direct service, CLI, and tool calls remain Proposal-ID-only compatible because `proposal_version` is still optional outside the approval gate.

target.title: fix(cron): filter non-string env entries instead of silently deleting the entire env block
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #105433.

When a cron schedule config contains a non-string environment variable (e.g. `env: { DEBUG: true }`), the normalization function `normalizeTrimmedStringRecord` encounters the non-string value and returns `undefined`. The caller at `normalize.ts:286-293` then executes `delete next.env` — **silently discarding the entire env block**, including any valid entries alongside the invalid one.

For example, with `env: { DEBUG: true, API_KEY: "secret", PATH: "/usr/bin" }`:
- **Before**: All three entries are lost — `API_KEY` and `PATH` silently deleted
- **After**: `API_KEY` and `PATH` are preserved, only `DEBUG` is filtered out

## Root Cause

`normalizeTrimmedStringRecord` (`src/cron/normalize.ts:57-71`) uses an all-or-nothing bail-out: when any entry has a non-string value, `return undefined` discards the entire record. This is unnecessarily destructive — env entries are independent, and one bad entry should not invalidate the rest.

## Fix

Change the invalid-entry handling from bail-out to skip:

```diff
-    if (!key || val === undefined) {
-      return undefined;
-    }
+    if (!key || val === undefined) {
+      continue;
     }
+  if (entries.length === 0) {
+    return undefined;
+  }
```

Two behavioural properties preserved:
- When **all** entries are invalid → return `undefined` (trigger deletion)
- When **some** entries are valid → return only the valid ones

A secondary bug is also fixed: a blank/whitespace-only key previously caused the entire block to be discarded; it is now correctly skipped.

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/cron/normalize.ts` | Two lines changed in `normalizeTrimmedStringRecord` |
| `src/cron/normalize.test.ts` | 3 new regression tests |

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof — verified with standalone Node.js script

```
node -e verification script:
Test 1: Mixed valid/invalid env
  Input: {"DEBUG":true,"FOO":"bar","COUNT":42,"PATH":"/usr/bin"}
  Old:   undefined <- BUG: entire block deleted!
  New:   {"FOO":"bar","PATH":"/usr/bin"} <- FIX: only valid entries kept
  PASS:  YES

Test 2: All non-string values
  Old: undefined (correct: undefined = delete)
  New: undefined (correct: undefined = delete)

Test 3: All valid string values
  Old: {"FOO":"bar","PATH":"/usr/bin"} (correct: preserved)
  New: {"FOO":"bar","PATH":"/usr/bin"} (correct: preserved)

Test 4: Empty key trimming
  Old: undefined  (empty key → lost everything!)
  New: {"FOO":"bar"} (empty key correctly skipped)

Test 5: Non-object input
  Old: undefined (unchanged)
  New: undefined (unchanged)
```

### New regression tests in `normalize.test.ts`:

| Test | Scenario |
|------|----------|
| filters non-string env values instead of silently deleting the entire env block | `{ DEBUG: true, FOO: "bar", COUNT: 42, PATH: "/usr/bin" }` → `{ FOO: "bar", PATH: "/usr/bin" }` |
| deletes the entire env block when every entry is non-string | `{ DEBUG: true, COUNT: 42 }` → `env` key removed |
| preserves env when it contains only valid string values | `{ FOO: "bar", PATH: "/usr/bin" }` → preserved unchanged (no regression) |

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


target.title: fix(cron): batch pending-media snapshot in session reaper to avoid O(SxT) loop
target.body:
#### What Problem This Solves

Close #105694

Fixes an O(S × T) CPU bottleneck in the cron session reaper that blocks the Node.js event loop on each timer tick. For every cron continuation row, `sweepCronRunSessions` called `hasPendingGeneratedMediaTaskForSessionKey`, which internally performs a full sorted clone of all task records and a full scan of in-process generated-media activity. With thousands of sessions, this synchronous work saturates the main thread and causes gateway timeout / WebSocket disconnection.

#### Why This Change Was Made

Instead of changing the per-row `hasPendingGeneratedMediaTaskForSessionKey` helper (still used by the single-invocation `cron-run-continuation-cleanup` path), this adds `buildPendingGeneratedMediaSessionKeySet` — a one-shot snapshot that collects all session keys with pending generated-media work by iterating the in-process activity map once and the full task registry once. The reaper then does O(1) `Set.has()` lookups inside the loop.

Key design decisions:
- Preserves the exact `requesterSessionKey` / `ownerKey` matching contract — no semantic change, only a scan-lifting optimization
- The snapshot is deliberately conservative: session keys that the reaper never visits may still be included, which is harmless
- ClawSweeper confirmed the shape: "one canonical bulk pending-generated-media session-key snapshot that combines active in-process work with nonterminal persisted requester and owner keys"

#### User Impact

No visible impact. The cron reaper produces identical pruning decisions with strictly less CPU time per sweep.

#### Evidence

- **Type check:** `tsgo` passes with no errors
- **Tests:**
  - `task-status-access.test.ts` — 10 tests pass (+6: `buildPendingGeneratedMediaSessionKeySet` covers empty set, in-process activity, requesterSessionKey, ownerKey, terminal exclusion, non-generated-media exclusion, combined snapshot)
  - `session-reaper.test.ts` — 20 tests pass (mock updated to use `buildPendingSet`; two pending-media tests now verify correct sessionKey membership)
  - `cron-run-continuation-cleanup.test.ts` — 5 tests pass (no regression)
- **Change scope:** 5 files, +136 −5 lines
  - `src/tasks/generated-media-task-activity.ts` — new `getAllActiveGeneratedMediaSessionKeys` export
  - `src/tasks/task-status-access.ts` — new `buildPendingGeneratedMediaSessionKeySet` helper
  - `src/cron/session-reaper.ts` — one snapshot call before the loop, `Set.has()` per row
  - `src/tasks/task-status-access.test.ts` — 6 new tests
  - `src/cron/session-reaper.test.ts` — mock updated for new function
  - No config, CLI, SDK, docs, or changelog surface affected
- **No new dependencies** — reuses existing `listTaskRecords`, `getActiveGeneratedMediaTasks`, `isTerminalTaskStatus`
- **Live proof:** standalone simulation at realistic scale (direct `node --import tsx`):

```
=== Session Reaper Batch Snapshot — Proof ===

[Case 1] Correctness — old and new produce identical results
  old: 50 pending (0.7ms, 50 listTaskRecords calls)
  new: 50 pending (0.4ms, 1 listTaskRecords call)
  ✓ identical results for all 50 sessions
  ✓ pending key sets match exactly

[Case 2] Performance scaling — O(S×T) vs O(T+S)
  scale: 500 sessions × 1000 tasks
  old: 13.6ms — 500 full task-list scans (clone+sort each)
  new: 0.5ms — 1 full task-list scan + 500 Set.has() lookups
  speedup: 27.2x
  ✓ identical results at scale (500 × 1000)
  ✓ old: 500 listTaskRecords calls
  ✓ new approach is faster
  real clone cost: old=500,000 element copies
  real clone cost: new=1,000 element copies

[Case 3] requesterSessionKey + ownerKey contract preserved
  pending: [owner-x, req-a, req-b]
  ✓ requesterSessionKey captured
  ✓ ownerKey captured (different from requester)
  ✓ requester == owner still captured
  ✓ chat task excluded (non-generated-media)
  ✓ terminal task excluded
  ✓ all 5 session keys match

[Case 4] Empty world — snapshot is empty set
  ✓ empty when no tasks or active media

[Case 5] Worst-case — every session has continuation, none have pending media
  1000 sessions, every one has continuation but 0 have pending media
  old: 0.4ms (1000 listTaskRecords calls)
  new: 0.2ms (1 listTaskRecords call, snap size=1)
  ✓ all 1000 sessions match
  ✓ old path: 1000 listTaskRecords calls
  speedup: 2.0x

=== Results: 18 passed / 0 failed ===
```

- In the real `listTaskRecords`, each call also performs a `toSorted(compareTasksNewestFirst)` — the old path does 500 sorts, the new path does 1. The simulation captures the essential O(S×T) → O(T+S) transition; real-world speedup is larger at scale.
- **Performance:** sweep goes from O(S × (T + M)) to O(T + M + S) where S = session rows, T = persisted tasks, M = active in-process media entries

## What Problem This Solves

Nostr profile imports could mutate config before the user reviewed relay data. While an import was pending, a same-field edit could be overwritten by the response. Cancel could close the form while a server-side merge still persisted.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Control UI now requests `autoMerge: false`, treats relay data as a draft, locks profile controls while importing, and aborts/invalidate imports on Cancel, disconnect, or form replacement. Late responses cannot update a hidden or newer form. Explicit **Save & Publish** remains the write path.

The existing HTTP contract is preserved: callers that explicitly send `autoMerge: true` retain server-side merge and persistence. Only the Control UI opts into draft mode.

## User Impact

Imported values fill the open form for review. Users can edit and explicitly publish them; Cancel cannot hide a persisted mutation, and stale responses cannot replace a newer form.

## Evidence

### Real Control UI + relay/browser proof

A standalone Chromium run drove the actual Control UI. Its import request was forwarded to the actual `createNostrProfileHttpHandler`, which queried the public relay `wss://nos.lol`. The server held the response until after the browser clicked Cancel; completion then produced no config write. The browser reopened the form and verified the local value remained, then exercised **Save & Publish** and observed the expected PUT and success UI.

Redacted output:

```json
{
  "browser": "Chromium",
  "relay": "wss://nos.lol",
  "pubkeyPrefix": "c938f0bd…",
  "relayPublish": "accepted",
  "pendingImport": { "browserRequest": { "autoMerge": false }, "fieldsDisabled": true },
  "cancel": {
    "clientAction": "Cancel",
    "serverCompletedAfterCancel": true,
    "serverPersistenceCalls": 0,
    "persistedProfile": { "name": "local" },
    "formValueAfterReopen": "local",
    "requestWasDelayedUntilCancel": true
  },
  "saveAndPublish": {
    "requestMethod": "PUT",
    "requestBody": { "name": "saved-draft" },
    "uiSuccess": true
  }
}
```

The run generated pending-import, after-Cancel/reopen, and after-Save screenshots plus a Chromium WebM recording under `.artifacts/control-ui-e2e/nostr-live-proof/`. The browser run was against the same implementation before the final rebases; those rebases only added current-main commits outside this PR’s changed paths.

### CI/base diagnosis and focused validation

- The earlier Apple i18n failure (`checks-node-compact-small-2`, run `29220125349`) was on old base `f26793ca54`; the PR never touched `apps/ios/Sources/Design/SettingsProTabSections.swift`. Current main contains the wrapper fix, and the later exact-head run passed that shard.
- Exact-head run `29220974456` identified the branch-specific guard failure: `ui/src/pages/channels/channels-page.ts` grew from 514 to 538 lines. This follow-up splits page-local Nostr helpers into `nostr-profile-operation.ts`, leaves the page at 497 lines, and removes its obsolete LOC baseline entry.
- The same exact-head run’s dependency failure listed only existing `src/agents/*` and `src/gateway/*` unused-export ratchet entries; no changed PR path was listed. Current-main CI independently reported the same dependency/guard job failures.
- Final sync base: `156f4c89ed0325049c6d83968d5a76c59ee7ff6d`.
- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node_modules/.bin/vitest run extensions/nostr/src/nostr-profile-http.test.ts extensions/nostr/src/nostr-profile-import.test.ts` — 34 tests passed.
- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node_modules/.bin/vitest run ui/src/pages/channels/channels-page.test.ts ui/src/pages/channels/view.test.ts` — 14 tests passed.
- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/nostr-profile-import.e2e.test.ts` — 1 Playwright test passed.
- Scoped `oxfmt` and `oxlint` passed for the changed UI and Nostr files.

## Limitations

The browser Save & Publish evidence uses the UI’s PUT request with a deterministic successful response; it does not claim a live publish from a running Nostr bus. The HTTP persistence path remains covered by focused handler tests. The live import/Cancel path uses a public relay and the actual HTTP handler in a real local HTTP runtime.

Crabbox was attempted but unavailable for this run: AWS had no usable credential/instance role, and the DigitalOcean provider required `DIGITALOCEAN_TOKEN` in the environment. No token was copied from chat and no remote lease was created; provider: local Chromium/direct local fallback, lease: N/A.

target.title: fix(agents): strip runtime stream-boundary markers from user-visible text
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #105113: runtime stream-boundary markers `[e~[` / `[e[` / `[1]` leak into user-visible channel deliveries.

When a tool-using assistant reply passes through the final channel delivery boundary, some streaming transports inject internal delimiters that the existing sanitizer pipeline does not strip — the markers reach the user as visible noise appended to the end of each message.

## Root Cause

The `sanitizeUserFacingText` pipeline strips `<tool_call>`, `<function_calls>`, `<system-reminder>`, MiniMax tool XML, legacy bracket blocks, and several other internal scaffolding patterns. However, it does **not** cover runtime stream-boundary markers (`[e~[`, `[e[`, `[1]`), which are functionally analogous to SSE `[DONE]`. These markers are injected at the transport layer and survive all existing strip stages.

The existing `stripMinimaxToolCallXml` handles MiniMax `<invoke>` and `<minimax:tool_call>` XML, but the `[e~[` marker is a separate pattern from a different layer of the stack.

## Fix

Add `stripRuntimeStreamMarkers` to the `sanitizeUserFacingText` pipeline. The function strips three patterns:

- `[e~[` / `[e[` — stream boundary marker (SSE `[DONE]` analog)
- Trailing `[1]` — compact marker after the boundary (only at end of text)
- Trailing lone `[` after whitespace — truncated marker fragment

Inline `[1]` references ("See [1] for details") are **preserved** — only a trailing `[1]` at the very end of the text is stripped, matching the "compact marker trailing the boundary" pattern from the issue report.

## Files Changed

- `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/sanitize-user-facing-text.ts` — new `stripRuntimeStreamMarkers` function + call in pipeline
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers.sanitizeuserfacingtext.test.ts` — 3 new regression tests

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof — stream markers stripped from user-visible text

```
BEFORE: "Hello, how can I help?[e~["
BEFORE: "Done.[1]"
BEFORE: "Partial reply ["

AFTER:  "Hello, how can I help?"
AFTER:  "Done."
AFTER:  "Partial reply"

KEEP:   "See [1] and [2] for details"   (inline references preserved)
```

### Vitest

New regression tests:

- strips runtime stream-boundary markers: `"Hello[e~["` → `"Hello"`
- strips compact markers trailing the boundary: `"Done.[1]"` → `"Done."`
- preserves inline `[1]` references: `"See [1] and [2]"` → unchanged

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

```json
  "environment": "macOS arm64 + Homebrew Tailscale 1.98.8 + real authorized tailscaled",
  "cycles": [
```

target.title: fix(memory-lancedb): make table initialization atomic
target.body:
Closes #105680

## What Problem This Solves

The bundled LanceDB memory plugin checked whether the `memories` table existed and then created it in a separate operation. Two OpenClaw processes initializing the same database could both observe the table as absent, race during creation, and fail startup with a missing-table or duplicate-create error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing fast path for an already-present table, but make the absent-table path use LanceDB's atomic `existOk` create mode. LanceDB 0.30.0 owns the cross-process creation contract, so this avoids adding a separate filesystem lock and keeps schema-row cleanup idempotent.

The new regression test starts six independent Node processes against one fresh LanceDB directory and requires every process to complete initialization successfully. The same test fails against the previous implementation with a Lance table creation/open race.

## User Impact

Gateway and worker processes can initialize the same memory-lancedb store concurrently without intermittent startup failures or index-directory races.

## Evidence

- Before fix: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-lancedb/memory-lancedb.concurrent.test.ts` fails with a concurrent Lance table initialization error.
- After fix: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-lancedb/index.test.ts extensions/memory-lancedb/memory-lancedb.concurrent.test.ts` — 126 tests passed.

target.title: fix(msteams): reset sessions on app removal lifecycle
target.body:
Closes #99054

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Microsoft Teams users who remove a personal app/bot and later add it again can continue the same OpenClaw server-side DM session, allowing the bot to use prior conversation context after an app lifecycle boundary.

This targets Teams app-management lifecycle signals that the bot can actually observe. Live capture showed Teams' local "Remove chat history" action can arrive later as an ordinary message in the same personal `conversation.id`, with no `installationUpdate`, `conversationUpdate`, `membersAdded`, or `membersRemoved` activity. This PR does not claim to detect that fully local clear-chat action when Teams gives the bot no lifecycle or conversation-boundary signal.

## Why This Change Was Made

Teams now routes `installationUpdate` removal activities and bot `membersRemoved` conversation updates into a lifecycle handler. On a removal boundary, the handler removes the cached Teams conversation reference, rotates the matching OpenClaw session entry to a new session id with `updatedAt: 0`, and clears provider-owned route/delivery/origin metadata so the next inbound message cannot resume the removed chat transcript.

The handler also treats a personal `installationUpdate action=add` as a reinstall boundary only when an existing route-matched Teams DM session is already active. That catches tenants or flows where the re-add signal is visible but the prior remove signal was missed, without resetting first-time installs. Finally, inbound personal DMs check for a stored same-user/same-bot conversation reference with a different Teams `conversation.id`; when Teams exposes that boundary, OpenClaw removes the previous reference and rotates the DM session.

## User Impact

After a true Teams app removal and re-add, the next inbound message starts from a fresh OpenClaw session instead of silently resuming prior DM or channel context. Operators also avoid retaining a cached proactive-send reference for the removed Teams conversation.

For Teams clear-chat/reopen flows, the patch protects the observable case where Teams gives the bot a new personal conversation id. If Teams reuses the same server-side conversation id and sends no lifecycle event, there is no bot-visible signal in the captured payloads; that remains a Teams platform limitation rather than a claim made by this PR.

Existing welcome-card behavior, normal messages, reactions, and unrelated lifecycle events are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Live corrected Dale smoke:
  - Baseline before app removal used a synthetic marker.
  - Teams app removal emitted `installationUpdate action=remove`.
  - Handler logged `msteams lifecycle remove handled`, `reason=installation-remove`, `conversationType=personal`, `conversationRemoved=true`, `sessionsReset=1`.
  - The session entry rotated to a new redacted session id with `updatedAt: 0` and no Teams route/delivery/origin metadata.
  - After re-add, Teams showed the welcome card and the verification prompt used a fresh session; the bot did not recall the pre-removal marker.
- Live Teams `Remove chat history` follow-up after deploying this branch:
  - Sent a synthetic pre-clear marker.
  - Used Teams `Remove chat history`, opened the app/chat again, and sent a verification prompt.
  - No `installationUpdate add`, lifecycle/remove activity, or DM conversation-boundary handler log appeared.
  - The same OpenClaw session id remained active, and the bot could recall the pre-clear marker.
  - This confirms the PR should not claim to fix Teams local clear-history behavior when Teams sends no lifecycle event and reuses the same server-side conversation id.
- Added regression coverage for:
  - personal `installationUpdate/remove`
  - personal `installationUpdate/remove-upgrade`
  - first-install `installationUpdate/add` with no active session
  - personal `installationUpdate/add` when an existing session is active
  - ignored channel `installationUpdate/add`
  - channel bot `membersRemoved`
  - ignored non-bot `membersRemoved`
  - race-safe session rotation
  - personal DM conversation-id boundary rotation
  - no rotation for matching personal conversation ids
  - no rotation for different stored bot ids
- Added monitor-level coverage proving the Teams activity shim dispatches `installationUpdate` and `membersRemoved` activities to registered lifecycle handlers.
- Validation:
  - `pnpm test extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/lifecycle-handler.test.ts` - 11 tests passed.
  - `pnpm test extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/message-handler.authz.test.ts` - 18 tests passed.
  - `pnpm test extensions/msteams` - 71 files passed, 1007 tests passed.
  - `pnpm run lint:extensions:bundled` - passed.
  - `pnpm format:check extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/lifecycle-handler.ts extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/lifecycle-handler.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/message-handler.ts` - passed.
  - `git diff --check` - passed.



---

Migration note: This PR replaces #100371 with the same published head commit, moved from `spinen/openclaw` to `jimmypuckett/openclaw` so OpenClaw maintainers and repository automation can update the contribution without transferring authorship. Prior review, proof, and CI history remain available on #100371.

target.title: fix(memory): backfill provider.model with resolved model name
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a memory embedding adapter returns an empty `provider.model` (because the user did not explicitly configure a model, leaving it to `adapter.defaultModel`), the downstream memory identity, `providerKey`, chunk model tags, and vector search filters all see `""` instead of the resolved model name. This causes persistent `Dirty` index state and broken vector search (`WHERE c.model = ''` returns zero rows), reported as issue #90042.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `createWithAdapter` function already resolves the model via `resolveProviderModel(adapter, options.model)` and passes it into `adapter.create(...)`. But the returned `result.provider.model` can be empty if the adapter itself returns an empty string — the resolved model is discarded after `create` returnscars, leaving downstream consumers with no fallback.

The fix is a single-line backfill at the return site: `result.provider.model || resolvedModel`. This is a *runtime backfill*, not a persisted-data migration.

## Behavior Matrix

| Scenario | result.provider.model | adapter.defaultModel (resolvedModel) | Before | After | Changed? |
|----------|----------------------|--------------------------------------|--------|-------|----------|
| User explicitly sets model | `"qwen3-8b"` | irrelevant | `"qwen3-8b"` | `"qwen3-8b"` (short-circuit `\|\|`) | ❌ No |
| User leaves empty, adapter has default | `""` | `"text-embedding-3-small"` | `""` (bug) | `"text-embedding-3-small"` | ✅ Fix |
| User leaves empty, adapter has no default | `""` | `""` | `""` | `""` (`"" \|\| ""` = `""`) | ❌ No |
| User leaves empty, provider returns correct model | `"ada-002"` | irrelevant | `"ada-002"` | `"ada-002"` (short-circuit `\|\|`) | ❌ No |

Only scenario 2 changes, which is the exact bug from issue #90042.

## User Impact

Transparent for correct configurations (scenarios 1, 3, 4 — zero change). Users who saw a persistent `Dirty` index due to an empty `provider.model` will find their vector search working again after upgrade. No migration or reindex needed.

## Real Behavior Proof

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node v24.13.1, upstream/main

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
node --import tsx --input-type=module -e "
import { createEmbeddingProvider } from './extensions/memory-core/src/memory/embeddings.ts';

// Scenario 1: Explicit model + live embedding via ZTE MaaS endpoint
const r1 = await createEmbeddingProvider({
  provider: 'openai-compatible',
  model: 'Qwen3-Embedding-8B',
  config: { models: { providers: { 'openai-compatible': { api: 'openai', baseUrl: '<redacted>', apiKey: '<redacted>' } } } },
  remote: { baseUrl: '<redacted>', apiKey: '<redacted>' },
});
console.log('Explicit model provider.model:', JSON.stringify(r1.provider?.model));
const vec = await r1.provider?.embedQuery?.('hello world');
console.log('embedQuery dims:', vec?.length);

// Scenario 2: No explicit model — backfill from adapter.defaultModel
const r2 = await createEmbeddingProvider({
  provider: 'openai',
  model: '',
  config: { models: { providers: { openai: { api: 'openai', baseUrl: '<redacted>', apiKey: '<redacted>' } } } },
  remote: { baseUrl: '<redacted>', apiKey: '<redacted>' },
});
console.log('Empty model provider.model (backfilled):', JSON.stringify(r2.provider?.model));
"
```

**Evidence after fix**:

```
Explicit model provider.model: "Qwen3-Embedding-8B"
embedQuery dims: 4096
Empty model provider.model (backfilled): "text-embedding-3-small"
```

**Observed result after fix**: Explicit model → `provider.model` matches. Empty model → `provider.model` backfilled from `adapter.defaultModel` (`"text-embedding-3-small"`). On upstream/main (without this patch), scenario 2 returns `""`.

**What was not tested**: Full `openclaw memory index --force` reindex through the gateway (requires full workspace setup). The proof covers the production `createEmbeddingProvider` → `embedQuery` code path with a real embedding endpoint, which is the exact code path changed by this PR.

Supersedes #91660 (31 days old, merge conflicts, larger diff with unrelated deletions). This branch is based on latest upstream/main with a focused +5/-2 diff.

target.title: fix(block-reply): flush buffered text in coalescer stop() to prevent silent message loss
target.body:
## Summary 📌

The block-reply coalescer's `stop()` silently dropped buffered sub-minChars text instead of delivering it, causing Telegram DM replies to lose their final tail. `stop()` now synchronously delivers any buffered text before clearing the timer.

- Problem: `coalescer.stop()` only called `clearIdleTimer()`, discarding any buffered text that hadn't reached `minChars`. Agent-runner line 2630 calls `stop()` without a prior `flush({force:true})`, so the final text tail in a long reply was silently dropped with no error or log.
- Solution: Make `stop()` synchronously construct and deliver the buffered payload (fire-and-forget via `void onFlush(...)`) before clearing the buffer, guarded by `shouldAbort()` to avoid delivering during an active abort.
- What changed: `src/auto-reply/reply/block-reply-coalescer.ts` (new `deliverBufferedBeforeStop` helper preserving all 7 buffered visibility flags including `isCommentary`, `stop` now points to it), `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-utils.test.ts` (4 regression tests), `src/auto-reply/reply/block-reply-pipeline.test.ts` (2 pipeline-level stop-delivery tests)
- What did NOT change: `flush()` logic, `enqueue()` logic, `shouldAbort()` behavior inside `flush()`, pipeline-level `flush`/`stop` ordering, `BlockStreamingCoalesceSchema` config surface, `flushOnEnqueue` exposure (tracked separately in #102580). All 7 buffered visibility flags (`isReasoning`, `isCommentary`, `isCompactionNotice`, `isFallbackNotice`, `isStatusNotice`, `replyToId`, `audioAsVoice`) are preserved in the stop() payload, matching `flush()` parity.

## Change Type (select all) 📌

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all) 📌

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR 📌

- Related to #102578
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation 📌

With block streaming enabled, the tail of a long assistant reply in a Telegram DM was silently dropped (never sent, no error logged). The coalescer supports `stop()` callers that don't force-flush first (agent-runner line 2630 in recovery/error paths), but `stop()` only cleared the idle timer without delivering buffered text.

The reporter confirmed 2 occurrences on 2026-07-09 with OpenClaw 2026.6.11, and both the issue reporter and ClawSweeper traced the root cause to the coalescer's `stop()` implementation.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs) 📌

- Behavior addressed: `coalescer.stop()` silently drops buffered sub-minChars text instead of delivering it
- Real environment tested: Ubuntu 24.04 (Linux x64), Node 22.19, branch `fix/block-coalescer-stop-flush-102578`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/reply-utils.test.ts --run
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/block-reply-pipeline.test.ts --run
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-payloads.test.ts --run
```

- Evidence after fix:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/reply-utils.test.ts --run
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  81 passed (81)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/block-reply-pipeline.test.ts --run
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  28 passed (28)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-payloads.test.ts --run
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  68 passed (68)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/ --run
Test Files  9 passed (9)
     Tests  176 passed (176)
```

New regression tests (6 tests across 2 files):

| Test case | File | Input | Expected |
|-----------|------|-------|----------|
| `stop() delivers buffered sub-minChars text` | reply-utils | enqueue 26-char text, minChars=800, stop() | text delivered |
| `stop() does not deliver when shouldAbort()=true` | reply-utils | enqueue text, set aborted=true, stop() | nothing delivered |
| `stop() after force-flush is idempotent` | reply-utils | enqueue 2 texts, flush({force:true}), stop() | exactly 1 delivery |
| `stop() preserves isCommentary` | reply-utils | enqueue commentary text, stop() | isCommentary=true preserved |
| `stop() delivers sub-minChars at pipeline level` | block-reply-pipeline | enqueue text below minChars, pipeline.stop() | text delivered via onBlockReply |
| `stop() flushes multiple coalesced chunks` | block-reply-pipeline | enqueue 3 small chunks, pipeline.stop() | all 3 coalesced and delivered |

- Observed result after fix:
  1. `stop()` now delivers buffered text that was previously silently dropped
  2. `stop()` correctly skips delivery when `shouldAbort()` returns true
  3. `stop()` after a prior `flush({force:true})` is idempotent — no double delivery
  4. `stop()` preserves `isCommentary` so commentary suppression gates still apply
  5. Pipeline-level `stop()` without prior force-flush delivers buffered text through `onBlockReply`
  6. All 176 existing + new tests continue to pass across 3 test suites

- What was not tested: Real Telegram DM block-streaming end-to-end with a gateway instance (requires Crabbox + Telegram bot setup)

## Root Cause

`createBlockReplyCoalescer.stop()` was defined as `() => clearIdleTimer()`. It cleared the idle timer but did not deliver any buffered text. The main agent runner has two stop paths:

| Call site | Code | Safe? |
|-----------|------|-------|
| agent-runner:1803-1805 | `await flush({force:true}); stop()` | ✅ force-flush first |
| agent-runner:2630 | `stop()` only | ❌ buffered text dropped |

The recovery/error path at line 2630 calls `stop()` without a prior force-flush, silently dropping any buffered sub-minChars tail.

**Provenance**: `introduced by` fd15704c775 (Peter Steinberger, 2026-01-09) — original coalescer implementation. **Confidence**: clear.

## Regression Test Plan

6 new regression tests across 2 files cover:
- stop() delivers buffered text (regression for the exact reported bug)
- stop() respects abort state (safety guard)
- stop() after force-flush is idempotent (no double-delivery for the normal path)
- stop() preserves isCommentary (commentary suppression gates still apply)
- Pipeline-level stop() without prior force-flush delivers buffered text
- Pipeline-level stop() flushes multiple coalesced chunks

## User-visible / Behavior Changes 📌

Telegram DM users with `streaming.mode="block"`: long multi-paragraph replies now deliver the complete text including the final tail. Previously the last ~300–600 chars could be silently dropped.

## Security Impact (required) 📌

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Ubuntu 24.04 (Linux x64)
- Runtime/container: Node 22.19
- Model/provider: N/A (coalescer-level fix, model-independent)
- Integration/channel: Telegram (block streaming mode)
- Relevant config (redacted): `channels.telegram.streaming.mode = "block"`

### Steps

1. Configure Telegram channel with `streaming.mode = "block"`
2. Trigger a long multi-paragraph DM reply (e.g., ask for a detailed explanation)
3. Observe the final text tail arrives complete (previously dropped)

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [ ] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required) 📌

- Verified scenarios: 6 new regression tests passing (coalescer + pipeline level), all 176 existing tests passing
- Edge cases checked: abort guard, idempotent after force-flush, minChars threshold, isCommentary preservation, multi-chunk coalescing

## Compatibility / Migration 📌

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict 📌

- **Best fix**: Yes. Fixing `stop()` at the coalescer level covers ALL callers (both the safe path at 1805 and the unsafe path at 2630) without requiring each call site to remember to force-flush first.
- **Refactor needed**: No. The coalescer is 252 lines and well-scoped; the fix reuses existing helpers (`copyReplyPayloadMetadata`, `resetBuffer`, `onFlush`) and follows existing fire-and-forget patterns (`void onFlush(...)`).
- **Alternative considered**:
  1. Change line 2630 to add `await flush({force:true})` before `stop()` — rejected because it only fixes one call site; the coalescer invariant "stop may drop text" remains a footgun
  2. Expose `flushOnEnqueue` in `BlockStreamingCoalesceSchema` — tracked separately in #102580; not a fix for the existing loss path

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude (via open-source-pr skill) <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Analyzed issue #102578, traced root cause to `stop: () => clearIdleTimer()` at block-reply-coalescer.ts:224, implemented `deliverBufferedBeforeStop` to synchronously flush buffered text

## Risks and Mitigations 📌

**Highest Risk Area**: `stop()` is called from multiple paths (normal finalization, error recovery, agent cleanup). A synchronous `onFlush` call could theoretically trigger downstream errors that were previously silent.

**Mitigation Methods**: The flush is fire-and-forget (`void onFlush(...)`) — errors in the async delivery are handled by the transport layer, same as every other `void flush()` / `void onFlush()` call in the coalescer (6 existing call sites). The `shouldAbort()` guard prevents delivery during an active abort. The payload construction is the same shape used in `flush()` (lines 90-98).

**Compatibility**: Fully backward compatible. The change only affects the case where `stop()` is called with buffered text — previously the text was silently dropped, now it's delivered. All other paths are unchanged.

---

Related to #102578

target.title: improve(control-ui): compress and cache bundled assets
target.body:
Related: #105889

## What Problem This Solves

Operators loading the bundled Control UI transfer uncompressed HTML, JavaScript, and CSS, then revalidate fingerprinted bundles on repeat loads.

## Why This Change Was Made

Vite now emits Brotli and gzip sidecars after every bundle rewrite, and `ui:build` verifies that every sidecar expands to the exact final asset. The Gateway safely negotiates those sidecars without request-time compression, while only package-proven bundled Vite assets receive immutable caching. Rewritten HTML uses a bounded four-entry compression cache; HTML, public files, and configured roots retain `no-cache`, and configured `.br`/`.gz` files remain directly accessible.

AI-assisted: implemented and reviewed with Codex; I understand the resulting build artifact, Gateway negotiation, and cache boundaries.

## User Impact

The bundled Control UI transfers substantially fewer bytes on cold loads, avoids request-time compression CPU for large static assets, and reuses fingerprinted assets without revalidation on repeat loads. Existing configured UI roots retain their current behavior.

## Evidence

- Exact-head focused proof: 388 Gateway, 16 Vite-config, and 11 prepack tests passed (415 total).

target.title: fix(gateway): drain root work continuations before stop process exit
target.body:
#### What Problem This Solves

Close #105697

When a gateway process receives a direct stop signal (SIGTERM/SIGINT without a restart intent), any `session_end` plugin hooks that were already started by session reset/delete/compaction may be truncated before they complete. This happens because the session is removed from the shutdown tracker synchronously before the hook fires asynchronously via `runWithGatewayIndependentRootWorkContinuation`, and the direct-stop path (`handleStopAfterServerClose`) exits the process without waiting for these continuations to settle. Affected plugins may lose database writes, memory summaries, or external resource cleanups.

#### Why This Change Was Made

The existing shutdown drain (`drainActiveSessionsForShutdown`) only covers sessions still in the active-session tracker when shutdown begins. Sessions already finalized by reset/delete/compaction are deliberately excluded to avoid double-firing. Their `session_end` hooks already run as tracked gateway root work continuations — the only gap is that the direct-stop path never waits for the root work set to drain before exiting.

Instead of changing the `emitGatewaySessionEndPluginHook` signature (which would alter latency on every normal finalization path), this fix adds a bounded drain of the existing gateway root work set to the direct-stop path, matching the approach recommended by ClawSweeper in the issue review.

The drain uses a referenced `setTimeout` poll loop (not `.unref()`) so that the polling timer keeps the Node.js event loop alive during the wait. The 2-second timeout bound and the `exitProcess(0)` fallback in the caller guarantee that a stuck hook cannot block shutdown past the supervisor stop timeout.

#### User Impact

No visible impact under normal operation. On graceful gateway stop, pending `session_end` hooks now have up to 2 seconds to complete before the process exits, reducing the chance of lost plugin finalization writes. The wait is bounded and the force-exit watchdog remains armed, so a stuck hook cannot block shutdown past the supervisor stop timeout.

#### Evidence

- **Type check:** `tsgo` passes with no errors on changed files
- **Tests:**
  ```
  $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/process/gateway-work-admission.test.ts src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.test.ts

  ✓ |unit| src/process/gateway-work-admission.test.ts (17 tests)
  ✓ |cli|  src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.test.ts (45 tests)

  Test Files  2 passed (2)
       Tests  62 passed (62)
  ```
  - `gateway-work-admission.test.ts` — 17 tests pass (+4: `waitForGatewayRootWorkDrain` success / timeout / immediate zero-count / poll-and-release)
  - `run-loop.test.ts` — 45 tests pass (+2: direct-stop drains root work before exit; warns and still exits on drain timeout; +1 mock fix)
- **Change scope:** 4 files, +116 lines
  - `src/process/gateway-work-admission.ts` — new `waitForGatewayRootWorkDrain` helper (referenced poll, no `.unref()`)
  - `src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.ts` — drain call in `handleStopAfterServerClose` before `exitProcess(0)`
  - `src/process/gateway-work-admission.test.ts` — 4 new tests for drain helper
  - `src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.test.ts` — 2 new regression tests + mock fix
  - Directory scope: `src/cli`, `src/process` — no config, CLI, SDK, docs, or changelog surface affected
- **No new dependencies** — reuses existing `getActiveGatewayRootWorkCount`
- **ClawSweeper P1 fix:** removed `.unref()` from the drain poll loop (`src/process/gateway-work-admission.ts:312`). The referenced `setTimeout` keeps the event loop alive during the bounded wait, so Node cannot exit naturally before the next poll fires. The 2-second timeout and caller's `exitProcess(0)` guarantee no infinite hang.
- **Live proof:** ran standalone script exercising `gateway-work-admission` internals under the exact race scenario:

```
=== Gateway Stop Root Work Drain — Proof Log ===

[Case 1] No pending root work — immediate return
  drain returned: true (0.1ms)
  ✓ returns true immediately
  ✓ <10ms (no busy-wait)

[Case 2] Pending session_end hook (350ms) — drain waits
  ✓ root admission acquired
  ✓ root + continuation tracked
  [0.365s] root released, 1 continuation still active
  ✓ only continuation remains
  [0.365s] SIGTERM received → starting stop drain...
  [0.715s] session_end hook: DB write complete (351ms)
  drain returned: true (353ms)
  ✓ drained before timeout
  ✓ waited for hook (~353ms >= 350ms)
  ✓ no remaining work

[Case 3] Stuck hook — timeout, warn, exit anyway
  ✓ 1 stuck continuation
  drain returned: false (200ms)
  ✓ returns false on timeout
  → gateway: warn + exitProcess(0)

[Case 4] 3 concurrent hooks (150/250/350ms) — drain waits for slowest
  ✓ 3 active hooks
  [1.071s] hook #1 done (151ms)
  [1.172s] hook #2 done (251ms)
  [1.272s] hook #3 done (351ms)
  drain returned: true (351ms)
  ✓ all drained
  ✓ waited for slowest (351ms)
  ✓ clean

=== Results: 14 passed / 0 failed ===
```

- drain blocks while hook executes (~353ms), returns true immediately after hook completes
- fast path with empty queue: returns in <1ms
- stuck hook: returns false after timeout, process still exits
- multiple concurrent hooks: waits for slowest to finish

target.title: Workspaces: add persistent notes widget
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Workspaces had persistent per-widget state after #101329, but no trusted built-in editor that used the contract safely. The legacy Notes implementation targeted the removed dashboard stack and could overwrite edits during hydration or write without a loaded concurrency version.

## Why This Change Was Made

This stacked rebuild adds `builtin:notes` to the current Workspaces registry and consumes the recovered widget-state contract through a trusted per-widget accessor. Every save uses optimistic concurrency, missing versions never degrade to unguarded writes, early edits queue until hydration completes, and conflicts surface visibly. Debounced writes are canceled on disconnect/unmount; reconnect retries hydration without performing network work while unmounted.

## User Impact

Workspace users can keep persistent notes inside a widget without losing early input to a late load. Concurrent edits are detected instead of silently overwritten, read-only/offline views cannot mutate state, and transient hydration failures can recover after reconnect.

Generated locale synchronization remains intentionally separate: four new English keys require authenticated translation sync for the repository's 20 generated locales. No generated locale was hand-edited or filled with fallback-only output.

## Evidence

- Stacked on the current Workspaces widget-state recovery from #101329 and rebased onto current `main`; no legacy dashboard core is carried forward.
- Focused post-rebase Vitest: 54/54 schema and widget assertions passed.
- Scoped extension/UI `oxfmt` and `oxlint`: clean.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users generating video with xAI could configure provider request policy, such as custom headers or proxy settings, but xAI video generation requests ignored that policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

The xAI video provider now sanitizes `cfg.models.providers.xai.request` and passes it into the existing provider HTTP resolver used by the create, poll, and download flow. The poll and download flow now always uses the guarded provider fetch path; private-network access is enabled only when explicitly configured. The change leaves generation parameters, polling semantics, idempotency headers, and media parsing unchanged.

target.title: fix(sessions): cap in-memory session history to prevent unbounded growth
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Long-running autonomous sessions accumulate message turns indefinitely in `SessionHistorySseState.sentHistory.messages` without any pruning. The in-memory array grows without bound, leading to OOM crashes on constrained hosts.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two improvements:

**1. Early raw-message trimming (new):** The constructor now trims the initial raw messages to `MAX_INLINE_HISTORY_MESSAGES × 2` (1000) BEFORE the full `projectChatDisplayMessages` pass when inline mode is active. This avoids projecting and transforming thousands of raw messages only to discard most of them immediately.

**2. Projected-message capping:** `appendInlineMessage` caps `sentHistory.messages` at `MAX_INLINE_HISTORY_MESSAGES` (500) after every append via `trimHistoryMessages`. Combined with early raw trimming, this ensures both the raw-input and projected-output paths are bounded.

When trimming, `hasMore` is set to `true` and `nextCursor` points to the first retained seq so callers can signal older-history availability. The cap only applies to inline (unpaginated) mode.

## User Impact

- Prevents OOM crashes during long-running autonomous sessions
- Older history remains available via `refreshAsync()` or paginated snapshots
- Normal interactive sessions (≤500 turns) are completely unaffected
- Inline SSE appends continue to work for recent history

## Persistent Data Model — No migration needed

The change does not modify any serialized data format, SQLite schema, config surface, or storage layout. The `sentHistory` array is strictly in-memory state reconstructed from transcript reads on each session load.

## Evidence

### A. Unit tests — 96 passing

target.title: fix(agents): reject invalid bundled LSP framing
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: bundled LSP stdout framing accepts numeric prefixes such as `Content-Length: 12junk`, does not reject duplicate lengths, and has no header/body size bounds.
- Solution: parse the header boundary strictly and fail the affected LSP session immediately on the first framing violation.
- What changed: one runtime parser and its focused regression tests.
- What was not changed: outbound framing, bundle discovery/configuration, LSP request payloads, tool schemas, or the general request timeout.

## What Problem This Solves

The current regex is not anchored to a complete header value and `Number.parseInt` accepts a decimal prefix. A malformed frame can therefore be cut at the wrong byte boundary; an oversized unterminated header or declared body can also remain buffered indefinitely. Subsequent JSON-RPC responses no longer align with pending request ids, so users see a misleading generic 10-second timeout instead of the framing error.

## User Impact

A broken or adversarial bundled language server can stall every pending LSP tool request in its session and retain an ever-growing buffer. After this patch, the first invalid frame rejects pending requests with a specific LSP framing error and terminates the child process, while valid frames keep completing normally.

## Origin / follow-up

- **Follows / completes:** #85341, which internalized the bundled agent LSP runtime.
- **Gap this fills:** the internalized stdio parser still partially accepts malformed `Content-Length` values and lacks framing size limits.
- **Consistency:** this keeps framing ownership and session cleanup inside `agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.ts`; no discovery or tool-contract layer is changed.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

- **Linked PR(s):** #103046.
- **Gap in linked PR(s):** it overlaps on oversized bodies but does not reject suffixed or duplicate `Content-Length` fields or bound unterminated headers.
- **Why this patch is better/canonical:** it fails at the fatal header boundary without adding cross-chunk drain state, so pending requests receive the actual error immediately.
- **Local real behavior proof advantage:** the proof drives `createBundleLspToolRuntime` through a real spawned stdio executable that emits both the invalid frame and a canonical control frame.

## Merge risk

- **Why it matters / User impact:** invalid child-process output currently becomes session stalls, retained buffers, and misleading timeouts.
- **Risk labels considered:** compatibility / session-state / availability.
- **Risk explanation:** protocol-invalid or over-limit frames that were previously partially accepted, skipped, or buffered now close the affected LSP session.
- **Why acceptable:** the intentional compatibility change is limited to invalid framing; valid chunked and multibyte frames retain the existing byte-oriented path, and both focused tests and a real subprocess control cover it.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High — RED reproduces the permissive parser, the exact-head 18-test focused suite passes in sanitized AWS Crabbox, and the changed runtime path is exercised through both a real third-party language server and a malformed real subprocess.
- **Patch quality notes:** the production diff adds a broad `JSON.parse` catch only at the untrusted frame boundary; it narrows the caught value when formatting the terminal protocol error and does not swallow it. The related open PR scan found #103046 and is documented above. Automated large-diff/session/message warnings include unrelated commits that advanced `origin/main`; the actual three-dot PR diff is two files: the LSP runtime and its test.
- **Target test file:** `src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.test.ts`.
- **Root cause:** the canonical stdout parser uses an unanchored `Content-Length` regex followed by `Number.parseInt`; because prefix parsing accepts `12junk` as `12`, the framing invariant is broken before bytes enter session state, and missing size bounds let incomplete declarations wait indefinitely.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** the change replaces the permissive framing parser at the sole stdout trust boundary, before bytes enter session state or responses reach the pending-request consumer.
- **What did NOT change:** this patch changes only bundled LSP stdout parsing and its focused tests. It does not change public API, configuration schema, outbound protocol framing, provider/channel behavior, default LSP methods, unrelated session state, docs, formatting, or lockfiles.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** `src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.ts` is the canonical owner of bundled LSP stdio framing, buffer state, pending request settlement, and child cleanup. The invariant is enforced there once rather than downstream in each LSP tool.
- **Scenario locked in:** suffixed length, duplicate length, oversized declared body, and oversized unterminated header all fail immediately; a canonical frame still completes initialize/hover.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** one parser result carries either completed messages plus remaining bytes or completed messages plus a terminal framing error; the existing session failure and process-tree cleanup functions handle the rest.

## Evidence

- **Exact PR head:** `5386f8b22bf56ecb7eb46ad390ba00e161e6ced3`.
- **Environment:** sanitized direct AWS Crabbox, Linux / Node 24.15.0, public networking, no Tailscale, no hydration, immutable `--fresh-pr openclaw/openclaw#105460` checkout.
- **Focused suite:** Crabbox run `run_55379c4d977b` passed all 18 tests in `src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.test.ts`, including manifest-registry reuse, valid `Content-Type`, colonless headers, duplicate/suffixed lengths, size bounds, chunking, request failure, and process cleanup.
- **Real third-party server:** Crabbox run `run_f805f238ea53` installed `typescript-language-server@5.3.0` with `typescript@5.9.3`, loaded it through a temporary enabled Claude bundle manifest/registry, spawned it through `createBundleLspToolRuntime`, and completed a canonical `textDocument/hover` through the resulting OpenClaw tool.
- **Malformed subprocess:** the same run loaded a second real Node child through the same bundle/runtime path. It returned a valid initialize response, then a hover response containing a colonless header line. The pending request rejected immediately with `LSP framing error: header line must contain a colon`, and the child recorded `SIGTERM`.
- **Boundary crossed:** bundle manifest/config and prepared manifest registry → embedded-agent LSP runtime → real OS process spawn → stdin JSON-RPC → stdout LSP framing → pending request settlement → process-tree termination.
- **Rebase integration:** the branch was rebased onto `origin/main` at `afb282ee682`; current main later advanced to `e9e7d385e013ef9dd0daba614a263d334f02eac0` without any intervening changes to either touched LSP file. Current-main manifest-registry plumbing remains present in the PR head.
- **Proof artifact:** the harness was temporary and uncommitted; it asserted the immutable checkout SHA before running and removed its bundle/server artifacts afterward.

```text
{
  "proof_sha": "5386f8b22bf56ecb7eb46ad390ba00e161e6ced3",
  "real_server": "typescript-language-server@5.3.0 + typescript@5.9.3",
  "canonical_hover": "completed through OpenClaw runtime",
  "malformed_header": "LSP framing error: header line must contain a colon",
  "malformed_child_termination": "SIGTERM"
}
```

- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.
- **Remaining proof gap:** no non-Linux platform was exercised.

## Review findings addressed

- **RF-001:** N/A — this is a new follow-up PR; no review findings exist on this head.

## Regression Test Plan

```bash
pnpm test src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.test.ts
```

Sanitized exact-head AWS Crabbox run `run_55379c4d977b` passed all 18 focused tests. Exact-head real behavior run `run_f805f238ea53` passed the canonical third-party-server and malformed-subprocess scenarios above.

## Risk / Compatibility

Medium compatibility/availability risk at a narrow protocol boundary. Standards-compliant positive safe `Content-Length` frames at or below 64 MiB are unchanged. Invalid values, duplicate fields, headers above 8 KiB, bodies above 64 MiB, and invalid JSON bodies now terminate only the affected bundled LSP session instead of being accepted or left pending.

## What was not changed

- Public API / schema / protocol / defaults: no outbound or public contract changes.
- Channel/provider/session/security behavior outside the fixed path: no changes.
- Unrelated cleanup, docs, formatting, lockfiles: none in the three-dot PR diff.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** the framing boundary used an unanchored regex plus prefix-tolerant integer parsing and had no header/body bounds.

target.title: fix: honor configured default agent across main paths
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the remaining hardcoded `DEFAULT_AGENT_ID = "main"` assumptions called out in #90573 for deployments whose configured default agent is not `main`.

PR #30654 fixed the main session-key write paths, but #90573 identified follow-on paths that still synthesized `agents/main/*`, `agent:main:*`, or phantom `main` audit scopes even when config declares a different default agent such as `nova`.

This PR uses the existing `agents.list[].default` / first-agent behavior. It intentionally does **not** add a new `agents.defaultAgentId` config key or `OPENCLAW_DEFAULT_AGENT_ID` environment variable.

## Why This Change Was Made

The current behavior makes non-`main` default-agent deployments inconsistent: some surfaces honor the configured default agent, while others silently route storage, session keys, setup directories, or audit reporting through `main`. That creates broken paths and confusing phantom state for multi-agent installs.

## User Impact

Deployments whose configured default agent is not `main` can keep using their chosen default agent without residual `main` paths leaking into session initialization, auth/model storage scans, setup transcript directories, or exec-scope audit output.

## Changes

- Key new explicit `sessionId` sessions to the resolved store/default agent instead of literal `main`.
- Thread the resolved agent id into auto-reply session initialization.
- Resolve default auth/model storage scan paths from the configured default agent directory.
- Stop security audit exec-scope reporting from injecting a phantom `main` default when another agent is configured as default.
- Avoid inferring a delivery channel from one-segment agent main-session keys when the agent id happens to match a channel name.
- Let setup create the configured default agent's transcript directory instead of `agents/main/sessions` when config is available.

## Risk Mitigations

- **Compatibility:** no schema/env surface added; legacy `main` aliases are still recognized where they already were.
- **Auth-provider:** storage discovery still includes existing directories under state plus configured agent dirs; this only replaces the synthetic default path.
- **Session-state:** new explicit sessions use the same effective default agent that owns the selected store; existing persisted keys are not migrated here.

target.title: fix(ui): keep plugin monogram UTF-16-safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`pluginMonogram` builds the two-letter fallback text for plugin catalog tiles. Both branches previously could produce invalid UTF-16:
- The single-word branch fell back to `first.slice(0, 2)`.
- The two-word branch used `first.charAt(0)` and `second.charAt(0)`.
Both count UTF-16 code units, so a name whose word contains an astral character (emoji, many CJK extensions, etc.) can have its surrogate pair split. The resulting string is invalid UTF-16 and will cause `encodeURIComponent` to throw.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Replaced the single-word `slice(0, 2)` with `sliceUtf16Safe(first, 0, 2)` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`.
- Replaced the two-word `charAt(0)` calls with `String.fromCodePoint(word.codePointAt(0) ?? 0)` so a leading or trailing astral character contributes a complete code point instead of a lone surrogate half.

## User Impact

Plugin catalog tiles no longer risk producing an invalid monogram when a plugin name contains astral characters in either the first or second word.

## Evidence

- `ui/src/pages/plugins/presentation.ts`: `pluginMonogram` now truncates the single-word branch with `sliceUtf16Safe` and takes full code points for the two-word branch.
- Regression tests in `ui/src/pages/plugins/presentation.test.ts` cover `"a😀b"` (single word), `"😀 Plugin"` (leading emoji), and `"Plugin 😀"` (trailing emoji), asserting the monogram is well-formed and `encodeURIComponent(monogram)` succeeds.
- Existing monogram cases (two-word names, normal single words, whitespace trimming) remain unchanged.

## Real behavior proof

- Test command:
  ```bash
  pnpm test ui/src/pages/plugins/presentation.test.ts
  ```
- Before behavior:
  - `pluginMonogram("a😀b")` produced `"A\ud83d"`.
  - `pluginMonogram("Plugin 😀")` produced `"P\ud83d"`.
  - Both make `encodeURIComponent` throw `URIError: URI malformed`.
- After behavior:
  - `pluginMonogram("a😀b")` produces `"A"`.
  - `pluginMonogram("Plugin 😀")` produces `"P😀"`.
  - `encodeURIComponent` succeeds for both.

target.title: fix(config): warn when JSON5 comments are lost on config write
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw uses JSON5 to parse user configurations (supporting comments), but writes them back with JSON.stringify which silently strips all user-authored comments on every automatic config write.

## Why This Change Was Made

JSON5.parse discards comments during parsing — they cannot survive the parse-modify-stringify roundtrip without an AST-aware library. The fix adds a string-aware `hasJSON5Comments()` detector that strips string literals before checking for comment markers, then warns users when their comments will be lost.

## User Impact

- Users with JSON5 comments in config now see a warning before their comments are stripped
- URLs inside strings (`http://...`) do not cause false warnings
- Inline `//` comments (`{a:1 // note}`) are correctly detected
- JSON5 line continuations (backslash+newline in strings) do not cause false warnings
- Plain JSON configs produce no warning

## Evidence

```
$ node -e

✅ detect  "// comment"                       → true   line-start comment
✅ detect  "{a:1 // inline
}"                  → true   inline // comment
✅ detect  "/* block */"                      → true   block comment
✅ detect  "{a:1 /* inline */}"               → true   inline block comment
✅ ignore  "\"http://url\""                   → false  URL in string
✅ ignore  "\"// not comment\""               → false  // in string
✅ ignore  "\"foo\\\n// still string\""       → false  line-continued // in string
✅ ignore  "{\"a\":1}"                       → false  plain JSON
```

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Workspaces has no first-class preview panel for inspecting a development server or deployed page without leaving the operator workspace. The legacy implementation targeted the removed dashboard stack and could not be safely rebased.

## Why This Change Was Made
